/**
   * This function takes a set of GETPROP nodes and produces a string that is
   * each property separated by dots. If the node ultimately under the left
   * sub-tree is not a simple name, this is not a valid qualified name.
   *
   * @return a null if this is not a qualified name, or a dot-separated string
   *         of the name and properties.
   */
Method code:
1552 |   public String getQualifiedName() {
1553 |     if (type == Token.NAME) {
1554 |       return getString();
1555 |     } else if (type == Token.GETPROP) {
1556 |       String left = getFirstChild().getQualifiedName();
1557 |       if (left == null) {
1558 |         return null;
1559 |       }
1560 |       return left + "." + getLastChild().getString();
1561 |     } else if (type == Token.THIS) {
1562 |       return "this";
1563 |     } else {
1564 |       return null;
1565 |     }
1566 |   }

===== M0008 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.InlineObjectLiterals.InliningBehavior.isInlinableObject(List<Reference>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/InlineObjectLiterals.java
Original range: 155-229
Documentation:
/**
     * Counts the number of direct (full) references to an object.
     * Specifically we check for references of the following type:
     * <pre>
     *   x;
     *   x.fn();
     * </pre>
     */
Method code:
155 |     private boolean isInlinableObject(List<Reference> refs) {
156 |       boolean ret = false;
157 |       for (Reference ref : refs) {
158 |         Node name = ref.getNode();
159 |         Node parent = ref.getParent();
160 |         Node gramps = ref.getGrandparent();
161 | 
162 |         // Ignore indirect references, like x.y (except x.y(), since
163 |         // the function referenced by y might reference 'this').
164 |         //
165 |         if (parent.isGetProp()) {
166 |           Preconditions.checkState(parent.getFirstChild() == name);
167 |           // A call target maybe using the object as a 'this' value.
168 |           if (gramps.isCall()
169 |               && gramps.getFirstChild() == parent) {
170 |             return false;
171 |           }
172 |           continue;
173 |         }
174 | 
175 |         // Only rewrite VAR declarations or simple assignment statements
176 |         if (!isVarOrAssignExprLhs(name)) {
177 |            return false;
178 |         }
179 | 
180 |         Node val = ref.getAssignedValue();
181 |         if (val == null) {
182 |           // A var with no assignment.
183 |           continue;
184 |         }
185 | 
186 |         // We're looking for object literal assignments only.
187 |         if (!val.isObjectLit()) {
188 |           return false;
189 |         }
190 | 
191 |         // Make sure that the value is not self-refential. IOW,
192 |         // disallow things like x = {b: x.a}.
193 |         //
194 |         // TODO: Only exclude unorderable self-referential
195 |         // assignments. i.e. x = {a: x.b, b: x.a} is not orderable,
196 |         // but x = {a: 1, b: x.a} is.
197 |         //
198 |         // Also, ES5 getters/setters aren't handled by this pass.
199 |         for (Node child = val.getFirstChild(); child != null;
200 |              child = child.getNext()) {
201 |           if (child.isGetterDef() ||
202 |               child.isSetterDef()) {
203 |             // ES5 get/set not supported.
204 |             return false;
205 |           }
206 |           Node childVal = child.getFirstChild();
207 |           // Check if childVal is the parent of any of the passed in
208 |           // references, as that is how self-referential assignments
209 |           // will happen.
210 |           for (Reference t : refs) {
211 |             Node refNode = t.getParent();
212 |             while (!NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(refNode)) {
213 |               if (refNode == childVal) {
214 |                 // There's a self-referential assignment
215 |                 return false;
216 |               }
217 |               refNode = refNode.getParent();
218 |             }
219 |           }
220 |         }
221 | 
222 | 
223 |         // We have found an acceptable object literal assignment. As
224 |         // long as there are no other assignments that mess things up,
225 |         // we can inline.
226 |         ret = true;
227 |       }
228 |       return ret;
229 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RenameProperties.ProcessProperties.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RenameProperties.java
Original range: 406-471
Documentation:

Method code:
406 |     @Override
407 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
408 |       switch (n.getType()) {
409 |         case Token.GETPROP:
410 |           Node propNode = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
411 |           if (propNode.isString()) {
412 |             maybeMarkCandidate(propNode);
413 |           }
414 |           break;
415 |         case Token.OBJECTLIT:
416 |           for (Node key = n.getFirstChild(); key != null; key = key.getNext()) {
417 |             if (!key.isQuotedString()) {
418 |               maybeMarkCandidate(key);
419 |             } else {
420 |               // Ensure that we never rename some other property in a way
421 |               // that could conflict with this quoted key.
422 |               quotedNames.add(key.getString());
423 |             }
424 |           }
425 |           break;
426 |         case Token.GETELEM:
427 |           // If this is a quoted property access (e.g. x['myprop']), we need to
428 |           // ensure that we never rename some other property in a way that
429 |           // could conflict with this quoted name.
430 |           Node child = n.getLastChild();
431 |           if (child != null && child.isString()) {
432 |             quotedNames.add(child.getString());
433 |           }
434 |           break;
435 |         case Token.CALL:
436 |           // We replace a JSCompiler_renameProperty function call with a string
437 |           // containing the renamed property.
438 |           Node fnName = n.getFirstChild();
439 |           if (fnName.isName() &&
440 |               RENAME_PROPERTY_FUNCTION_NAME.equals(fnName.getString())) {
441 |             callNodeToParentMap.put(n, parent);
442 |             countCallCandidates(t, n);
443 |           }
444 |           break;
445 |         case Token.FUNCTION:
446 |           // We eliminate any stub implementations of JSCompiler_renameProperty
447 |           // that we encounter.
448 |           if (NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(n)) {
449 |             String name = n.getFirstChild().getString();
450 |             if (RENAME_PROPERTY_FUNCTION_NAME.equals(name)) {
451 |               if (parent.isExprResult()) {
452 |                 parent.detachFromParent();
453 |               } else {
454 |                 parent.removeChild(n);
455 |               }
456 |               compiler.reportCodeChange();
457 |             }
458 |           } else if (parent.isName() &&
459 |                      RENAME_PROPERTY_FUNCTION_NAME.equals(parent.getString())) {
460 |             Node varNode = parent.getParent();
461 |             if (varNode.isVar()) {
462 |               varNode.removeChild(parent);
463 |               if (!varNode.hasChildren()) {
464 |                 varNode.detachFromParent();
465 |               }
466 |               compiler.reportCodeChange();
467 |             }
468 |           }
469 |           break;
470 |       }
471 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.GlobalNamespace.BuildGlobalNamespace.collect(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)

Method code:
302 |     public void collect(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
303 |       if (nodeFilter != null && !nodeFilter.apply(n)) {
304 |         return;
305 |       }
306 | 
307 |       // If we are traversing the externs, then we save a pointer to the scope
308 |       // generated by them, so that we can do lookups in it later.
309 |       if (externsRoot != null && n == externsRoot) {
310 |         externsScope = t.getScope();
311 |       }
312 | 
313 |       String name;
314 |       boolean isSet = false;
315 |       Name.Type type = Name.Type.OTHER;
316 |       boolean isPropAssign = false;
317 | 
318 |       switch (n.getType()) {
319 |         case Token.GETTER_DEF:
320 |         case Token.SETTER_DEF:
321 |         case Token.STRING:
322 |           // This may be a key in an object literal declaration.
323 |           name = null;
324 |           if (parent != null && parent.isObjectLit()) {
325 |             name = getNameForObjLitKey(n);
326 |           }
327 |           if (name == null) return;
328 |           isSet = true;
329 |           switch (n.getType()) {
330 |             case Token.STRING:
331 |               type = getValueType(n.getFirstChild());
332 |               break;
333 |             case Token.GETTER_DEF:
334 |               type = Name.Type.GET;
335 |               break;
336 |             case Token.SETTER_DEF:
337 |               type = Name.Type.SET;
338 |               break;
339 |             default:
340 |               throw new IllegalStateException("unexpected:" + n);
341 |           }
342 |           break;
343 |         case Token.NAME:
344 |           // This may be a variable get or set.
345 |           if (parent != null) {
346 |             switch (parent.getType()) {
347 |               case Token.VAR:
348 |                 isSet = true;
349 |                 Node rvalue = n.getFirstChild();
350 |                 type = rvalue == null ? Name.Type.OTHER : getValueType(rvalue);
351 |                 break;
352 |               case Token.ASSIGN:
353 |                 if (parent.getFirstChild() == n) {
354 |                   isSet = true;
355 |                   type = getValueType(n.getNext());
356 |                 }
357 |                 break;
358 |               case Token.GETPROP:
359 |                 return;
360 |               case Token.FUNCTION:
361 |                 Node gramps = parent.getParent();
362 |                 if (gramps == null ||
363 |                     NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(parent)) return;
364 |                 isSet = true;
365 |                 type = Name.Type.FUNCTION;
366 |                 break;
367 |               case Token.INC:
368 |               case Token.DEC:
369 |                 isSet = true;
370 |                 type = Name.Type.OTHER;
371 |                 break;
372 |               default:
373 |                 if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(parent) &&
374 |                     parent.getFirstChild() == n) {
375 |                   isSet = true;
376 |                   type = Name.Type.OTHER;
377 |                 }
378 |             }
379 |           }
380 |           name = n.getString();
381 |           break;
382 |         case Token.GETPROP:
383 |           // This may be a namespaced name get or set.
384 |           if (parent != null) {
385 |             switch (parent.getType()) {
386 |               case Token.ASSIGN:
387 |                 if (parent.getFirstChild() == n) {
388 |                   isSet = true;
389 |                   type = getValueType(n.getNext());
390 |                   isPropAssign = true;
391 |                 }
392 |                 break;
393 |               case Token.INC:
394 |               case Token.DEC:
395 |                 isSet = true;
396 |                 type = Name.Type.OTHER;
397 |                 break;
398 |               case Token.GETPROP:
399 |                 return;
400 |               default:
401 |                 if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(parent) &&
402 |                     parent.getFirstChild() == n) {
403 |                   isSet = true;
404 |                   type = Name.Type.OTHER;
405 |                 }
406 |             }
407 |           }
408 |           name = n.getQualifiedName();
409 |           if (name == null) return;
410 |           break;
411 |         default:
412 |           return;
413 |       }
414 | 
415 |       // We are only interested in global names.
416 |       Scope scope = t.getScope();
417 |       if (!isGlobalNameReference(name, scope)) {
418 |         return;
419 |       }
420 | 
421 |       if (isSet) {
422 |         if (isGlobalScope(scope)) {
423 |           handleSetFromGlobal(t, n, parent, name, isPropAssign, type);
424 |         } else {
425 |           handleSetFromLocal(t, n, parent, name);
426 |         }
427 |       } else {
428 |         handleGet(t, n, parent, name);
429 |       }
430 |     }

===== M0039 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.FunctionType.setPrototypeBasedOn(ObjectType,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/FunctionType.java
Original range: 331-358
Documentation:

Method code:
331 |   void setPrototypeBasedOn(ObjectType baseType, Node propertyNode) {
332 |     // This is a bit weird. We need to successfully handle these
333 |     // two cases:
334 |     // Foo.prototype = new Bar();
335 |     // and
336 |     // Foo.prototype = {baz: 3};
337 |     // In the first case, we do not want new properties to get
338 |     // added to Bar. In the second case, we do want new properties
339 |     // to get added to the type of the anonymous object.
340 |     //
341 |     // We handle this by breaking it into two cases:
342 |     //
343 |     // In the first case, we create a new PrototypeObjectType and set
344 |     // its implicit prototype to the type being assigned. This ensures
345 |     // that Bar will not get any properties of Foo.prototype, but properties
346 |     // later assigned to Bar will get inherited properly.
347 |     //
348 |     // In the second case, we just use the anonymous object as the prototype.
349 |     if (baseType.hasReferenceName() ||
350 |         isNativeObjectType() ||
351 |         baseType.isFunctionPrototypeType() ||
352 |         !(baseType instanceof PrototypeObjectType)) {
353 | 
354 |       baseType = new PrototypeObjectType(
355 |           registry, this.getReferenceName() + ".prototype", baseType);
356 |     }
357 |     setPrototype((PrototypeObjectType) baseType, propertyNode);
358 |   }

===== M0057 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeFoldConstants.tryFoldAndOr(Node,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeFoldConstants.java
Original range: 562-600
Documentation:
/**
   * Try to fold a AND/OR node.
   */
Method code:
562 |   private Node tryFoldAndOr(Node n, Node left, Node right) {
563 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
564 | 
565 |     Node result = null;
566 | 
567 |     int type = n.getType();
568 | 
569 |     TernaryValue leftVal = NodeUtil.getImpureBooleanValue(left);
570 | 
571 |     if (leftVal != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
572 |       boolean lval = leftVal.toBoolean(true);
573 | 
574 |       // (TRUE || x) => TRUE (also, (3 || x) => 3)
575 |       // (FALSE && x) => FALSE
576 |       if (lval && type == Token.OR ||
577 |           !lval && type == Token.AND) {
578 |         result = left;
579 | 
580 |       } else if (!mayHaveSideEffects(left)) {
581 |         // (FALSE || x) => x
582 |         // (TRUE && x) => x
583 |         result = right;
584 |       }
585 |     }
586 | 
587 |     // Note: Right hand side folding is handled by
588 |     // PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax#tryMinimizeCondition
589 | 
590 |     if (result != null) {
591 |       // Fold it!
592 |       n.removeChild(result);
593 |       parent.replaceChild(n, result);
594 |       reportCodeChange();
595 | 
596 |       return result;
597 |     } else {
598 |       return n;
599 |     }
600 |   }

===== M0086 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CreateSyntheticBlocks.Callback.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CreateSyntheticBlocks.java
Original range: 169-215
Documentation:

Method code:
169 |     @Override
170 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
171 |       if (!n.isCall() || !n.getFirstChild().isName()) {
172 |         return;
173 |       }
174 | 
175 |       Node callTarget = n.getFirstChild();
176 |       String callName = callTarget.getString();
177 | 
178 |       if (startMarkerName.equals(callName)) {
179 |         if (!parent.isExprResult()) {
180 |           compiler.report(
181 |               t.makeError(n, INVALID_MARKER_USAGE, startMarkerName));
182 |           return;
183 |         }
184 |         markerStack.push(parent);
185 |         return;
186 |       }
187 | 
188 |       if (!endMarkerName.equals(callName)) {
189 |         return;
190 |       }
191 | 
192 |       Node endMarkerNode = parent;
193 |       if (!endMarkerNode.isExprResult()) {
194 |         compiler.report(
195 |             t.makeError(n, INVALID_MARKER_USAGE, endMarkerName));
196 |         return;
197 |       }
198 | 
199 |       if (markerStack.isEmpty()) {
200 |         compiler.report(t.makeError(n, UNMATCHED_END_MARKER,
201 |             startMarkerName, endMarkerName));
202 |         return;
203 |       }
204 | 
205 |       Node startMarkerNode = markerStack.pop();
206 |       if (endMarkerNode.getParent() != startMarkerNode.getParent()) {
207 |         // The end marker isn't in the same block as the start marker.
208 |         compiler.report(t.makeError(n, UNMATCHED_END_MARKER,
209 |             startMarkerName, endMarkerName));
210 |         return;
211 |       }
212 | 
213 |       // This is a valid marker set add it to the list of markers to process.
214 |       validMarkers.add(new Marker(startMarkerNode, endMarkerNode));
215 |     }

   * Merge a block with its parent block.
   * @return Whether the block was removed.
   */
Method code:
1817 |   static boolean tryMergeBlock(Node block) {
1818 |     Preconditions.checkState(block.isBlock());
1819 |     Node parent = block.getParent();
1820 |     // Try to remove the block if its parent is a block/script or if its
1821 |     // parent is label and it has exactly one child.

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.DefinitionsRemover.getDefinition(Node,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/DefinitionsRemover.java
Original range: 37-65

/**
   * @return an {@link Definition} object if the node contains a definition or
   *     {@code null} otherwise.
   */
Method code:
37 |   static Definition getDefinition(Node n, boolean isExtern) {
38 |     // TODO(user): Since we have parent pointers handy. A lot of constructors
39 |     // can be simplified.
40 | 
41 |     // This logic must match #isDefinitionNode
42 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
43 |     if (parent == null) {
44 |       return null;
45 |     }
46 | 
47 |     if (NodeUtil.isVarDeclaration(n) && n.hasChildren()) {

50 |       if (!NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(parent)) {
51 |         return new NamedFunctionDefinition(parent, isExtern);

59 |           isExtern);
60 |     } else if (parent.isParamList()) {
61 |       Node function = parent.getParent();
62 |       return new FunctionArgumentDefinition(function, n, isExtern);

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeTraversal.traverseFunction(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeTraversal.java
Original range: 510-545
Documentation:
/**
   * Traverses a function.
   */
Method code:
510 |   private void traverseFunction(Node n, Node parent) {
511 |     Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 3);
512 |     Preconditions.checkState(n.isFunction());
513 | 
514 |     final Node fnName = n.getFirstChild();
515 | 
516 |     boolean isFunctionExpression = (parent != null)
517 |         && NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(n);
518 | 
519 |     if (!isFunctionExpression) {
520 |       // Functions declarations are in the scope containing the declaration.
521 |       traverseBranch(fnName, n);
522 |     }
523 | 
524 |     curNode = n;
525 |     pushScope(n);
526 | 
527 |     if (isFunctionExpression) {
528 |       // Function expression names are only accessible within the function
529 |       // scope.
530 |       traverseBranch(fnName, n);
531 |     }
532 | 
533 |     final Node args = fnName.getNext();
534 |     final Node body = args.getNext();
535 | 
536 |     // Args
537 |     traverseBranch(args, n);
538 | 
539 |     // Body
540 |     Preconditions.checkState(body.getNext() == null &&
541 |             body.isBlock(), body);
542 |     traverseBranch(body, n);
543 | 
544 |     popScope();
545 |   }

/**

   * defined in the global scope exactly once.

/**
   * Updates the first initialization (a.k.a "declaration") of a global name
   * that occurs at an ASSIGN node. See comment for
   * {@link #updateObjLitOrFunctionDeclaration}.
   *
   * @param n An object representing a global name (e.g. "a", "a.b.c")
   * @param alias The flattened name for {@code n} (e.g. "a", "a$b$c")
   */
Method code:
659 |   private void updateObjLitOrFunctionDeclarationAtAssignNode(
660 |       Name n, String alias, boolean canCollapseChildNames) {
661 |     // NOTE: It's important that we don't add additional nodes
662 |     // (e.g. a var node before the exprstmt) because the exprstmt might be
663 |     // the child of an if statement that's not inside a block).
664 | 
665 |     Ref ref = n.getDeclaration();
666 |     Node rvalue = ref.node.getNext();
667 |     Node varNode = new Node(Token.VAR);
668 |     Node varParent = ref.node.getAncestor(3);
669 |     Node gramps = ref.node.getAncestor(2);
670 |     boolean isObjLit = rvalue.isObjectLit();
671 |     boolean insertedVarNode = false;
672 | 
673 |     if (isObjLit && n.canEliminate()) {
674 |       // Eliminate the object literal altogether.
675 |       varParent.replaceChild(gramps, varNode);
676 |       ref.node = null;
677 |       insertedVarNode = true;
678 | 
679 |     } else if (!n.isSimpleName()) {
680 |       // Create a VAR node to declare the name.
681 |       if (rvalue.isFunction()) {
682 |         checkForHosedThisReferences(rvalue, n.docInfo, n);
683 |       }
684 | 
685 |       ref.node.getParent().removeChild(rvalue);
686 | 
687 |       Node nameNode = NodeUtil.newName(
688 |           compiler.getCodingConvention(),
689 |           alias, ref.node.getAncestor(2), n.getFullName());
690 | 
691 |       JSDocInfo info = ref.node.getParent().getJSDocInfo();
692 |       if (ref.node.getLastChild().getBooleanProp(Node.IS_CONSTANT_NAME) ||
693 |           (info != null && info.isConstant())) {
694 |         nameNode.putBooleanProp(Node.IS_CONSTANT_NAME, true);
695 |       }
696 | 
697 |       varNode.addChildToBack(nameNode);
698 |       nameNode.addChildToFront(rvalue);
699 |       varParent.replaceChild(gramps, varNode);
700 | 
701 |       // Update the node ancestry stored in the reference.
702 |       ref.node = nameNode;
703 |       insertedVarNode = true;
704 |     }
705 | 
706 |     if (canCollapseChildNames) {
707 |       if (isObjLit) {
708 |         declareVarsForObjLitValues(
709 |             n, alias, rvalue,
710 |             varNode, varParent.getChildBefore(varNode), varParent);
711 |       }
712 | 
713 |       addStubsForUndeclaredProperties(n, alias, varParent, varNode);
714 |     }
715 | 
716 |     if (insertedVarNode) {
717 |       if (!varNode.hasChildren()) {
718 |         varParent.removeChild(varNode);
719 |       }
720 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
721 |     }
722 |   }

===== M0155 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CollapseProperties.inlineAliases(GlobalNamespace)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CollapseProperties.java
Original range: 161-197
Documentation:
/**
   * For each qualified name N in the global scope, we check if:
   * (a) No ancestor of N is ever aliased or assigned an unknown value type.
   *     (If N = "a.b.c", "a" and "a.b" are never aliased).
   * (b) N has exactly one write, and it lives in the global scope.
   * (c) N is aliased in a local scope.
   *
   * If (a) is true, then GlobalNamespace must know all the writes to N.
   * If (a) and (b) are true, then N cannot change during the execution of
   *    a local scope.
   * If (a) and (b) and (c) are true, then the alias can be inlined if the
   *    alias obeys the usual rules for how we decide whether a variable is
   *    inlineable.
   * @see InlineVariables
   */
Method code:
161 |   private void inlineAliases(GlobalNamespace namespace) {
162 |     // Invariant: All the names in the worklist meet condition (a).
163 |     Deque<Name> workList = new ArrayDeque<Name>(namespace.getNameForest());
164 |     while (!workList.isEmpty()) {
165 |       Name name = workList.pop();
166 | 
167 |       // Don't attempt to inline a getter or setter property as a variable.
168 |       if (name.type == Name.Type.GET || name.type == Name.Type.SET) {
169 |         continue;
170 |       }
171 | 
172 |       if (name.globalSets == 1 && name.localSets == 0 &&
173 |           name.aliasingGets > 0) {
174 |         // {@code name} meets condition (b). Find all of its local aliases
175 |         // and try to inline them.
176 |         List<Ref> refs = Lists.newArrayList(name.getRefs());
177 |         for (Ref ref : refs) {
178 |           if (ref.type == Type.ALIASING_GET && ref.scope.isLocal()) {
179 |             // {@code name} meets condition (c). Try to inline it.
180 |             if (inlineAliasIfPossible(ref, namespace)) {
181 |               name.removeRef(ref);
182 |             }
183 |           }
184 |         }
185 |       }
186 | 
187 |       // Check if {@code name} has any aliases left after the
188 |       // local-alias-inlining above.
189 |       if ((name.type == Name.Type.OBJECTLIT ||
190 |            name.type == Name.Type.FUNCTION) &&
191 |           name.aliasingGets == 0 && name.props != null) {
192 |         // All of {@code name}'s children meet condition (a), so they can be
193 |         // added to the worklist.
194 |         workList.addAll(name.props);
195 |       }
196 |     }
197 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.InlineFunctions.isCandidateUsage(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/InlineFunctions.java
Original range: 427-461

/**
   * @return Whether the name is used in a way that might be a candidate
   *   for inlining.
   */
Method code:
427 |   static boolean isCandidateUsage(Node name) {
428 |     Node parent = name.getParent();
429 |     Preconditions.checkState(name.isName());
430 |     if (parent.isVar() || parent.isFunction()) {
431 |       // This is a declaration.  Duplicate declarations are handle during
432 |       // function candidate gathering.
433 |       return true;
434 |     }

437 |       // This is a normal reference to the function.

441 |     // Check for a ".call" to the named function:
442 |     //   CALL
443 |     //     GETPROP/GETELEM
444 |     //       NAME
445 |     //       STRING == "call"
446 |     //     This-Value
447 |     //     Function-parameter-1
448 |     //     ...

455 |           && gramps.getFirstChild() == parent) {
456 |         // Yep, a ".call".
457 |         return true;
458 |       }
459 |     }

/**
   * Stop the trace.
   * This may only be done once and must be done from the same thread
   * that started it.

   * ms will be left out of the trace report. A value of -1 indicates
   * that the current ThreadTrace silence_threshold should be used.
   * @return The time that this trace actually ran

407 |   long stop(int silence_threshold) {
408 |     Preconditions.checkState(Thread.currentThread() == startThread);
409 |

412 |     if (!trace.isInitialized()) {

===== M0174 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.InlineVariables.InliningBehavior.isImmutableAndWellDefinedVariable(Var,ReferenceCollection)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/InlineVariables.java
Original range: 672-722
Documentation:
/**
     * Determines whether the reference collection describes a variable that
     * is initialized to an immutable value, never modified, and defined before
     * every reference.
     */
Method code:
672 |     private boolean isImmutableAndWellDefinedVariable(Var v,
673 |         ReferenceCollection refInfo) {
674 |       List<Reference> refSet = refInfo.references;
675 |       int startingReadRef = 1;
676 |       Reference refDecl = refSet.get(0);
677 |       if (!isValidDeclaration(refDecl)) {
678 |         return false;
679 |       }
680 | 
681 |       boolean isNeverAssigned = refInfo.isNeverAssigned();
682 |       // For values that are never assigned, only the references need to be
683 |       // checked.
684 |       if (!isNeverAssigned) {
685 |         Reference refInit = refInfo.getInitializingReference();
686 |         if (!isValidInitialization(refInit)) {
687 |           return false;
688 |         }
689 | 
690 |         if (refDecl != refInit) {
691 |           Preconditions.checkState(refInit == refSet.get(1));
692 |           startingReadRef = 2;
693 |         }
694 | 
695 |         if (!refInfo.isWellDefined()) {
696 |           return false;
697 |         }
698 | 
699 |         Node value = refInit.getAssignedValue();
700 |         Preconditions.checkNotNull(value);
701 | 
702 |         boolean isImmutableValueWorthInlining =
703 |             NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(value) &&
704 |             (!value.isString() ||
705 |                 isStringWorthInlining(v, refInfo.references));
706 |         boolean isInlinableThisAlias =
707 |             value.isThis() &&
708 |             !refInfo.isEscaped();
709 |         if (!isImmutableValueWorthInlining && !isInlinableThisAlias) {
710 |           return false;
711 |         }
712 |       }
713 | 
714 |       for (int i = startingReadRef; i < refSet.size(); i++) {
715 |         Reference ref = refSet.get(i);
716 |         if (!isValidReference(ref)) {
717 |           return false;
718 |         }
719 |       }
720 | 
721 |       return true;
722 |     }

791 |         Node key = transformAsString(el.getLeft());
792 |         Node value = transform(el.getRight());
793 |         if (el.isGetter()) {
794 |           key.setType(Token.GETTER_DEF);
795 |           Preconditions.checkState(value.isFunction());
796 |           if (getFnParamNode(value).hasChildren()) {
797 |             reportGetterParam(el.getLeft());
798 |           }
799 |         } else if (el.isSetter()) {
800 |           key.setType(Token.SETTER_DEF);
801 |           Preconditions.checkState(value.isFunction());
802 |           if (!getFnParamNode(value).hasOneChild()) {
803 |             reportSetterParam(el.getLeft());
804 |           }
805 |         }
806 |         key.addChildToFront(value);
807 |         node.addChildToBack(key);
808 |       }
809 |       return node;
810 |     }

174 |     // Find all the global names with a @define annotation
175 |     List<Name> allDefines = Lists.newArrayList();
176 |     for (Name name : namespace.getNameIndex().values()) {
177 |       Ref decl = name.getDeclaration();

346 |             return;
347 |           } else {
348 |             report(t, n, GOOG_SCOPE_ALIAS_REDEFINED, n.getString());
349 |           }
350 |         }
351 | 
352 |         if (type == Token.RETURN) {
353 |           report(t, n, GOOG_SCOPE_USES_RETURN);
354 |         } else if (type == Token.THIS) {
355 |           report(t, n, GOOG_SCOPE_REFERENCES_THIS);
356 |         } else if (type == Token.THROW) {
357 |           report(t, n, GOOG_SCOPE_USES_THROW);
358 |         }
359 |       }
360 | 
361 |       // Validate all descendent scopes of the goog.scope block.
362 |       if (t.getScopeDepth() >= 2) {
363 |         // Check if this name points to an alias.
364 |         if (aliasVar != null) {
365 |           // Note, to support the transitive case, it's important we don't
366 |           // clone aliasedNode here.  For example,
367 |           // var g = goog; var d = g.dom; d.createElement('DIV');
368 |           // The node in aliasedNode (which is "g") will be replaced in the
369 |           // changes pass above with "goog".  If we cloned here, we'd end up
370 |           // with <code>g.dom.createElement('DIV')</code>.
371 |           Node aliasedNode = aliasVar.getInitialValue();
372 |           aliasUsages.add(new AliasedNode(n, aliasedNode));
373 |         }
374 | 
375 |         JSDocInfo info = n.getJSDocInfo();
376 |         if (info != null) {
377 |           for (Node node : info.getTypeNodes()) {
378 |             fixTypeNode(node);
379 |           }
380 |         }
381 | 
382 |         // TODO(robbyw): Error for goog.scope not at root.
383 |       }
384 |     }

===== M0232 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.AstChangeProxy.replaceWith(Node,Node,List<Node>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/AstChangeProxy.java
Original range: 94-131
Documentation:
/**
   * Replaces a node with the provided list.
   */
Method code:
94 |   final void replaceWith(Node parent, Node node, List<Node> replacements) {
95 |     Preconditions.checkNotNull(replacements, "\"replacements\" is null.");
96 | 
97 |     int size = replacements.size();
98 | 
99 |     if ((size == 1) && node.isEquivalentTo(replacements.get(0))) {
100 |       // trees are equal... don't replace
101 |       return;
102 |     }
103 | 
104 |     int parentType = parent.getType();
105 | 
106 |     Preconditions.checkState(size == 1 ||
107 |         parentType == Token.BLOCK ||
108 |         parentType == Token.SCRIPT ||
109 |         parentType == Token.LABEL);
110 | 
111 |     if (parentType == Token.LABEL && size != 1) {
112 |       Node block = IR.block();
113 |       for (Node newChild : replacements) {
114 |         newChild.copyInformationFrom(node);
115 |         Node oldParent = newChild.getParent();
116 |         block.addChildToBack(newChild);
117 |       }
118 | 
119 |       parent.replaceChild(node, block);
120 | 
121 |     } else {
122 |       for (Node newChild : replacements) {
123 |         newChild.copyInformationFrom(node);
124 |         Node oldParent = newChild.getParent();
125 |         parent.addChildBefore(newChild, node);
126 |       }
127 |       parent.removeChild(node);
128 | 
129 |     }
130 |     notifyOfRemoval(node);
131 |   }

338 |           }

342 |           }
343 | 
344 |           if (flags.areAllFlagsSet()) {
345 |             break;
346 |           }
347 |         }
348 |       }
349 | 
350 |       // Handle special cases (Math, RegEx)
351 |       if (callNode.isCall()) {
352 |         Preconditions.checkState(compiler != null);
353 |         if (!NodeUtil.functionCallHasSideEffects(callNode, compiler)) {
354 |           flags.clearSideEffectFlags();
355 |         }
356 |       } else if (callNode.isNew()) {
357 |         // Handle known cases now (Object, Date, RegExp, etc)
358 |         if (!NodeUtil.constructorCallHasSideEffects(callNode)) {
359 |           flags.clearSideEffectFlags();
360 |         }
361 |       }
362 | 
363 |       callNode.setSideEffectFlags(flags.valueOf());
364 |     }
365 |   }

     * @return Whether the definitionSite represents a function whose call

619 |     private boolean canChangeSignature(Node function) {

622 |

626 |       for (UseSite site : useSites) {

628 |

===== M0269 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.tryRemoveRedundantExit(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.java
Original range: 508-539
Documentation:
/**
   * Remove duplicate exits.  If the node following the exit node expression
   * has the same effect as exit node, the node can be removed.
   * For example:
   *   "if (a) {return f()} return f();" ==> "if (a) {} return f();"
   *   "if (a) {throw 'ow'} throw 'ow';" ==> "if (a) {} throw 'ow';"
   *
   * @param n An follow control exit expression (a THROW or RETURN node)
   * @return The replacement for n, or the original if no change was made.
   */
Method code:
508 |   private Node tryRemoveRedundantExit(Node n) {
509 |     Node exitExpr = n.getFirstChild();
510 | 
511 |     Node follow = ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode(n);
512 | 
513 |     // Skip pass all the finally blocks because both the fall through and return
514 |     // will also trigger all the finally blocks.
515 |     Node prefinallyFollows = follow;
516 |     follow = skipFinallyNodes(follow);
517 |     if (prefinallyFollows != follow) {
518 |       // There were finally clauses
519 |       if (!isPure(exitExpr)) {
520 |         // Can't replace the return
521 |         return n;
522 |       }
523 |     }
524 | 
525 |     if (follow == null && (n.isThrow() || exitExpr != null)) {
526 |       // Can't complete remove a throw here or a return with a result.
527 |       return n;
528 |     }
529 | 
530 |     // When follow is null, this mean the follow of a break target is the
531 |     // end of a function. This means a break is same as return.
532 |     if (follow == null || areMatchingExits(n, follow)) {
533 |       n.detachFromParent();
534 |       reportCodeChange();
535 |       return null;
536 |     }
537 | 
538 |     return n;
539 |   }

===== M0278 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RenameVars.assignNames(Set<Assignment>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RenameVars.java
Original range: 441-511
Documentation:
/**
   * Determines which new names to substitute for the original names.
   */
Method code:
441 |   private void assignNames(Set<Assignment> varsToRename) {
442 |     NameGenerator globalNameGenerator =
443 |         new NameGenerator(reservedNames, prefix, reservedCharacters);
444 | 
445 |     // Local variables never need a prefix.
446 |     NameGenerator localNameGenerator =
447 |         prefix.isEmpty() ? globalNameGenerator : new NameGenerator(
448 |             reservedNames, "", reservedCharacters);
449 | 
450 |     // Generated names and the assignments for non-local vars.
451 |     List<Assignment> pendingAssignments = new ArrayList<Assignment>();
452 |     List<String> generatedNamesForAssignments = new ArrayList<String>();
453 | 
454 |     for (Assignment a : varsToRename) {
455 |       if (a.newName != null) {
456 |         continue;
457 |       }
458 | 
459 |       if (externNames.contains(a.oldName)) {
460 |         continue;
461 |       }
462 | 
463 |       String newName;
464 |       if (a.oldName.startsWith(LOCAL_VAR_PREFIX)) {
465 |         // For local variable, we make the assignment right away.
466 |         newName = localNameGenerator.generateNextName();
467 |         finalizeNameAssignment(a, newName);
468 |       } else {
469 |         // For non-local variable, delay finalizing the name assignment
470 |         // until we know how many new names we'll have of length 2, 3, etc.
471 |         newName = globalNameGenerator.generateNextName();
472 |         pendingAssignments.add(a);
473 |         generatedNamesForAssignments.add(newName);
474 |       }
475 |       reservedNames.add(newName);
476 |     }
477 | 
478 |     // Now that we have a list of generated names, and a list of variable
479 |     // Assignment objects, we assign the generated names to the vars as
480 |     // follows:
481 |     // 1) The most frequent vars get the shorter names.
482 |     // 2) If N number of vars are going to be assigned names of the same
483 |     //    length, we assign the N names based on the order at which the vars
484 |     //    first appear in the source. This makes the output somewhat less
485 |     //    random, because symbols declared close together are assigned names
486 |     //    that are quite similar. With this heuristic, the output is more
487 |     //    compressible.
488 |     //    For instance, the output may look like:
489 |     //    var da = "..", ea = "..";
490 |     //    function fa() { .. } function ga() { .. }
491 | 
492 |     int numPendingAssignments = generatedNamesForAssignments.size();
493 |     for (int i = 0; i < numPendingAssignments;) {
494 |       SortedSet<Assignment> varsByOrderOfOccurrence =
495 |           new TreeSet<Assignment>(ORDER_OF_OCCURRENCE_COMPARATOR);
496 | 
497 |       // Add k number of Assignment to the set, where k is the number of
498 |       // generated names of the same length.
499 |       int len = generatedNamesForAssignments.get(i).length();
500 |       for (int j = i; j < numPendingAssignments
501 |           && generatedNamesForAssignments.get(j).length() == len; j++) {
502 |         varsByOrderOfOccurrence.add(pendingAssignments.get(j));
503 |       }
504 | 
505 |       // Now, make the assignments
506 |       for (Assignment a : varsByOrderOfOccurrence) {
507 |         finalizeNameAssignment(a, generatedNamesForAssignments.get(i));
508 |         ++i;
509 |       }
510 |     }
511 |   }

===== M0282 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.MaybeReachingVariableUse.computeMayUse(Node,Node,ReachingUses,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/MaybeReachingVariableUse.java
Original range: 151-236
Documentation:

Method code:
151 |   private void computeMayUse(
152 |       Node n, Node cfgNode, ReachingUses output, boolean conditional) {
153 |     switch (n.getType()) {
154 | 
155 |       case Token.BLOCK:
156 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
157 |         return;
158 | 
159 |       case Token.NAME:
160 |         addToUseIfLocal(n.getString(), cfgNode, output);
161 |         return;
162 | 
163 |       case Token.WHILE:
164 |       case Token.DO:
165 |       case Token.IF:
166 |         computeMayUse(
167 |             NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), cfgNode, output, conditional);
168 |         return;
169 | 
170 |       case Token.FOR:
171 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(n)) {
172 |           computeMayUse(
173 |               NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), cfgNode, output, conditional);
174 |         } else {
175 |           // for(x in y) {...}
176 |           Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
177 |           Node rhs = lhs.getNext();
178 |           if (lhs.isVar()) {
179 |             lhs = lhs.getLastChild(); // for(var x in y) {...}
180 |           }
181 |           if (lhs.isName() && !conditional) {
182 |             removeFromUseIfLocal(lhs.getString(), output);
183 |           }
184 |           computeMayUse(rhs, cfgNode, output, conditional);
185 |         }
186 |         return;
187 | 
188 |       case Token.AND:
189 |       case Token.OR:
190 |         computeMayUse(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
191 |         computeMayUse(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
192 |         return;
193 | 
194 |       case Token.HOOK:
195 |         computeMayUse(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
196 |         computeMayUse(n.getFirstChild().getNext(), cfgNode, output, true);
197 |         computeMayUse(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
198 |         return;
199 | 
200 |       case Token.VAR:
201 |         Node varName = n.getFirstChild();
202 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.hasChildren(), "AST should be normalized");
203 | 
204 |         if (varName.hasChildren()) {
205 |           computeMayUse(varName.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
206 |           if (!conditional) {
207 |             removeFromUseIfLocal(varName.getString(), output);
208 |           }
209 |         }
210 |         return;
211 | 
212 |       default:
213 |         if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n) && n.getFirstChild().isName()) {
214 |           Node name = n.getFirstChild();
215 |           if (!conditional) {
216 |             removeFromUseIfLocal(name.getString(), output);
217 |           }
218 | 
219 |           // In case of a += "Hello". There is a read of a.
220 |           if (!n.isAssign()) {
221 |             addToUseIfLocal(name.getString(), cfgNode, output);
222 |           }
223 | 
224 |           computeMayUse(name.getNext(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
225 |         } else {
226 |           /*
227 |            * We want to traverse in reverse order because we want the LAST
228 |            * definition in the sub-tree....
229 |            * But we have no better way to traverse in reverse other :'(
230 |            */
231 |           for (Node c = n.getLastChild(); c != null; c = n.getChildBefore(c)) {
232 |             computeMayUse(c, cfgNode, output, conditional);
233 |           }
234 |         }
235 |     }
236 |   }

493 |   private void tryOptimizeConditionalAfterAssign(Node n) {
494 |     Node next = n.getNext();
495 | 
496 |     // Look for patterns like the following and replace the if-condition with
497 |     // a constant value so it can later be folded:
498 |     //   var a = /a/;
499 |     //   if (a) {foo(a)}
500 |     // or
501 |     //   a = 0;
502 |     //   a ? foo(a) : c;
503 |     // or
504 |     //   a = 0;
505 |     //   a || foo(a);
506 |     // or
507 |     //   a = 0;
508 |     //   a && foo(a)
509 |     //
510 |     // TODO(johnlenz): This would be better handled by control-flow sensitive
511 |     // constant propagation. As the other case that I want to handle is:
512 |     //   i=0; for(;i<0;i++){}
513 |     // as right now nothing facilitates removing a loop like that.
514 |     // This is here simply to remove the cruft left behind goog.userAgent and
515 |     // similar cases.
516 | 
517 |     if (isSimpleAssignment(n) && isConditionalStatement(next)) {
518 |       Node lhsAssign = getSimpleAssignmentName(n);
519 | 
520 |       Node condition = getConditionalStatementCondition(next);
521 |       if (lhsAssign.isName() && condition.isName()
522 |           && lhsAssign.getString().equals(condition.getString())) {
523 |         Node rhsAssign = getSimpleAssignmentValue(n);
524 |         TernaryValue value = NodeUtil.getImpureBooleanValue(rhsAssign);
525 |         if (value != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {

527 |               NodeUtil.booleanNode(value.toBoolean(true));
528 |           condition.getParent().replaceChild(condition,

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.OptimizeParameters.isMovableValue(Node,Scope)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/OptimizeParameters.java
Original range: 345-380
Documentation:
/**
   * @return Whether the expression can be safely moved to another function
   *   in another scope.
   */
Method code:
345 |   private boolean isMovableValue(Node n, Scope s) {
346 |     // Things that can change value or are inaccessible can't be moved, these
347 |     // are "this", "arguments", local names, and functions that capture local
348 |     // values.
349 |     switch (n.getType()) {
350 |       case Token.THIS:
351 |         return false;
352 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
353 |         // Don't move function closures.
354 |         // TODO(johnlenz): Closure that only contain global reference can be
355 |         // moved.
356 |         return false;
357 |       case Token.NAME:
358 |         if (n.getString().equals("arguments")) {
359 |           return false;
360 |         } else {
361 |           Var v = s.getVar(n.getString());
362 |           // Make sure that the variable is global. A caught exception, while
363 |           // it is in the global scope object in the compiler, it is not a
364 |           // global variable.
365 |           if (v != null &&
366 |               (v.isLocal() ||
367 |                v.nameNode.getParent().isCatch())) {
368 |             return false;
369 |           }
370 |         }
371 |         break;
372 |     }
373 | 
374 |     for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
375 |       if (!isMovableValue(c, s)) {
376 |         return false;
377 |       }
378 |     }
379 |     return true;
380 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.tryReplaceIf(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.java
Original range: 297-368
Documentation:
/**
   * Use "return x?1:2;" in place of "if(x)return 1;return 2;"
   */
Method code:
297 |   private Node tryReplaceIf(Node n) {
298 | 
299 |     for (Node child = n.getFirstChild();
300 |          child != null; child = child.getNext()){
301 |       if (child.isIf()){
302 |         Node cond = child.getFirstChild();
303 |         Node thenBranch = cond.getNext();
304 |         Node elseBranch = thenBranch.getNext();
305 |         Node nextNode = child.getNext();
306 | 
307 |         if (nextNode != null && elseBranch == null
308 |             && isReturnBlock(thenBranch)
309 |             && nextNode.isIf()) {
310 |           Node nextCond = nextNode.getFirstChild();
311 |           Node nextThen = nextCond.getNext();
312 |           Node nextElse = nextThen.getNext();
313 |           if (thenBranch.isEquivalentToTyped(nextThen)) {
314 |             // Transform
315 |             //   if (x) return 1; if (y) return 1;
316 |             // to
317 |             //   if (x||y) return 1;
318 |             child.detachFromParent();
319 |             child.detachChildren();
320 |             Node newCond = new Node(Token.OR, cond);
321 |             nextNode.replaceChild(nextCond, newCond);
322 |             newCond.addChildToBack(nextCond);
323 |             reportCodeChange();
324 |           } else if (nextElse != null
325 |               && thenBranch.isEquivalentToTyped(nextElse)) {
326 |             // Transform
327 |             //   if (x) return 1; if (y) foo() else return 1;
328 |             // to
329 |             //   if (!x&&y) foo() else return 1;
330 |             child.detachFromParent();
331 |             child.detachChildren();
332 |             Node newCond = new Node(Token.AND,
333 |                 IR.not(cond).srcref(cond));
334 |             nextNode.replaceChild(nextCond, newCond);
335 |             newCond.addChildToBack(nextCond);
336 |             reportCodeChange();
337 |           }
338 |         } else if (nextNode != null && elseBranch == null &&
339 |             isReturnBlock(thenBranch) && isReturnExpression(nextNode)) {
340 |           Node thenExpr = null;
341 |           // if(x)return; return 1 -> return x?void 0:1
342 |           if (isReturnExpressBlock(thenBranch)) {
343 |             thenExpr = getBlockReturnExpression(thenBranch);
344 |             thenExpr.detachFromParent();
345 |           } else {
346 |             thenExpr = NodeUtil.newUndefinedNode(child);
347 |           }
348 | 
349 |           Node elseExpr = nextNode.getFirstChild();
350 | 
351 |           cond.detachFromParent();
352 |           elseExpr.detachFromParent();
353 | 
354 |           Node returnNode = IR.returnNode(
355 |                                 IR.hook(cond, thenExpr, elseExpr)
356 |                                     .srcref(child));
357 |           n.replaceChild(child, returnNode);
358 |           n.removeChild(nextNode);
359 |           reportCodeChange();
360 |         } else if (elseBranch != null && statementMustExitParent(thenBranch)) {
361 |           child.removeChild(elseBranch);
362 |           n.addChildAfter(elseBranch, child);
363 |           reportCodeChange();
364 |         }
365 |       }
366 |     }
367 |     return n;
368 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.process(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 148-190

Method code:
148 |   @Override
149 |   public void process(Node externs, Node root) {
150 |     this.root = root;
151 |     astPositionCounter = 0;
152 |     astPosition = Maps.newHashMap();
153 |     nodePriorities = Maps.newHashMap();
154 |     cfg = new AstControlFlowGraph(computeFallThrough(root), nodePriorities,
155 |                                   edgeAnnotations);
156 |     NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, root, this);
157 |     astPosition.put(null, ++astPositionCounter); // the implicit return is last.
158 | 
159 |     // Now, generate the priority of nodes by doing a depth-first
160 |     // search on the CFG.
161 |     priorityCounter = 0;
162 |     DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> entry = cfg.getEntry();
163 |     prioritizeFromEntryNode(entry);

167 |       // priority of them too.

169 |         Node value = candidate.getValue();

171 |           Preconditions.checkState(
172 |               !nodePriorities.containsKey(candidate) || candidate == entry);
173 |           prioritizeFromEntryNode(candidate);

175 |       }
176 |     }
177 |

179 |     // unreachable nodes have not been given a priority. Put them last.
180 |     // Presumably, it doesn't really matter what priority they get, since
181 |     // this shouldn't happen in real code.
182 |     for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> candidate : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
183 |       if (!nodePriorities.containsKey(candidate)) {
184 |         nodePriorities.put(candidate, ++priorityCounter);
185 |       }
186 |     }
187 | 
188 |     // Again, the implicit return node is always last.
189 |     nodePriorities.put(cfg.getImplicitReturn(), ++priorityCounter);
190 |   }

/**
   * Merges the line number and character number in one integer. The Character
   * number takes the first 12 bits and the line number takes the rest. If
   * the character number is greater than <code>2<sup>12</sup>-1</code> it is
   * adjusted to <code>2<sup>12</sup>-1</code>.
   */
Method code:
1182 |   protected static int mergeLineCharNo(int lineno, int charno) {
1183 |     if (lineno < 0 || charno < 0) {
1184 |       return -1;
1185 |     } else if ((charno & ~COLUMN_MASK) != 0) {
1186 |       return lineno << COLUMN_BITS | COLUMN_MASK;
1187 |     } else {
1188 |       return lineno << COLUMN_BITS | (charno & COLUMN_MASK);
1189 |     }
1190 |   }

===== M0316 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.canBeSideEffected(Node,Set<String>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 1110-1142
Documentation:
/**
   * @param knownConstants A set of names known to be constant value at
   * node 'n' (such as locals that are last written before n can execute).
   * @return Whether the tree can be affected by side-effects or
   * has side-effects.
   */
Method code:
1110 |   static boolean canBeSideEffected(Node n, Set<String> knownConstants) {
1111 |     switch (n.getType()) {
1112 |       case Token.CALL:
1113 |       case Token.NEW:
1114 |         // Function calls or constructor can reference changed values.
1115 |         // TODO(johnlenz): Add some mechanism for determining that functions
1116 |         // are unaffected by side effects.
1117 |         return true;
1118 |       case Token.NAME:
1119 |         // Non-constant names values may have been changed.
1120 |         return !isConstantName(n)
1121 |             && !knownConstants.contains(n.getString());
1122 | 
1123 |       // Properties on constant NAMEs can still be side-effected.
1124 |       case Token.GETPROP:
1125 |       case Token.GETELEM:
1126 |         return true;
1127 | 
1128 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
1129 |         // Function expression are not changed by side-effects,
1130 |         // and function declarations are not part of expressions.
1131 |         Preconditions.checkState(isFunctionExpression(n));
1132 |         return false;
1133 |     }
1134 | 
1135 |     for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
1136 |       if (canBeSideEffected(c, knownConstants)) {
1137 |         return true;
1138 |       }
1139 |     }
1140 | 
1141 |     return false;
1142 |   }

===== M0329 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CoalesceVariableNames.computeVariableNamesInterferenceGraph(NodeTraversal,ControlFlowGraph<Node>,Set<Var>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CoalesceVariableNames.java
Original range: 212-305
Documentation:

Method code:
212 |   private UndiGraph<Var, Void> computeVariableNamesInterferenceGraph(
213 |       NodeTraversal t, ControlFlowGraph<Node> cfg, Set<Var> escaped) {
214 |     UndiGraph<Var, Void> interferenceGraph =
215 |         LinkedUndirectedGraph.create();
216 |     Scope scope = t.getScope();
217 | 
218 |     // First create a node for each non-escaped variable.
219 |     for (Iterator<Var> i = scope.getVars(); i.hasNext();) {
220 |       Var v = i.next();
221 |       if (!escaped.contains(v)) {
222 | 
223 |         // TODO(user): In theory, we CAN coalesce function names just like
224 |         // any variables. Our Liveness analysis captures this just like it as
225 |         // described in the specification. However, we saw some zipped and
226 |         // and unzipped size increase after this. We are not totally sure why
227 |         // that is but, for now, we will respect the dead functions and not play
228 |         // around with it.
229 |         if (!v.getParentNode().isFunction()) {
230 |           interferenceGraph.createNode(v);
231 |         }
232 |       }
233 |     }
234 | 
235 |     // Go through each variable and try to connect them.
236 |     for (Iterator<Var> i1 = scope.getVars(); i1.hasNext();) {
237 |       Var v1 = i1.next();
238 | 
239 |       NEXT_VAR_PAIR:
240 |       for (Iterator<Var> i2 = scope.getVars(); i2.hasNext();) {
241 |         Var v2 = i2.next();
242 | 
243 |         // Skip duplicate pairs.
244 |         if (v1.index >= v2.index) {
245 |           continue;
246 |         }
247 | 
248 |         if (!interferenceGraph.hasNode(v1) ||
249 |             !interferenceGraph.hasNode(v2)) {
250 |           // Skip nodes that were not added. They are globals and escaped
251 |           // locals. Also avoid merging a variable with itself.
252 |           continue NEXT_VAR_PAIR;
253 |         }
254 | 
255 |         if (v1.getParentNode().isParamList() &&
256 |             v2.getParentNode().isParamList()) {
257 |           interferenceGraph.connectIfNotFound(v1, null, v2);
258 |           continue NEXT_VAR_PAIR;
259 |         }
260 | 
261 |         // Go through every CFG node in the program and look at
262 |         // this variable pair. If they are both live at the same
263 |         // time, add an edge between them and continue to the next pair.
264 |         NEXT_CROSS_CFG_NODE:
265 |         for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> cfgNode : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
266 |           if (cfg.isImplicitReturn(cfgNode)) {
267 |             continue NEXT_CROSS_CFG_NODE;
268 |           }
269 | 
270 |           FlowState<LiveVariableLattice> state = cfgNode.getAnnotation();
271 |           // Check the live states and add edge when possible.
272 |           if ((state.getIn().isLive(v1) && state.getIn().isLive(v2)) ||
273 |               (state.getOut().isLive(v1) && state.getOut().isLive(v2))) {
274 |             interferenceGraph.connectIfNotFound(v1, null, v2);
275 |             continue NEXT_VAR_PAIR;
276 |           }
277 |         }
278 | 
279 |         // v1 and v2 might not have an edge between them! woohoo. there's
280 |         // one last sanity check that we have to do: we have to check
281 |         // if there's a collision *within* the cfg node.
282 |         NEXT_INTRA_CFG_NODE:
283 |         for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> cfgNode : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
284 |           if (cfg.isImplicitReturn(cfgNode)) {
285 |             continue NEXT_INTRA_CFG_NODE;
286 |           }
287 | 
288 |           FlowState<LiveVariableLattice> state = cfgNode.getAnnotation();
289 |           boolean v1OutLive = state.getOut().isLive(v1);
290 |           boolean v2OutLive = state.getOut().isLive(v2);
291 |           CombinedLiveRangeChecker checker = new CombinedLiveRangeChecker(
292 |               new LiveRangeChecker(v1, v2OutLive ? null : v2),
293 |               new LiveRangeChecker(v2, v1OutLive ? null : v1));
294 |           NodeTraversal.traverse(
295 |               compiler,
296 |               cfgNode.getValue(),
297 |               checker);
298 |           if (checker.connectIfCrossed(interferenceGraph)) {
299 |             continue NEXT_VAR_PAIR;
300 |           }
301 |         }
302 |       }
303 |     }
304 |     return interferenceGraph;
305 |   }

767 |     public boolean shouldTraverse(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
768 |       if (parent == null) {

770 |       }
771 | 
772 |       // Gather the list of nodes that either have side effects, are
773 |       // arguments to function calls with side effects or are used in
774 |       // control structure predicates.  These names are always

786 |           Node iter = decl.getNext();

788 |           addAllChildren(iter);
789 |         }

794 |           parent.isReturn() ||
795 |           parent.isThrow()) {

797 |       }

800 |            parent.isWhile() ||
801 |            parent.isWith() ||
802 |            parent.isSwitch() ||
803 |            parent.isCase()) &&
804 |           parent.getFirstChild() == n) {
805 |         addAllChildren(n);
806 |       }

809 |         addAllChildren(n);

453 |         return emptyStringNode;
454 |       case 1:
455 |         Node foldedStringNode = arrayFoldedChildren.remove(0);
456 |         if (foldedSize > originalSize) {
457 |           return n;
458 |         }
459 |         arrayNode.detachChildren();
460 |         if (!foldedStringNode.isString()) {
461 |           // If the Node is not a string literal, ensure that
462 |           // it is coerced to a string.
463 |           Node replacement = IR.add(
464 |               IR.string("").srcref(n),
465 |               foldedStringNode);
466 |           foldedStringNode = replacement;
467 |         }
468 |         n.getParent().replaceChild(n, foldedStringNode);
469 |         reportCodeChange();
470 |         return foldedStringNode;
471 |       default:
472 |         // No folding could actually be performed.
473 |         if (arrayFoldedChildren.size() == arrayNode.getChildCount()) {
474 |           return n;
475 |         }
476 |         int kJoinOverhead = "[].join()".length();
477 |         foldedSize += kJoinOverhead;
478 |         foldedSize += (right != null) ? InlineCostEstimator.getCost(right) : 0;
479 |         if (foldedSize > originalSize) {
480 |           return n;
481 |         }
482 |         arrayNode.detachChildren();
483 |         for (Node node : arrayFoldedChildren) {
484 |           arrayNode.addChildToBack(node);
485 |         }
486 |         reportCodeChange();
487 |         break;
488 |     }
489 | 
490 |     return n;
491 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ReferenceCollectingCallback.ReferenceCollection.isWellDefined()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ReferenceCollectingCallback.java
Original range: 310-333
Documentation:
/**
     * Determines if the variable for this reference collection is
     * "well-defined." A variable is well-defined if we can prove at
     * compile-time that it's assigned a value before it's used.
     *
     * Notice that if this function returns false, this doesn't imply that the
     * variable is used before it's assigned. It just means that we don't
     * have enough information to make a definitive judgement.
     */
Method code:
310 |     protected boolean isWellDefined() {
311 |       int size = references.size();
312 |       if (size == 0) {
313 |         return false;
314 |       }
315 | 
316 |       // If this is a declaration that does not instantiate the variable,
317 |       // it's not well-defined.
318 |       Reference init = getInitializingReference();
319 |       if (init == null) {
320 |         return false;
321 |       }
322 | 
323 |       Preconditions.checkState(references.get(0).isDeclaration());
324 |       BasicBlock initBlock = init.getBasicBlock();
325 |       for (int i = 1; i < size; i++) {
326 |         if (!initBlock.provablyExecutesBefore(
327 |                 references.get(i).getBasicBlock())) {
328 |           return false;
329 |         }
330 |       }
331 | 
332 |       return true;
333 |     }

/**
   * Since this pass reports errors only when a global {@code this} keyword
   * is encountered, there is no reason to traverse non global contexts.
   */
Method code:
79 |   @Override
80 |   public boolean shouldTraverse(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
81 | 
82 |     if (n.isFunction()) {
83 |       // Don't traverse functions that are constructors or have the @this
84 |       // or @override annotation.
85 |       JSDocInfo jsDoc = getFunctionJsDocInfo(n);
86 |       if (jsDoc != null &&
87 |           (jsDoc.isConstructor() ||
88 |            jsDoc.isInterface() ||
89 |            jsDoc.hasThisType() ||
90 |            jsDoc.isOverride())) {
91 |         return false;
92 |       }
93 | 
94 |       // Don't traverse functions unless they would normally
95 |       // be able to have a @this annotation associated with them. e.g.,
96 |       // var a = function() { }; // or
97 |       // function a() {} // or
98 |       // a.x = function() {}; // or
99 |       // var a = {x: function() {}};
100 |       int pType = parent.getType();
101 |       if (!(pType == Token.BLOCK ||
102 |             pType == Token.SCRIPT ||
103 |             pType == Token.NAME ||
104 |             pType == Token.ASSIGN ||
105 | 
106 |             // object literal keys
107 |             pType == Token.STRING)) {
108 |         return false;
109 |       }
110 | 
111 |       // Don't traverse functions that are getting lent to a prototype.
112 |       Node gramps = parent.getParent();
113 |       if (NodeUtil.isObjectLitKey(parent, gramps)) {
114 |         JSDocInfo maybeLends = gramps.getJSDocInfo();
115 |         if (maybeLends != null &&
116 |             maybeLends.getLendsName() != null &&
117 |             maybeLends.getLendsName().endsWith(".prototype")) {
118 |           return false;
119 |         }
120 |       }
121 |     }
122 | 
123 |     if (parent != null && parent.isAssign()) {
124 |       Node lhs = parent.getFirstChild();
125 |       Node rhs = lhs.getNext();
126 | 
127 |       if (n == lhs) {
128 |         // Always traverse the left side of the assignment. To handle
129 |         // nested assignments properly (e.g., (a = this).property = c;),
130 |         // assignLhsChild should not be overridden.
131 |         if (assignLhsChild == null) {
132 |           assignLhsChild = lhs;
133 |         }
134 |       } else {
135 |         // Only traverse the right side if it's not an assignment to a prototype
136 |         // property or subproperty.
137 |         if (NodeUtil.isGet(lhs)) {
138 |           if (lhs.isGetProp() &&
139 |               lhs.getLastChild().getString().equals("prototype")) {
140 |             return false;
141 |           }
142 |           Node llhs = lhs.getFirstChild();
143 |           if (llhs.isGetProp() &&
144 |               llhs.getLastChild().getString().equals("prototype")) {
145 |             return false;
146 |           }
147 |         }
148 |       }
149 |     }
150 | 
151 |     return true;
152 |   }

Documentation:
/**
   * Traverses everything in the current scope and marks variables that
   * are referenced.
   *
   * During traversal, we identify subtrees that will only be
   * referenced if their enclosing variables are referenced. Instead of
   * traversing those subtrees, we create a continuation for them,
   * and traverse them lazily.
   */
Method code:
192 |   private void traverseNode(Node n, Node parent, Scope scope) {
193 |     int type = n.getType();
194 |     Var var = null;
195 |     switch (type) {
196 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
197 |         // If this function is a removable var, then create a continuation
198 |         // for it instead of traversing immediately.
199 |         if (NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(n)) {
200 |           var = scope.getVar(n.getFirstChild().getString());
201 |         }
202 | 
203 |         if (var != null && isRemovableVar(var)) {
204 |           continuations.put(var, new Continuation(n, scope));
205 |         } else {
206 |           traverseFunction(n, scope);
207 |         }
208 |         return;
209 | 
210 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
211 |         Assign maybeAssign = Assign.maybeCreateAssign(n);
212 |         if (maybeAssign != null) {
213 |           // Put this in the assign map. It might count as a reference,
214 |           // but we won't know that until we have an index of all assigns.
215 |           var = scope.getVar(maybeAssign.nameNode.getString());
216 |           if (var != null) {
217 |             assignsByVar.put(var, maybeAssign);
218 |             assignsByNode.put(maybeAssign.nameNode, maybeAssign);
219 | 
220 |             if (isRemovableVar(var) &&
221 |                 !maybeAssign.mayHaveSecondarySideEffects) {
222 |               // If the var is unreferenced and performing this assign has
223 |               // no secondary side effects, then we can create a continuation
224 |               // for it instead of traversing immediately.
225 |               continuations.put(var, new Continuation(n, scope));
226 |               return;
227 |             }
228 |           }
229 |         }
230 |         break;
231 | 
232 |       case Token.CALL:
233 |         // Look for calls to inheritance-defining calls (such as goog.inherits).
234 |         SubclassRelationship subclassRelationship =
235 |             codingConvention.getClassesDefinedByCall(n);
236 |         if (subclassRelationship != null) {
237 |           Var subclassVar = scope.getVar(subclassRelationship.subclassName);
238 |           // Don't try to track the inheritance calls for non-globals. It would
239 |           // be more correct to only not track when the subclass does not
240 |           // reference a constructor, but checking that it is a global is
241 |           // easier and mostly the same.
242 |           if (subclassVar != null && subclassVar.isGlobal()
243 |               && !referenced.contains(subclassVar)) {
244 |             // Save a reference to the EXPR node.
245 |             inheritsCalls.put(subclassVar, parent);
246 |             continuations.put(subclassVar, new Continuation(n, scope));
247 |             return;
248 |           }
249 |         }
250 |         break;
251 | 
252 |       case Token.NAME:
253 |         var = scope.getVar(n.getString());
254 |         if (parent.isVar()) {
255 |           Node value = n.getFirstChild();
256 |           if (value != null && var != null && isRemovableVar(var) &&
257 |               !NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(value)) {
258 |             // If the var is unreferenced and creating its value has no side
259 |             // effects, then we can create a continuation for it instead
260 |             // of traversing immediately.
261 |             continuations.put(var, new Continuation(n, scope));
262 |             return;
263 |           }
264 |         } else {
265 | 
266 |           // If arguments is escaped, we just assume the worst and continue
267 |           // on all the parameters.
268 |           if ("arguments".equals(n.getString()) && scope.isLocal()) {
269 |             Node lp = scope.getRootNode().getFirstChild().getNext();
270 |             for (Node a = lp.getFirstChild(); a != null; a = a.getNext()) {
271 |               markReferencedVar(scope.getVar(a.getString()));
272 |             }
273 |           }
274 | 
275 |           // All name references that aren't declarations or assigns
276 |           // are references to other vars.
277 |           if (var != null) {
278 |             // If that var hasn't already been marked referenced, then
279 |             // start tracking it.  If this is an assign, do nothing
280 |             // for now.
281 |             if (isRemovableVar(var)) {
282 |               if (!assignsByNode.containsKey(n)) {
283 |                 markReferencedVar(var);
284 |               }
285 |             } else {
286 |               markReferencedVar(var);
287 |             }
288 |           }
289 |         }
290 |         break;
291 |     }
292 | 
293 |     for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
294 |       traverseNode(c, n, scope);
295 |     }
296 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.tryReplaceExitWithBreak(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.java
Original range: 445-496
Documentation:
/**
   * Replace duplicate exits in control structures.  If the node following
   * the exit node expression has the same effect as exit node, the node can
   * be replaced or removed.
   * For example:
   *   "while (a) {return f()} return f();" ==> "while (a) {break} return f();"
   *   "while (a) {throw 'ow'} throw 'ow';" ==> "while (a) {break} throw 'ow';"
   *
   * @param n An follow control exit expression (a THROW or RETURN node)
   * @return The replacement for n, or the original if no change was made.
   */
Method code:
445 |   private Node tryReplaceExitWithBreak(Node n) {
446 |     Node result = n.getFirstChild();
447 | 
448 |     // Find the enclosing control structure, if any, that a "break" would exit
449 |     // from.
450 |     Node breakTarget = n;
451 |     for (;!ControlFlowAnalysis.isBreakTarget(breakTarget, null /* no label */);
452 |         breakTarget = breakTarget.getParent()) {
453 |       if (breakTarget.isFunction() || breakTarget.isScript()) {
454 |         // No break target.
455 |         return n;
456 |       }
457 |     }
458 | 
459 |     Node follow = ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode(breakTarget);
460 | 
461 |     // Skip pass all the finally blocks because both the break and return will
462 |     // also trigger all the finally blocks. However, the order of execution is
463 |     // slightly changed. Consider:
464 |     //
465 |     // return a() -> finally { b() } -> return a()
466 |     //
467 |     // which would call a() first. However, changing the first return to a
468 |     // break will result in calling b().
469 | 
470 |     Node prefinallyFollows = follow;
471 |     follow = skipFinallyNodes(follow);
472 | 
473 |     if (prefinallyFollows != follow) {
474 |       // There were finally clauses
475 |       if (!isPure(result)) {
476 |         // Can't defer the exit
477 |         return n;
478 |       }
479 |     }
480 | 
481 |     if (follow == null && (n.isThrow() || result != null)) {
482 |       // Can't complete remove a throw here or a return with a result.
483 |       return n;
484 |     }
485 | 
486 |     // When follow is null, this mean the follow of a break target is the
487 |     // end of a function. This means a break is same as return.
488 |     if (follow == null || areMatchingExits(n, follow)) {
489 |       Node replacement = IR.breakNode();
490 |       n.getParent().replaceChild(n, replacement);
491 |       this.reportCodeChange();
492 |       return replacement;
493 |     }
494 | 
495 |     return n;
496 |   }

Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/JSType.java
Original range: 989-991
Documentation:
/**
   * Checks whether {@code this} is a subtype of {@code that}.<p>
   *
   * Subtyping rules:
   * <ul>
   * <li>(unknown) &mdash; every type is a subtype of the Unknown type.</li>
   * <li>(no) &mdash; the No type is a subtype of every type.</li>
   * <li>(no-object) &mdash; the NoObject type is a subtype of every object
   * type (i.e. subtypes of the Object type).</li>
   * <li>(ref) &mdash; a type is a subtype of itself.</li>
   * <li>(union-l) &mdash; A union type is a subtype of a type U if all the
   * union type's constituents are a subtype of U. Formally<br>
   * {@code (T<sub>1</sub>, &hellip;, T<sub>n</sub>) &lt;: U} if and only
   * {@code T<sub>k</sub> &lt;: U} for all {@code k &isin; 1..n}.</li>
   * <li>(union-r) &mdash; A type U is a subtype of a union type if it is a
   * subtype of one of the union type's constituents. Formally<br>
   * {@code U &lt;: (T<sub>1</sub>, &hellip;, T<sub>n</sub>)} if and only
   * if {@code U &lt;: T<sub>k</sub>} for some index {@code k}.</li>
   * <li>(objects) &mdash; an Object {@code O<sub>1</sub>} is a subtype
   * of an object {@code O<sub>2</sub>} if it has more properties
   * than {@code O<sub>2</sub>} and all common properties are
   * pairwise subtypes.</li>
   * </ul>
   *
   * @return {@code this &lt;: that}
   */
Method code:
989 |   public boolean isSubtype(JSType that) {
990 |     return isSubtypeHelper(this, that);
991 |   }

Documentation:
/**
   * Compute set of escaped variables. When a variable is escaped in a
   * dataflow analysis, it can be reference outside of the code that we are
   * analyzing. A variable is escaped if any of the following is true:
   *
   * <p><ol>
   * <li>It is defined as the exception name in CATCH clause so it became a
   * variable local not to our definition of scope.</li>
   * <li>Exported variables as they can be needed after the script terminates.
   * </li>
   * <li>Names of named functions because in javascript, <i>function foo(){}</i>
   * does not kill <i>foo</i> in the dataflow.</li>
   */
Method code:
546 |   static void computeEscaped(final Scope jsScope, final Set<Var> escaped,
547 |       AbstractCompiler compiler) {
548 |     // TODO(user): Very good place to store this information somewhere.
549 |     AbstractPostOrderCallback finder = new AbstractPostOrderCallback() {
550 |       @Override
551 |       public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
552 |         if (jsScope == t.getScope() || !n.isName()
553 |             || parent.isFunction()) {
554 |           return;
555 |         }
556 |         String name = n.getString();
557 |         Var var = t.getScope().getVar(name);
558 |         if (var != null && var.scope == jsScope) {
559 |           escaped.add(jsScope.getVar(name));
560 |         }
561 |       }
562 |     };
563 | 
564 |     NodeTraversal t = new NodeTraversal(compiler, finder);
565 |     t.traverseAtScope(jsScope);
566 | 
567 |     // 1: Remove the exception name in CATCH which technically isn't local to
568 |     //    begin with.
569 |     for (Iterator<Var> i = jsScope.getVars(); i.hasNext();) {
570 |       Var var = i.next();
571 |       if (var.getParentNode().isCatch() ||
572 |           compiler.getCodingConvention().isExported(var.getName())) {
573 |         escaped.add(var);
574 |       }
575 |     }
576 |   }

===== M0536 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.graph.FixedPointGraphTraversal.computeFixedPoint(DiGraph<N, E>,Set<N>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/graph/FixedPointGraphTraversal.java
Original range: 93-128
Documentation:
/**
   * Compute a fixed point for the given graph, entering from the given nodes.
   * @param graph The graph to traverse.
   * @param entrySet The nodes to begin traversing from.
   */
Method code:
93 |   public void computeFixedPoint(DiGraph<N, E> graph, Set<N> entrySet) {
94 |     int cycleCount = 0;
95 |     long nodeCount = graph.getNodes().size();
96 | 
97 |     // Choose a bail-out heuristically in case the computation
98 |     // doesn't converge.
99 |     long maxIterations = Math.max(nodeCount * nodeCount * nodeCount, 100);
100 | 
101 |     // Use a LinkedHashSet, so that the traversal is deterministic.
102 |     LinkedHashSet<DiGraphNode<N, E>> workSet =
103 |         Sets.newLinkedHashSet();
104 |     for (N n : entrySet) {
105 |       workSet.add(graph.getDirectedGraphNode(n));
106 |     }
107 |     for (; !workSet.isEmpty() && cycleCount < maxIterations; cycleCount++) {
108 |       // For every out edge in the workSet, traverse that edge. If that
109 |       // edge updates the state of the graph, then add the destination
110 |       // node to the resultSet, so that we can update all of its out edges
111 |       // on the next iteration.
112 |       DiGraphNode<N, E> source = workSet.iterator().next();
113 |       N sourceValue = source.getValue();
114 | 
115 |       workSet.remove(source);
116 | 
117 |       List<DiGraphEdge<N, E>> outEdges = source.getOutEdges();
118 |       for (DiGraphEdge<N, E> edge : outEdges) {
119 |         N destNode = edge.getDestination().getValue();
120 |         if (callback.traverseEdge(sourceValue, edge.getValue(), destNode)) {
121 |           workSet.add(edge.getDestination());
122 |         }
123 |       }
124 |     }
125 | 
126 |     Preconditions.checkState(cycleCount != maxIterations,
127 |         NON_HALTING_ERROR_MSG);
128 |   }
