Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.OptimizeParameters.canChangeSignature(DefinitionSite,SimpleDefinitionFinder)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/OptimizeParameters.java
Original range: 85-147
Documentation:
/**
   * @return Whether the definitionSite represents a function whose call
   *      signature can be modified.
   */
Method code:
85 |   private boolean canChangeSignature(
86 |       DefinitionSite definitionSite, SimpleDefinitionFinder defFinder) {
87 |     Definition definition = definitionSite.definition;
88 | 
89 |     if (definitionSite.inExterns) {
90 |       return false;
91 |     }
92 | 
93 |     // Only functions may be rewritten.
94 |     // Functions that access "arguments" are not eligible since
95 |     // rewrite changes the structure of this object.
96 |     Node rValue = definition.getRValue();
97 |     if (rValue == null ||
98 |         !rValue.isFunction() ||
99 |         NodeUtil.isVarArgsFunction(rValue)) {
100 |       return false;
101 |     }
102 | 
103 |     // TODO(johnlenz): support rewriting methods defined as part of
104 |     // object literals (they are generally problematic because they may be
105 |     // maps of functions use in for-in expressions, etc).
106 |     // Be conservative, don't try to optimize any declaration that isn't as
107 |     // simple function declaration or assignment.
108 |     if (!SimpleDefinitionFinder.isSimpleFunctionDeclaration(rValue)) {
109 |       return false;
110 |     }
111 | 
112 |     // Assume an exported method result is used.
113 |     if (!defFinder.canModifyDefinition(definition)) {
114 |       return false;
115 |     }
116 | 
117 |     Collection<UseSite> useSites = defFinder.getUseSites(definition);
118 | 
119 |     if (useSites.isEmpty()) {
120 |       return false;
121 |     }
122 | 
123 |     for (UseSite site : useSites) {
124 |       // Any non-call reference maybe introducing an alias. Don't try to
125 |       // change the function signature, if all the aliases can't also be
126 |       // changed.
127 |       // TODO(johnlenz): Support .call signature changes.
128 |       if (!SimpleDefinitionFinder.isCallOrNewSite(site)) {
129 |         return false;
130 |       }
131 | 
132 |       // TODO(johnlenz): support specialization
133 | 
134 |       // Multiple definitions prevent rewrite.
135 |       // TODO(johnlenz): Allow rewrite all definitions are valid.
136 |       Node nameNode = site.node;
137 |       Collection<Definition> singleSiteDefinitions =
138 |           defFinder.getDefinitionsReferencedAt(nameNode);
139 |       if (singleSiteDefinitions.size() > 1) {
140 |         return false;
141 |       }
142 |       Preconditions.checkState(!singleSiteDefinitions.isEmpty());
143 |       Preconditions.checkState(singleSiteDefinitions.contains(definition));
144 |     }
145 | 
146 |     return true;
147 |   }

===== M0551 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.tryMinimizeCondition(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.java
Original range: 1120-1300
Documentation:
/**
   * Try to minimize conditions expressions, as there are additional
   * assumptions that can be made when it is known that the final result
   * is a boolean.
   *
   * The following transformations are done recursively:
   *   !(x||y) --> !x&&!y
   *   !(x&&y) --> !x||!y
   *   !!x     --> x
   * Thus:
   *   !(x&&!y) --> !x||!!y --> !x||y
   *
   *   Returns the replacement for n, or the original if no change was made
   */
Method code:
1120 |   private Node tryMinimizeCondition(Node n) {
1121 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
1122 | 
1123 |     switch (n.getType()) {
1124 |       case Token.NOT:
1125 |         Node first = n.getFirstChild();
1126 |         switch (first.getType()) {
1127 |           case Token.NOT: {
1128 |               Node newRoot = first.removeFirstChild();
1129 |               parent.replaceChild(n, newRoot);
1130 |               reportCodeChange();
1131 |               // No need to traverse, tryMinimizeCondition is called on the
1132 |               // NOT children are handled below.
1133 |               return newRoot;
1134 |             }
1135 |           case Token.AND:
1136 |           case Token.OR: {
1137 |               // !(!x && !y) --> x || y
1138 |               // !(!x || !y) --> x && y
1139 |               // !(!x && y) --> x || !y
1140 |               // !(!x || y) --> x && !y
1141 |               // !(x && !y) --> !x || y
1142 |               // !(x || !y) --> !x && y
1143 |               // !(x && y) --> !x || !y
1144 |               // !(x || y) --> !x && !y
1145 |               Node leftParent = first.getFirstChild();
1146 |               Node rightParent = first.getLastChild();
1147 |               Node left, right;
1148 | 
1149 |               // Check special case when such transformation cannot reduce
1150 |               // due to the added ()
1151 |               // It only occurs when both of expressions are not NOT expressions
1152 |               if (!leftParent.isNot()
1153 |                   && !rightParent.isNot()) {
1154 |                 // If an expression has higher precendence than && or ||,
1155 |                 // but lower precedence than NOT, an additional () is needed
1156 |                 // Thus we do not preceed
1157 |                 int op_precedence = NodeUtil.precedence(first.getType());
1158 |                 if ((isLowerPrecedence(leftParent, NOT_PRECEDENCE)
1159 |                     && isHigherPrecedence(leftParent, op_precedence))
1160 |                     || (isLowerPrecedence(rightParent, NOT_PRECEDENCE)
1161 |                     && isHigherPrecedence(rightParent, op_precedence))) {
1162 |                   return n;
1163 |                 }
1164 |               }
1165 | 
1166 |               if (leftParent.isNot()) {
1167 |                 left = leftParent.removeFirstChild();
1168 |               } else {
1169 |                 leftParent.detachFromParent();
1170 |                 left = IR.not(leftParent).srcref(leftParent);
1171 |               }
1172 |               if (rightParent.isNot()) {
1173 |                 right = rightParent.removeFirstChild();
1174 |               } else {
1175 |                 rightParent.detachFromParent();
1176 |                 right = IR.not(rightParent).srcref(rightParent);
1177 |               }
1178 | 
1179 |               int newOp = (first.isAnd()) ? Token.OR : Token.AND;
1180 |               Node newRoot = new Node(newOp, left, right);
1181 |               parent.replaceChild(n, newRoot);
1182 |               reportCodeChange();
1183 |               // No need to traverse, tryMinimizeCondition is called on the
1184 |               // AND and OR children below.
1185 |               return newRoot;
1186 |             }
1187 | 
1188 |            default:
1189 |              TernaryValue nVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(first);
1190 |              if (nVal != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
1191 |                boolean result = nVal.not().toBoolean(true);
1192 |                int equivalentResult = result ? 1 : 0;
1193 |                return maybeReplaceChildWithNumber(n, parent, equivalentResult);
1194 |              }
1195 |         }
1196 |         // No need to traverse, tryMinimizeCondition is called on the NOT
1197 |         // children in the general case in the main post-order traversal.
1198 |         return n;
1199 | 
1200 |       case Token.OR:
1201 |       case Token.AND: {
1202 |         Node left = n.getFirstChild();
1203 |         Node right = n.getLastChild();
1204 | 
1205 |         // Because the expression is in a boolean context minimize
1206 |         // the children, this can't be done in the general case.
1207 |         left = tryMinimizeCondition(left);
1208 |         right = tryMinimizeCondition(right);
1209 | 
1210 |         // Remove useless conditionals
1211 |         // Handle four cases:
1212 |         //   x || false --> x
1213 |         //   x || true  --> true
1214 |         //   x && true --> x
1215 |         //   x && false  --> false
1216 |         TernaryValue rightVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(right);
1217 |         if (NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(right) != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
1218 |           int type = n.getType();
1219 |           Node replacement = null;
1220 |           boolean rval = rightVal.toBoolean(true);
1221 | 
1222 |           // (x || FALSE) => x
1223 |           // (x && TRUE) => x
1224 |           if (type == Token.OR && !rval ||
1225 |               type == Token.AND && rval) {
1226 |             replacement = left;
1227 |           } else if (!mayHaveSideEffects(left)) {
1228 |             replacement = right;
1229 |           }
1230 | 
1231 |           if (replacement != null) {
1232 |             n.detachChildren();
1233 |             parent.replaceChild(n, replacement);
1234 |             reportCodeChange();
1235 |             return replacement;
1236 |           }
1237 |         }
1238 |         return n;
1239 |       }
1240 | 
1241 |       case Token.HOOK: {
1242 |         Node condition = n.getFirstChild();
1243 |         Node trueNode = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
1244 |         Node falseNode = n.getLastChild();
1245 | 
1246 |         // Because the expression is in a boolean context minimize
1247 |         // the result children, this can't be done in the general case.
1248 |         // The condition is handled in the general case in #optimizeSubtree
1249 |         trueNode = tryMinimizeCondition(trueNode);
1250 |         falseNode = tryMinimizeCondition(falseNode);
1251 | 
1252 |         // Handle four cases:
1253 |         //   x ? true : false --> x
1254 |         //   x ? false : true --> !x
1255 |         //   x ? true : y     --> x || y
1256 |         //   x ? y : false    --> x && y
1257 |         Node replacement = null;
1258 |         TernaryValue trueNodeVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(trueNode);
1259 |         TernaryValue falseNodeVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(falseNode);
1260 |         if (trueNodeVal == TernaryValue.TRUE
1261 |             && falseNodeVal == TernaryValue.FALSE) {
1262 |           // Remove useless conditionals, keep the condition
1263 |           condition.detachFromParent();
1264 |           replacement = condition;
1265 |         } else if (trueNodeVal == TernaryValue.FALSE
1266 |             && falseNodeVal == TernaryValue.TRUE) {
1267 |           // Remove useless conditionals, keep the condition
1268 |           condition.detachFromParent();
1269 |           replacement = IR.not(condition);
1270 |         } else if (trueNodeVal == TernaryValue.TRUE) {
1271 |           // Remove useless true case.
1272 |           n.detachChildren();
1273 |           replacement = IR.or(condition, falseNode);
1274 |         } else if (falseNodeVal == TernaryValue.FALSE) {
1275 |           // Remove useless false case
1276 |           n.detachChildren();
1277 |           replacement = IR.and(condition, trueNode);
1278 |         }
1279 | 
1280 |         if (replacement != null) {
1281 |           parent.replaceChild(n, replacement);
1282 |           n = replacement;
1283 |           reportCodeChange();
1284 |         }
1285 | 
1286 |         return n;
1287 |       }
1288 | 
1289 |       default:
1290 |         // while(true) --> while(1)
1291 |         TernaryValue nVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(n);
1292 |         if (nVal != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
1293 |           boolean result = nVal.toBoolean(true);
1294 |           int equivalentResult = result ? 1 : 0;
1295 |           return maybeReplaceChildWithNumber(n, parent, equivalentResult);
1296 |         }
1297 |         // We can't do anything else currently.
1298 |         return n;
1299 |     }
1300 |   }

/**
   * Gets the boolean value of a node that represents a literal. This method
   * effectively emulates the <code>Boolean()</code> JavaScript cast function
   * except it return UNKNOWN for known values with side-effects, use
   * getExpressionBooleanValue if you don't care about side-effects.
   */
Method code:
124 |   static TernaryValue getPureBooleanValue(Node n) {
125 |     switch (n.getType()) {
126 |       case Token.STRING:
127 |         return TernaryValue.forBoolean(n.getString().length() > 0);
128 | 
129 |       case Token.NUMBER:
130 |         return TernaryValue.forBoolean(n.getDouble() != 0);
131 | 
132 |       case Token.NOT:
133 |         return getPureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild()).not();
134 | 
135 |       case Token.NULL:
136 |       case Token.FALSE:
137 |         return TernaryValue.FALSE;
138 | 
139 |       case Token.VOID:
140 |         if (!mayHaveSideEffects(n.getFirstChild())) {
141 |           return TernaryValue.FALSE;
142 |         }
143 |         break;
144 | 
145 |       case Token.NAME:
146 |         String name = n.getString();
147 |         if ("undefined".equals(name)
148 |             || "NaN".equals(name)) {
149 |           // We assume here that programs don't change the value of the keyword
150 |           // undefined to something other than the value undefined.
151 |           return TernaryValue.FALSE;
152 |         } else if ("Infinity".equals(name)) {
153 |           return TernaryValue.TRUE;
154 |         }
155 |         break;
156 | 
157 |       case Token.TRUE:
158 |       case Token.REGEXP:
159 |         return TernaryValue.TRUE;
160 | 
161 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
162 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
163 |         if (!mayHaveSideEffects(n)) {
164 |           return TernaryValue.TRUE;
165 |         }
166 |         break;
167 |     }
168 | 
169 |     return TernaryValue.UNKNOWN;
170 |   }

254 |     private void inlineNonConstants(
255 |         Var v, ReferenceCollection referenceInfo,
256 |         boolean maybeModifiedArguments) {
257 |       int refCount = referenceInfo.references.size();
258 |       Reference declaration = referenceInfo.references.get(0);
259 |       Reference init = referenceInfo.getInitializingReference();
260 |       int firstRefAfterInit = (declaration == init) ? 2 : 3;
261 | 
262 |       if (refCount > 1 &&
263 |           isImmutableAndWellDefinedVariable(v, referenceInfo)) {
264 |         // if the variable is referenced more than once, we can only
265 |         // inline it if it's immutable and never defined before referenced.
266 |         Node value;
267 |         if (init != null) {
268 |           value = init.getAssignedValue();
269 |         } else {
270 |           // Create a new node for variable that is never initialized.
271 |           Node srcLocation = declaration.getNode();
272 |           value = NodeUtil.newUndefinedNode(srcLocation);
273 |         }
274 |         Preconditions.checkNotNull(value);
275 |         inlineWellDefinedVariable(v, value, referenceInfo.references);
276 |         staleVars.add(v);
277 |       } else if (refCount == firstRefAfterInit) {
278 |         // The variable likely only read once, try some more
279 |         // complex inlining heuristics.
280 |         Reference reference = referenceInfo.references.get(
281 |             firstRefAfterInit - 1);
282 |         if (canInline(declaration, init, reference)) {
283 |           inline(v, declaration, init, reference);
284 |           staleVars.add(v);
285 |         }
286 |       } else if (declaration != init && refCount == 2) {
287 |         if (isValidDeclaration(declaration) && isValidInitialization(init)) {
288 |           // The only reference is the initialization, remove the assignment and
289 |           // the variable declaration.
290 |           Node value = init.getAssignedValue();
291 |           Preconditions.checkNotNull(value);
292 |           inlineWellDefinedVariable(v, value, referenceInfo.references);
293 |           staleVars.add(v);
294 |         }
295 |       }
296 | 
297 |       // If this variable was not inlined normally, check if we can
298 |       // inline an alias of it. (If the variable was inlined, then the
299 |       // reference data is out of sync. We're better off just waiting for
300 |       // the next pass.)
301 |       if (!maybeModifiedArguments &&
302 |           !staleVars.contains(v) && referenceInfo.isWellDefined() &&
303 |           referenceInfo.isAssignedOnceInLifetime()) {
304 |         List<Reference> refs = referenceInfo.references;
305 |         for (int i = 1 /* start from a read */; i < refs.size(); i++) {
306 |           Node nameNode = refs.get(i).getNode();
307 |           if (aliasCandidates.containsKey(nameNode)) {
308 |             AliasCandidate candidate = aliasCandidates.get(nameNode);
309 |             if (!staleVars.contains(candidate.alias) &&
310 |                 !isVarInlineForbidden(candidate.alias)) {
311 |               Reference aliasInit;
312 |               aliasInit = candidate.refInfo.getInitializingReference();
313 |               Node value = aliasInit.getAssignedValue();
314 |               Preconditions.checkNotNull(value);
315 |               inlineWellDefinedVariable(candidate.alias,

134 |

136 |       Collections.sort(worklist, new Comparator<GraphNode<N, E>>() {
137 |         @Override
138 |         public int compare(GraphNode<N, E> o1, GraphNode<N, E> o2) {
139 |           int result = graph.getWeight(o2.getValue())
140 |               - graph.getWeight(o1.getValue());
141 |           return result == 0 && tieBreaker != null ?
142 |               tieBreaker.compare(o1.getValue(), o2.getValue()) : result;
143 |         }

147 |       // a unique color if none of its neighbor has been assigned that color.

153 |           GraphNode<N, E> node = i.next();
154 |           if (subgraph.isIndependentOf(node.getValue())) {
155 |             subgraph.addNode(node.getValue());
156 |             node.setAnnotation(color);

===== M0652 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.GlobalNamespace.BuildGlobalNamespace.getValueType(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/GlobalNamespace.java
Original range: 508-530
Documentation:
/**
     * Gets the type of a value or simple expression.
     *
     * @param n An rvalue in an assignment or variable declaration (not null)
     * @return A {@link Name.Type}
     */
Method code:
508 |     Name.Type getValueType(Node n) {
509 |       switch (n.getType()) {
510 |         case Token.OBJECTLIT:
511 |           return Name.Type.OBJECTLIT;
512 |         case Token.FUNCTION:
513 |           return Name.Type.FUNCTION;
514 |         case Token.OR:
515 |           // Recurse on the second value. If the first value were an object
516 |           // literal or function, then the OR would be meaningless and the
517 |           // second value would be dead code. Assume that if the second value
518 |           // is an object literal or function, then the first value will also
519 |           // evaluate to one when it doesn't evaluate to false.
520 |           return getValueType(n.getLastChild());
521 |         case Token.HOOK:
522 |           // The same line of reasoning used for the OR case applies here.
523 |           Node second = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
524 |           Name.Type t = getValueType(second);
525 |           if (t != Name.Type.OTHER) return t;
526 |           Node third = second.getNext();
527 |           return getValueType(third);
528 |       }
529 |       return Name.Type.OTHER;
530 |     }

831 |           recordReference(

833 |         }

836 |         // the inheritance, so that the inherits() function itself does

861 |       // determine all enclosing dependency scopes because this callback should
862 |       // create a chain of references between them.

872 |

874 |       // can be an alias to global object.
875 |       // Here we add a alias to the general "global" object
876 |       // to act as a placeholder for the actual (unnamed) value.
877 |       if (maybeHiddenAlias(name, n)) {
878 |         recordAlias(name, WINDOW);
879 |       }
880 | 
881 |       // An externally referenceable name must always be defined, so we add a
882 |       // reference to it from the global scope (a.k.a. window).
883 |       if (nameInfo.isExternallyReferenceable) {
884 |         recordReference(WINDOW, name, RefType.REGULAR);
885 |         maybeRecordAlias(name, parent, referring, referringName);
886 |         return;
887 |       }
888 | 
889 |       // An assignment implies a reference from the enclosing dependency scope.
890 |       // For example, foo references bar in: function foo() {bar=5}.
891 |       if (NodeUtil.isVarOrSimpleAssignLhs(n, parent)) {
892 |         if (referring != null) {

908 |               RefType.INHERITANCE : RefType.REGULAR;
909 |           recordReference(referringName, name, depType);
910 |         }

913 |         // mean that the expression is a child of an function expression

Method code:
193 |   private void removeDeadExprStatementSafely(Node n) {
194 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
195 |     if (n.isEmpty() ||

198 |       return;

200 |

210 |         // blocks in TRYs
211 |         if (parent.isTry()) {
212 |           if (NodeUtil.isTryCatchNodeContainer(n)) {
213 |             return;
214 |           }
215 |         }
216 |         break;
217 | 
218 |       case Token.CATCH:
219 |         Node tryNode = parent.getParent();
220 |         NodeUtil.maybeAddFinally(tryNode);
221 |         break;
222 |     }
223 | 
224 | 
225 |     if (n.isVar() && !n.getFirstChild().hasChildren()) {
226 |       // Very Edge case, Consider this:
227 |       // File 1: {throw 1}
228 |       // File 2: {var x}
229 |       // The node var x is unreachable in the global scope.
230 |       // Before we remove the node, redeclareVarsInsideBranch
231 |       // would basically move var x to the beginning of File 2,
232 |       // which resulted in zero change in the AST but triggered
233 |       // reportCodeChange().
234 |       // Instead, we should just ignore dead variable declarations.
235 |       return;
236 |     }
237 | 
238 |     NodeUtil.redeclareVarsInsideBranch(n);
239 |     compiler.reportCodeChange();
240 |     if (logger.isLoggable(Level.FINE)) {
241 |       logger.fine("Removing " + n.toString());
242 |     }
243 |     NodeUtil.removeChild(n.getParent(), n);
244 |   }

/**
   * Determines whether we know enough about the given value to be able
   * to collapse it into subsequent expressions.
   *
   * For example, we can collapse booleans and variable names:
   * <code>
   * x = 3; y = x; // y = x = 3;
   * a = true; b = true; // b = a = true;
   * <code>
   * But we won't try to collapse complex expressions.
   *
   * @param value The value node.
   * @param isLValue Whether it's on the left-hand side of an expr.
   */
Method code:
76 |   private boolean isCollapsibleValue(Node value, boolean isLValue) {
77 |     switch (value.getType()) {
78 |       case Token.GETPROP:
79 |         // Do not collapse GETPROPs on arbitrary objects, because
80 |         // they may be implemented  setter functions, and oftentimes
81 |         // setter functions fail on native objects. This is ok for "THIS"
82 |         // objects, because we assume that they are non-native.
83 |         return !isLValue || value.getFirstChild().isThis();
84 | 
85 |       case Token.NAME:
86 |         return true;
87 | 
88 |       default:
89 |         return NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(value);
90 |     }
91 |   }

/**
   * Flattens all references to a collapsible property of a global name except
   * its initial definition.
   *
   * @param n A global property name (e.g. "a.b" or "a.b.c.d")
   * @param alias The flattened name (e.g. "a$b" or "a$b$c$d")
   */
Method code:
356 |   private void flattenReferencesTo(Name n, String alias) {
357 |     String originalName = n.getFullName();
358 |     for (Ref r : n.getRefs()) {
359 |       if (r == n.getDeclaration()) {
360 |         // Declarations are handled separately.
361 |         continue;
362 |       }
363 | 
364 |       Node rParent = r.node.getParent();
365 | 
366 |       // There are two cases when we shouldn't flatten a reference:
367 |       // 1) Object literal keys, because duplicate keys show up as refs.
368 |       // 2) References inside a complex assign. (a = x.y = 0). These are
369 |       //    called TWIN references, because they show up twice in the

379 |     // replaced with "a$b" in all occurrences of "a.b.c", "a.b.c.d", etc.
380 |     if (n.props != null) {
381 |       for (Name p : n.props) {

===== M0739 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Denormalize.maybeCollapseIntoForStatements(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Denormalize.java
Original range: 65-127
Documentation:
/**
   * Collapse VARs and EXPR_RESULT node into FOR loop initializers where
   * possible.
   */
Method code:
65 |   private void maybeCollapseIntoForStatements(Node n, Node parent) {
66 |     // Only SCRIPT, BLOCK, and LABELs can have FORs that can be collapsed into.
67 |     // LABELs are not supported here.
68 |     if (parent == null || !NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(parent)) {
69 |       return;
70 |     }
71 | 
72 |     // Is the current node something that can be in a for loop initializer?
73 |     if (!n.isExprResult() && !n.isVar()) {
74 |       return;
75 |     }
76 | 
77 |     // Is the next statement a valid FOR?
78 |     Node nextSibling = n.getNext();
79 |     if (nextSibling == null) {
80 |       return;
81 |     } else if (NodeUtil.isForIn(nextSibling)) {
82 |       Node forNode = nextSibling;
83 |       Node forVar = forNode.getFirstChild();
84 |       if (forVar.isName()
85 |           && n.isVar() && n.hasOneChild()) {
86 |         Node name = n.getFirstChild();
87 |         if (!name.hasChildren()
88 |             && forVar.getString().equals(name.getString())) {
89 |           // Ok, the names match, and the var declaration does not have an
90 |           // initializer. Move it into the loop.
91 |           parent.removeChild(n);
92 |           forNode.replaceChild(forVar, n);
93 |           compiler.reportCodeChange();
94 |         }
95 |       }
96 |     } else if (nextSibling.isFor()
97 |         && nextSibling.getFirstChild().isEmpty()) {
98 | 
99 |       // Does the current node contain an in operator?  If so, embedding
100 |       // the expression in a for loop can cause some Javascript parsers (such
101 |       // as the Playstation 3's browser based on Access's NetFront
102 |       // browser) to fail to parse the code.
103 |       // See bug 1778863 for details.
104 |       if (NodeUtil.containsType(n, Token.IN)) {
105 |         return;
106 |       }
107 | 
108 |       // Move the current node into the FOR loop initializer.
109 |       Node forNode = nextSibling;
110 |       Node oldInitializer = forNode.getFirstChild();
111 |       parent.removeChild(n);
112 | 
113 |       Node newInitializer;
114 |       if (n.isVar()) {
115 |         newInitializer = n;
116 |       } else {
117 |         // Extract the expression from EXPR_RESULT node.
118 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.hasOneChild());
119 |         newInitializer = n.getFirstChild();
120 |         n.removeChild(newInitializer);
121 |       }
122 | 
123 |       forNode.replaceChild(oldInitializer, newInitializer);
124 | 
125 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
126 |     }
127 |   }

===== M0749 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PureFunctionIdentifier.propagateSideEffects()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PureFunctionIdentifier.java
Original range: 252-302
Documentation:
/**
   * Propagate side effect information by building a graph based on
   * call site information stored in FunctionInformation and the
   * DefinitionProvider and then running GraphReachability to
   * determine the set of functions that have side effects.
   */
Method code:
252 |   private void propagateSideEffects() {
253 |     // Nodes are function declarations; Edges are function call sites.
254 |     DiGraph<FunctionInformation, Node> sideEffectGraph =
255 |         LinkedDirectedGraph.createWithoutAnnotations();
256 | 
257 |     // create graph nodes
258 |     for (FunctionInformation functionInfo : functionSideEffectMap.values()) {
259 |       sideEffectGraph.createNode(functionInfo);
260 |     }
261 | 
262 |     // add connections to called functions and side effect root.
263 |     for (FunctionInformation functionInfo : functionSideEffectMap.values()) {
264 |       if (!functionInfo.mayHaveSideEffects()) {
265 |         continue;
266 |       }
267 | 
268 |       for (Node callSite : functionInfo.getCallsInFunctionBody()) {
269 |         Node callee = callSite.getFirstChild();
270 |         Collection<Definition> defs =
271 |             getCallableDefinitions(definitionProvider, callee);
272 |         if (defs == null) {
273 |           // Definition set is not complete or eligible.  Possible
274 |           // causes include:
275 |           //  * "callee" is not of type NAME or GETPROP.
276 |           //  * One or more definitions are not functions.
277 |           //  * One or more definitions are complex.
278 |           //    (e.i. return value of a call that returns a function).
279 |           functionInfo.setTaintsUnknown();
280 |           break;
281 |         }
282 | 
283 |         for (Definition def : defs) {
284 |           Node defValue = def.getRValue();
285 |           FunctionInformation dep = functionSideEffectMap.get(defValue);
286 |           Preconditions.checkNotNull(dep);
287 |           sideEffectGraph.connect(dep, callSite, functionInfo);
288 |         }
289 |       }
290 |     }
291 | 
292 |     // Propagate side effect information to a fixed point.
293 |     FixedPointGraphTraversal.newTraversal(new SideEffectPropagationCallback())
294 |         .computeFixedPoint(sideEffectGraph);
295 |

/**
   * Determines if a function result might be used.  A result might be use if:
   * - Function must is exported.
   * - The definition is never accessed outside a function call context.
   */
Method code:
76 |   private boolean callResultsMaybeUsed(
77 |       SimpleDefinitionFinder defFinder, DefinitionSite definitionSite) {
78 | 
79 |     Definition definition = definitionSite.definition;
80 | 
81 |     // Assume non-function definitions results are used.
82 |     Node rValue = definition.getRValue();
83 |     if (rValue == null || !rValue.isFunction()) {
84 |       return true;
85 |     }
86 | 
87 |     // Be conservative, don't try to optimize any declaration that isn't as
88 |     // simple function declaration or assignment.
89 |     if (!SimpleDefinitionFinder.isSimpleFunctionDeclaration(rValue)) {
90 |       return true;
91 |     }
92 | 
93 |     if (!defFinder.canModifyDefinition(definition)) {
94 |       return true;
95 |     }
96 | 
97 |     Collection<UseSite> useSites = defFinder.getUseSites(definition);
98 |     for (UseSite site : useSites) {
99 |       // Assume indirect definitions references use the result
100 |       Node useNodeParent = site.node.getParent();
101 |       if (isCall(site)) {
102 |         Node callNode = useNodeParent;
103 |         Preconditions.checkState(callNode.isCall());
104 |         if (NodeUtil.isExpressionResultUsed(callNode)) {
105 |           return true;
106 |         }
107 |       } else {
108 |         // Allow a standalone name reference.
109 |         //     var a;
110 |         if (!useNodeParent.isVar()) {
111 |           return true;
112 |         }
113 |       }
114 | 
115 |       // TODO(johnlenz): Add specialization support.
116 |     }
117 | 
118 |     // No possible use of the definition result
119 |     return false;
120 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.tryFoldLiteralConstructor(Node)

Original range: 1358-1406
Documentation:
/**
   * Replaces a new Array or Object node with an object literal, unless the
   * call to Array or Object is to a local function with the same name.
   */
Method code:
1358 |   private Node tryFoldLiteralConstructor(Node n) {
1359 |     Preconditions.checkArgument(n.isCall()
1360 |         || n.isNew());
1361 | 
1362 |     Node constructorNameNode = n.getFirstChild();
1363 | 
1364 |     Node newLiteralNode = null;
1365 | 
1366 |     // We require the AST to be normalized to ensure that, say,
1367 |     // Object() really refers to the built-in Object constructor
1368 |     // and not a user-defined constructor with the same name.
1369 | 
1370 |     if (isASTNormalized() && Token.NAME == constructorNameNode.getType()) {
1371 | 
1372 |       String className = constructorNameNode.getString();
1373 | 
1374 |       if ("RegExp".equals(className)) {
1375 |         // "RegExp("boo", "g")" --> /boo/g
1376 |         return tryFoldRegularExpressionConstructor(n);
1377 |       } else {
1378 |         boolean constructorHasArgs = constructorNameNode.getNext() != null;
1379 | 
1380 |         if ("Object".equals(className) && !constructorHasArgs) {
1381 |           // "Object()" --> "{}"
1382 |           newLiteralNode = IR.objectlit();
1383 |         } else if ("Array".equals(className)) {
1384 |           // "Array(arg0, arg1, ...)" --> "[arg0, arg1, ...]"
1385 |           Node arg0 = constructorNameNode.getNext();
1386 |           FoldArrayAction action = isSafeToFoldArrayConstructor(arg0);
1387 | 
1388 |           if (action == FoldArrayAction.SAFE_TO_FOLD_WITH_ARGS ||
1389 |               action == FoldArrayAction.SAFE_TO_FOLD_WITHOUT_ARGS) {
1390 |             newLiteralNode = IR.arraylit();
1391 |             n.removeChildren();
1392 |             if (action == FoldArrayAction.SAFE_TO_FOLD_WITH_ARGS) {
1393 |               newLiteralNode.addChildrenToFront(arg0);
1394 |             }
1395 |           }
1396 |         }
1397 | 
1398 |         if (newLiteralNode != null) {
1399 |           n.getParent().replaceChild(n, newLiteralNode);
1400 |           reportCodeChange();
1401 |           return newLiteralNode;
1402 |         }
1403 |       }
1404 |     }
1405 |     return n;
1406 |   }

102 |       @Override
103 |       public int compare(Property p1, Property p2) {
104 | 
105 |         /**
106 |          * First a frequently used names would always be picked first.
107 |          */
108 |         if (p1.numOccurrences != p2.numOccurrences) {
109 |           return p2.numOccurrences - p1.numOccurrences;

123 |          */

   * for more on Basic Latin.

   * @param s The string to be checked for ASCII-goodness.
   *
   * @return True if all characters in the string are in Basic Latin set.
   */

/**
     * Checks if the function matches the pattern:
     *   function(<value>, <rest>) {this.<name> = <value>}
     * and returns <name> if a match is found.
     *
     * @return STRING node that is the rhs of a this property get; or null.
     */

===== M0820 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CheckSideEffects.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CheckSideEffects.java
Original range: 83-166
Documentation:

Method code:
83 |   @Override
84 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
85 |     // VOID nodes appear when there are extra semicolons at the BLOCK level.
86 |     // I've been unable to think of any cases where this indicates a bug,
87 |     // and apparently some people like keeping these semicolons around,
88 |     // so we'll allow it.
89 |     if (n.isEmpty() ||
90 |         n.isComma()) {
91 |       return;
92 |     }
93 | 
94 |     if (parent == null) {
95 |       return;
96 |     }
97 | 
98 |     int pt = parent.getType();
99 |     if (pt == Token.COMMA) {
100 |       Node gramps = parent.getParent();
101 |       if (gramps.isCall() &&
102 |           parent == gramps.getFirstChild()) {
103 |         // Semantically, a direct call to eval is different from an indirect
104 |         // call to an eval. See Ecma-262 S15.1.2.1. So it's ok for the first
105 |         // expression to a comma to be a no-op if it's used to indirect
106 |         // an eval.
107 |         if (n == parent.getFirstChild() &&
108 |             parent.getChildCount() == 2 &&
109 |             n.getNext().isName() &&
110 |             "eval".equals(n.getNext().getString())) {
111 |           return;
112 |         }
113 |       }
114 | 
115 |       if (n == parent.getLastChild()) {
116 |         for (Node an : parent.getAncestors()) {
117 |           int ancestorType = an.getType();
118 |           if (ancestorType == Token.COMMA)
119 |             continue;
120 |           if (ancestorType != Token.EXPR_RESULT &&
121 |               ancestorType != Token.BLOCK)
122 |             return;
123 |           else
124 |             break;
125 |         }
126 |       }
127 |     } else if (pt != Token.EXPR_RESULT && pt != Token.BLOCK) {
128 |       if (pt == Token.FOR && parent.getChildCount() == 4 &&
129 |           (n == parent.getFirstChild() ||
130 |            n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext())) {
131 |         // Fall through and look for warnings for the 1st and 3rd child
132 |         // of a for.
133 |       } else {
134 |         return;  // it might be ok to not have a side-effect
135 |       }
136 |     }
137 | 
138 |     boolean isSimpleOp = NodeUtil.isSimpleOperatorType(n.getType());
139 |     if (isSimpleOp ||
140 |         !NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(n, t.getCompiler())) {
141 |       if (n.isQualifiedName() && n.getJSDocInfo() != null) {
142 |         // This no-op statement was there so that JSDoc information could
143 |         // be attached to the name. This check should not complain about it.
144 |         return;
145 |       } else if (n.isExprResult()) {
146 |         // we already reported the problem when we visited the child.
147 |         return;
148 |       }
149 | 
150 |       String msg = "This code lacks side-effects. Is there a bug?";
151 |       if (n.isString()) {
152 |         msg = "Is there a missing '+' on the previous line?";
153 |       } else if (isSimpleOp) {
154 |         msg = "The result of the '" + Token.name(n.getType()).toLowerCase() +
155 |             "' operator is not being used.";
156 |       }
157 | 
158 |       t.getCompiler().report(
159 |           t.makeError(n, level, USELESS_CODE_ERROR, msg));
160 |       // TODO(johnlenz): determine if it is necessary to
161 |       // try to protect side-effect free statements as well.
162 |       if (!NodeUtil.isStatement(n)) {
163 |         problemNodes.add(n);
164 |       }
165 |     }
166 |   }

===== M0833 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NameAnalyzer.getRhsSubexpressions(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NameAnalyzer.java
Original range: 1764-1801
Documentation:
/**
   * Extract a list of subexpressions that act as right hand sides.
   */
Method code:
1764 |   private List<Node> getRhsSubexpressions(Node n) {
1765 |     switch (n.getType()) {
1766 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
1767 |         // process body
1768 |         return getRhsSubexpressions(n.getFirstChild());
1769 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
1770 |         // function nodes have no rhs
1771 |         return Collections.emptyList();
1772 |       case Token.NAME:
1773 |         {
1774 |           // parent is a var node.  rhs is first child
1775 |           Node rhs = n.getFirstChild();
1776 |           if (rhs != null) {
1777 |             return Lists.newArrayList(rhs);
1778 |           } else {
1779 |             return Collections.emptyList();
1780 |           }
1781 |         }
1782 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
1783 |         {
1784 |           // add lhs and rhs expressions - lhs may be a complex expression
1785 |           Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
1786 |           Node rhs = lhs.getNext();
1787 |           return Lists.newArrayList(lhs, rhs);
1788 |         }
1789 |       case Token.VAR:
1790 |         {
1791 |           // recurse on all children
1792 |           List<Node> nodes = Lists.newArrayList();
1793 |           for (Node child : n.children()) {
1794 |             nodes.addAll(getRhsSubexpressions(child));
1795 |           }
1796 |           return nodes;
1797 |         }
1798 |       default:
1799 |         throw new IllegalArgumentException("AstChangeProxy::getRhs " + n);
1800 |     }
1801 |   }

===== M0848 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeRemoveDeadCode.trySimplifyUnusedResult(Node,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeRemoveDeadCode.java
Original range: 170-279
Documentation:
/**
   * General cascading unused operation node removal.
   * @param n The root of the expression to simplify.
   * @param removeUnused If true, the node is removed from the AST if
   *     it is not useful, otherwise it replaced with an EMPTY node.
   * @return The replacement node, or null if the node was is not useful.
   */
Method code:
170 |   private Node trySimplifyUnusedResult(Node n, boolean removeUnused) {
171 |     Node result = n;
172 | 
173 |     // Simplify the results of conditional expressions
174 |     switch (n.getType()) {
175 |       case Token.HOOK:
176 |         Node trueNode = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild().getNext());
177 |         Node falseNode = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getLastChild());
178 |         // If one or more of the conditional children were removed,
179 |         // transform the HOOK to an equivalent operation:
180 |         //    x() ? foo() : 1 --> x() && foo()
181 |         //    x() ? 1 : foo() --> x() || foo()
182 |         //    x() ? 1 : 1 --> x()
183 |         //    x ? 1 : 1 --> null
184 |         if (trueNode == null && falseNode != null) {
185 |           n.setType(Token.OR);
186 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 2);
187 |         } else if (trueNode != null && falseNode == null) {
188 |           n.setType(Token.AND);
189 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 2);
190 |         } else if (trueNode == null && falseNode == null) {
191 |           result = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild());
192 |         } else {
193 |           // The structure didn't change.
194 |           result = n;
195 |         }
196 |         break;
197 |       case Token.AND:
198 |       case Token.OR:
199 |         // Try to remove the second operand from a AND or OR operations:
200 |         //    x() || f --> x()
201 |         //    x() && f --> x()
202 |         Node conditionalResultNode = trySimplifyUnusedResult(
203 |             n.getLastChild());
204 |         if (conditionalResultNode == null) {
205 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.hasOneChild());
206 |           // The conditionally executed code was removed, so
207 |           // replace the AND/OR with its LHS or remove it if it isn't useful.
208 |           result = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild());
209 |         }
210 |         break;
211 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
212 |         // A function expression isn't useful if it isn't used, remove it and
213 |         // don't bother to look at its children.
214 |         result = null;
215 |         break;
216 |       case Token.COMMA:
217 |         // We rewrite other operations as COMMA expressions (which will later
218 |         // get split into individual EXPR_RESULT statement, if possible), so
219 |         // we special case COMMA (we don't want to rewrite COMMAs as new COMMAs
220 |         // nodes.
221 |         Node left = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild());
222 |         Node right = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getLastChild());
223 |         if (left == null && right == null) {
224 |           result = null;
225 |         } else if (left == null) {
226 |           result = right;
227 |         } else if (right == null){
228 |           result = left;
229 |         } else {
230 |           // The structure didn't change.
231 |           result = n;
232 |         }
233 |         break;
234 |       default:
235 |         if (!NodeUtil.nodeTypeMayHaveSideEffects(n)) {
236 |           // This is the meat of this function. The node itself doesn't generate
237 |           // any side-effects but preserve any side-effects in the children.
238 |           Node resultList = null;
239 |           for (Node next, c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = next) {
240 |             next = c.getNext();
241 |             c = trySimplifyUnusedResult(c);
242 |             if (c != null) {
243 |               c.detachFromParent();
244 |               if (resultList == null)  {
245 |                 // The first side-effect can be used stand-alone.
246 |                 resultList = c;
247 |               } else {
248 |                 // Leave the side-effects in-place, simplifying it to a COMMA
249 |                 // expression.
250 |                 resultList = IR.comma(resultList, c).srcref(c);
251 |               }
252 |             }
253 |           }
254 |           result = resultList;
255 |         }
256 |     }
257 | 
258 |     // Fix up the AST, replace or remove the an unused node (if requested).
259 |     if (n != result) {
260 |       Node parent = n.getParent();
261 |       if (result == null) {
262 |         if (removeUnused) {
263 |           parent.removeChild(n);
264 |         } else {
265 |           result = IR.empty().srcref(n);
266 |           parent.replaceChild(n, result);
267 |         }
268 |       } else {
269 |         // A new COMMA expression may not have an existing parent.
270 |         if (result.getParent() != null) {
271 |           result.detachFromParent();
272 |         }
273 |         n.getParent().replaceChild(n, result);
274 |       }
275 |       reportCodeChange();
276 |     }
277 | 
278 |     return result;
279 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.LiveVariablesAnalysis.computeGenKill(Node,BitSet,BitSet,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/LiveVariablesAnalysis.java
Original range: 183-272
Documentation:
/**
   * Computes the GEN and KILL set.
   *
   * @param n Root node.
   * @param gen Local variables that are live because of the instruction at
   *        {@code n} will be added to this set.
   * @param kill Local variables that are killed because of the instruction at
   *        {@code n} will be added to this set.
   * @param conditional {@code true} if any assignments encountered are
   *        conditionally executed. These assignments might not kill a variable.
   */
Method code:
183 |   private void computeGenKill(Node n, BitSet gen, BitSet kill,
184 |       boolean conditional) {
185 | 
186 |     switch (n.getType()) {
187 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
188 |       case Token.BLOCK:
189 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
190 |         return;
191 | 
192 |       case Token.WHILE:
193 |       case Token.DO:
194 |       case Token.IF:
195 |         computeGenKill(NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), gen, kill,
196 |             conditional);
197 |         return;
198 | 
199 |       case Token.FOR:
200 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(n)) {
201 |           computeGenKill(NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), gen, kill,
202 |               conditional);
203 |         } else {
204 |           // for(x in y) {...}
205 |           Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
206 |           Node rhs = lhs.getNext();
207 |           if (lhs.isVar()) {
208 |             // for(var x in y) {...}
209 |             lhs = lhs.getLastChild();
210 |           }
211 |           if (lhs.isName()) {
212 |             addToSetIfLocal(lhs, kill);
213 |             addToSetIfLocal(lhs, gen);
214 |           } else {
215 |             computeGenKill(lhs, gen, kill, conditional);
216 |           }
217 |           computeGenKill(rhs, gen, kill, conditional);
218 |         }
219 |         return;
220 | 
221 |       case Token.VAR:
222 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
223 |           if (c.hasChildren()) {
224 |             computeGenKill(c.getFirstChild(), gen, kill, conditional);
225 |             if (!conditional) {
226 |               addToSetIfLocal(c, kill);
227 |             }
228 |           }
229 |         }
230 |         return;
231 | 
232 |       case Token.AND:
233 |       case Token.OR:
234 |         computeGenKill(n.getFirstChild(), gen, kill, conditional);
235 |         // May short circuit.
236 |         computeGenKill(n.getLastChild(), gen, kill, true);
237 |         return;
238 | 
239 |       case Token.HOOK:
240 |         computeGenKill(n.getFirstChild(), gen, kill, conditional);
241 |         // Assume both sides are conditional.
242 |         computeGenKill(n.getFirstChild().getNext(), gen, kill, true);
243 |         computeGenKill(n.getLastChild(), gen, kill, true);
244 |         return;
245 | 
246 |       case Token.NAME:
247 |         if (isArgumentsName(n)) {
248 |           markAllParametersEscaped();
249 |         } else {
250 |           addToSetIfLocal(n, gen);
251 |         }
252 |         return;
253 | 
254 |       default:
255 |         if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n) && n.getFirstChild().isName()) {
256 |           Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
257 |           if (!conditional) {
258 |             addToSetIfLocal(lhs, kill);
259 |           }
260 |           if (!n.isAssign()) {
261 |             // assignments such as a += 1 reads a.
262 |             addToSetIfLocal(lhs, gen);
263 |           }
264 |           computeGenKill(lhs.getNext(), gen, kill, conditional);
265 |         } else {
266 |           for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
267 |             computeGenKill(c, gen, kill, conditional);
268 |           }
269 |         }
270 |         return;
271 |     }
272 |   }

===== M0861 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.evaluatesToLocalValue(Node,Predicate<Node>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 2893-2957
Documentation:
/**
   * @param locals A predicate to apply to unknown local values.
   * @return Whether the node is known to be a value that is not a reference
   *     outside the expression scope.
   */
Method code:
2893 |   static boolean evaluatesToLocalValue(Node value, Predicate<Node> locals) {
2894 |     switch (value.getType()) {
2895 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
2896 |         // A result that is aliased by a non-local name, is the effectively the
2897 |         // same as returning a non-local name, but this doesn't matter if the
2898 |         // value is immutable.
2899 |         return NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(value.getLastChild())
2900 |             || (locals.apply(value)
2901 |                 && evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getLastChild(), locals));
2902 |       case Token.COMMA:
2903 |         return evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getLastChild(), locals);
2904 |       case Token.AND:
2905 |       case Token.OR:
2906 |         return evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getFirstChild(), locals)
2907 |            && evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getLastChild(), locals);
2908 |       case Token.HOOK:
2909 |         return evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getFirstChild().getNext(), locals)
2910 |            && evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getLastChild(), locals);
2911 |       case Token.INC:
2912 |       case Token.DEC:
2913 |         if (value.getBooleanProp(Node.INCRDECR_PROP)) {
2914 |           return evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getFirstChild(), locals);
2915 |         } else {
2916 |           return true;
2917 |         }
2918 |       case Token.THIS:
2919 |         return locals.apply(value);
2920 |       case Token.NAME:
2921 |         return isImmutableValue(value) || locals.apply(value);
2922 |       case Token.GETELEM:
2923 |       case Token.GETPROP:
2924 |         // There is no information about the locality of object properties.
2925 |         return locals.apply(value);
2926 |       case Token.CALL:
2927 |         return callHasLocalResult(value)
2928 |             || isToStringMethodCall(value)
2929 |             || locals.apply(value);
2930 |       case Token.NEW:
2931 |         return newHasLocalResult(value)
2932 |                || locals.apply(value);
2933 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
2934 |       case Token.REGEXP:
2935 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
2936 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
2937 |         // Literals objects with non-literal children are allowed.
2938 |         return true;
2939 |       case Token.DELPROP:
2940 |       case Token.IN:
2941 |         // TODO(johnlenz): should IN operator be included in #isSimpleOperator?
2942 |         return true;
2943 |       default:
2944 |         // Other op force a local value:
2945 |         //  x = '' + g (x is now an local string)
2946 |         //  x -= g (x is now an local number)
2947 |         if (isAssignmentOp(value)
2948 |             || isSimpleOperator(value)
2949 |             || isImmutableValue(value)) {
2950 |           return true;
2951 |         }
2952 | 
2953 |         throw new IllegalStateException(
2954 |             "Unexpected expression node" + value +
2955 |             "\n parent:" + value.getParent());
2956 |     }
2957 |   }

/**
   * Computes the new flow state at a given node's entry by merging the
   * output (input) lattice of the node's predecessor (successor).
   *
   * @param node Node to compute new join.

Method code:
284 |   protected void joinInputs(DiGraphNode<N, Branch> node) {
285 |     FlowState<L> state = node.getAnnotation();
286 |     if (isForward()) {
287 |       if (cfg.getEntry() == node) {
288 |         state.setIn(createEntryLattice());
289 |       } else {
290 |         List<DiGraphNode<N, Branch>> inNodes = cfg.getDirectedPredNodes(node);
291 |         if (inNodes.size() == 1) {
292 |           FlowState<L> inNodeState = inNodes.get(0).getAnnotation();
293 |           state.setIn(inNodeState.getOut());
294 |         } else if (inNodes.size() > 1) {
295 |           List<L> values = new ArrayList<L>(inNodes.size());
296 |           for (DiGraphNode<N, Branch> currentNode : inNodes) {
297 |             FlowState<L> currentNodeState = currentNode.getAnnotation();
298 |             values.add(currentNodeState.getOut());
299 |           }
300 |           state.setIn(joinOp.apply(values));

307 |         if (inNode == cfg.getImplicitReturn()) {
308 |           state.setOut(createEntryLattice());
309 |         } else {
310 |           FlowState<L> inNodeState = inNode.getAnnotation();
311 |           state.setOut(inNodeState.getIn());
312 |         }
313 |       } else if (inNodes.size() > 1) {
314 |         List<L> values = new ArrayList<L>(inNodes.size());
315 |         for (DiGraphNode<N, Branch> currentNode : inNodes) {
316 |           FlowState<L> currentNodeState = currentNode.getAnnotation();

===== M0911 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(Node,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 585-622
Documentation:
/**
   * Returns true if this is a literal value. We define a literal value
   * as any node that evaluates to the same thing regardless of when or
   * where it is evaluated. So /xyz/ and [3, 5] are literals, but
   * the name a is not.
   *
   * Function literals do not meet this definition, because they
   * lexically capture variables. For example, if you have
   * <code>
   * function() { return a; }
   * </code>
   * If it is evaluated in a different scope, then it
   * captures a different variable. Even if the function did not read
   * any captured vairables directly, it would still fail this definition,
   * because it affects the lifecycle of variables in the enclosing scope.
   *
   * However, a function literal with respect to a particular scope is
   * a literal.
   *
   * @param includeFunctions If true, all function expressions will be
   *     treated as literals.
   */
Method code:
585 |   static boolean isLiteralValue(Node n, boolean includeFunctions) {
586 |     switch (n.getType()) {
587 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
588 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild(); child != null;
589 |              child = child.getNext()) {
590 |           if ((!child.isEmpty()) && !isLiteralValue(child, includeFunctions)) {
591 |             return false;
592 |           }
593 |         }
594 |         return true;
595 | 
596 |       case Token.REGEXP:
597 |         // Return true only if all children are const.
598 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild(); child != null;
599 |              child = child.getNext()) {
600 |           if (!isLiteralValue(child, includeFunctions)) {
601 |             return false;
602 |           }
603 |         }
604 |         return true;
605 | 
606 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
607 |         // Return true only if all values are const.
608 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild(); child != null;
609 |              child = child.getNext()) {
610 |           if (!isLiteralValue(child.getFirstChild(), includeFunctions)) {
611 |             return false;
612 |           }
613 |         }
614 |         return true;
615 | 
616 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
617 |         return includeFunctions && !NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(n);
618 | 
619 |       default:
620 |         return isImmutableValue(n);
621 |     }
622 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.MinimizeExitPoints.tryMinimizeExits(Node,int,String)

/**
   * Attempts to minimize the number of explicit exit points in a control
   * structure to take advantage of the implied exit at the end of the
   * structure.  This is accomplished by removing redundant statements, and
   * moving statements following a qualifying IF node into that node.
   * For example:
   *
   * function () {
   *   if (x) return;
   *   else blah();
   *   foo();
   * }
   *
   * becomes:
   *
   * function () {
   *  if (x) ;
   *  else {
   *    blah();
   *    foo();
   *  }
   *
   * @param n The execution node of a parent to inspect.
   * @param exitType The type of exit to look for.
   * @param labelName If parent is a label the name of the label to look for,
   *   null otherwise.
   * @nullable labelName non-null only for breaks within labels.
   */
Method code:
114 |   void tryMinimizeExits(Node n, int exitType, String labelName) {
115 | 
116 |     // Just an 'exit'.
117 |     if (matchingExitNode(n, exitType, labelName)) {
118 |       NodeUtil.removeChild(n.getParent(), n);
119 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
120 |       return;
121 |     }
122 | 
123 |     // Just an 'if'.
124 |     if (n.isIf()) {
125 |       Node ifBlock = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
126 |       tryMinimizeExits(ifBlock, exitType, labelName);
127 |       Node elseBlock = ifBlock.getNext();
128 |       if (elseBlock != null) {
129 |         tryMinimizeExits(elseBlock, exitType, labelName);
130 |       }
131 |       return;
132 |     }
133 | 
134 |     // Just a 'try/catch/finally'.
135 |     if (n.isTry()) {
136 |       Node tryBlock = n.getFirstChild();
137 |       tryMinimizeExits(tryBlock, exitType, labelName);
138 |       Node allCatchNodes = NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(n);
139 |       if (NodeUtil.hasCatchHandler(allCatchNodes)) {
140 |         Preconditions.checkState(allCatchNodes.hasOneChild());
141 |         Node catchNode = allCatchNodes.getFirstChild();
142 |         Node catchCodeBlock = catchNode.getLastChild();
143 |         tryMinimizeExits(catchCodeBlock, exitType, labelName);
144 |       }
145 |       if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(n)) {
146 |         Node finallyBlock = n.getLastChild();
147 |         tryMinimizeExits(finallyBlock, exitType, labelName);
148 |       }
149 |     }
150 | 
151 |     // Just a 'label'.
152 |     if (n.isLabel()) {
153 |       Node labelBlock = n.getLastChild();
154 |       tryMinimizeExits(labelBlock, exitType, labelName);
155 |     }
156 | 
157 |     // TODO(johnlenz): The last case of SWITCH statement?
158 | 
159 |     // The rest assumes a block with at least one child, bail on anything else.
160 |     if (!n.isBlock() || n.getLastChild() == null) {
161 |       return;
162 |     }
163 | 
164 |     // Multiple if-exits can be converted in a single pass.
165 |     // Convert "if (blah) break;  if (blah2) break; other_stmt;" to
166 |     // become "if (blah); else { if (blah2); else { other_stmt; } }"
167 |     // which will get converted to "if (!blah && !blah2) { other_stmt; }".
168 |     for (Node c : n.children()) {
169 | 
170 |       // An 'if' block to process below.
171 |       if (c.isIf()) {
172 |         Node ifTree = c;
173 |         Node trueBlock, falseBlock;
174 | 
175 |         // First, the true condition block.
176 |         trueBlock = ifTree.getFirstChild().getNext();
177 |         falseBlock = trueBlock.getNext();
178 |         tryMinimizeIfBlockExits(trueBlock, falseBlock,
179 |             ifTree, exitType, labelName);
180 | 
181 |         // Now the else block.
182 |         // The if blocks may have changed, get them again.
183 |         trueBlock = ifTree.getFirstChild().getNext();
184 |         falseBlock = trueBlock.getNext();
185 |         if (falseBlock != null) {
186 |           tryMinimizeIfBlockExits(falseBlock, trueBlock,
187 |               ifTree, exitType, labelName);
188 |         }
189 |       }
190 | 
191 |       if (c == n.getLastChild()) {
192 |         break;
193 |       }
194 |     }
195 | 
196 |     // Now try to minimize the exits of the last child, if it is removed
197 |     // look at what has become the last child.
198 |     for (Node c = n.getLastChild(); c != null; c = n.getLastChild()) {
199 |       tryMinimizeExits(c, exitType, labelName);
200 |       // If the node is still the last child, we are done.
201 |       if (c == n.getLastChild()) {
202 |         break;
203 |       }
204 |     }
205 |   }

285 |       // TODO(user): Side-effect is ok sometimes. As long as there are no
286 |       // side-effect function down all paths to the use. Once we have all the
287 |       // side-effect analysis tool.
288 |       if (NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(def.getLastChild())) {
289 |         return false;
290 |       }
291 | 
292 |       // TODO(user): We could inline all the uses if the expression is short.
293 | 
294 |       // Finally we have to make sure that there are no more than one use
295 |       // in the program and in the CFG node. Even when it is semantically
296 |       // correctly inlining twice increases code size.
297 |       if (numUseWithinUseCfgNode != 1) {
298 |         return false;
299 |       }
300 | 
301 |       // Make sure that the name is not within a loop
302 |       if (NodeUtil.isWithinLoop(use)) {
303 |         return false;
304 |       }
305 | 
306 | 
307 |       Collection<Node> uses = reachingUses.getUses(varName, defCfgNode);
308 | 
309 |       if (uses.size() != 1) {
310 |         return false;
311 |       }
312 | 
313 |       // We give up inling stuff with R-Value that has GETPROP, GETELEM,
314 |       // or anything that creates a new object.
315 |       // Example:
316 |       // var x = a.b.c; j.c = 1; print(x);
317 |       // Inlining print(a.b.c) is not safe consider j and be alias to a.b.
318 |       // TODO(user): We could get more accuracy by looking more in-detail
319 |       // what j is and what x is trying to into to.
320 |       if (NodeUtil.has(def.getLastChild(),
321 |           new Predicate<Node>() {
322 |               @Override
323 |               public boolean apply(Node input) {
324 |                 switch (input.getType()) {
325 |                   case Token.GETELEM:
326 |                   case Token.GETPROP:
327 |                   case Token.ARRAYLIT:
328 |                   case Token.OBJECTLIT:
329 |                   case Token.REGEXP:
330 |                   case Token.NEW:
331 |                     return true;
332 |                 }
333 |                 return false;
334 |               }
335 |           },
336 |           new Predicate<Node>() {
337 |               @Override
338 |               public boolean apply(Node input) {
339 |                 // Recurse if the node is not a function.
340 |                 return !input.isFunction();
341 |               }
342 |           })) {
343 |         return false;
344 |       }
345 | 
346 |       // We can skip the side effect check along the paths of two nodes if
347 |       // they are just next to each other.
348 |       if (NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(defCfgNode.getParent()) &&
349 |           defCfgNode.getNext() != useCfgNode) {
350 |         // Similar side effect check as above but this time the side effect is
351 |         // else where along the path.
352 |         // x = readProp(b); while(modifyProp(b)) {}; print(x);
353 |         CheckPathsBetweenNodes<Node, ControlFlowGraph.Branch>
354 |           pathCheck = new CheckPathsBetweenNodes<Node, ControlFlowGraph.Branch>(
355 |                  cfg,
356 |                  cfg.getDirectedGraphNode(defCfgNode),
357 |                  cfg.getDirectedGraphNode(useCfgNode),
358 |                  SIDE_EFFECT_PREDICATE,
359 |                  Predicates.
360 |                      <DiGraphEdge<Node, ControlFlowGraph.Branch>>alwaysTrue(),
361 |                  false);
362 |         if (pathCheck.somePathsSatisfyPredicate()) {
363 |           return false;
364 |         }
365 |       }
366 | 
367 |       return true;
368 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.removeChild(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 1748-1801
Documentation:
/** Safely remove children while maintaining a valid node structure. */
Method code:
1748 |   static void removeChild(Node parent, Node node) {
1749 |     if (isTryFinallyNode(parent, node)) {
1750 |       if (NodeUtil.hasCatchHandler(getCatchBlock(parent))) {
1751 |         // A finally can only be removed if there is a catch.
1752 |         parent.removeChild(node);
1753 |       } else {
1754 |         // Otherwise only its children can be removed.
1755 |         node.detachChildren();
1756 |       }
1757 |     } else if (node.isCatch()) {
1758 |       // The CATCH can can only be removed if there is a finally clause.
1759 |       Node tryNode = node.getParent().getParent();
1760 |       Preconditions.checkState(NodeUtil.hasFinally(tryNode));
1761 |       node.detachFromParent();
1762 |     } else if (isTryCatchNodeContainer(node)) {
1763 |       // The container node itself can't be removed, but the contained CATCH
1764 |       // can if there is a 'finally' clause
1765 |       Node tryNode = node.getParent();
1766 |       Preconditions.checkState(NodeUtil.hasFinally(tryNode));
1767 |       node.detachChildren();
1768 |     } else if (node.isBlock()) {
1769 |       // Simply empty the block.  This maintains source location and
1770 |       // "synthetic"-ness.
1771 |       node.detachChildren();
1772 |     } else if (isStatementBlock(parent)
1773 |         || isSwitchCase(node)) {
1774 |       // A statement in a block can simply be removed.
1775 |       parent.removeChild(node);
1776 |     } else if (parent.isVar()) {
1777 |       if (parent.hasMoreThanOneChild()) {
1778 |         parent.removeChild(node);
1779 |       } else {
1780 |         // Remove the node from the parent, so it can be reused.
1781 |         parent.removeChild(node);
1782 |         // This would leave an empty VAR, remove the VAR itself.
1783 |         removeChild(parent.getParent(), parent);
1784 |       }
1785 |     } else if (parent.isLabel()
1786 |         && node == parent.getLastChild()) {
1787 |       // Remove the node from the parent, so it can be reused.
1788 |       parent.removeChild(node);
1789 |       // A LABEL without children can not be referred to, remove it.
1790 |       removeChild(parent.getParent(), parent);
1791 |     } else if (parent.isFor()
1792 |         && parent.getChildCount() == 4) {
1793 |       // Only Token.FOR can have an Token.EMPTY other control structure
1794 |       // need something for the condition. Others need to be replaced
1795 |       // or the structure removed.
1796 |       parent.replaceChild(node, IR.empty());
1797 |     } else {
1798 |       throw new IllegalStateException("Invalid attempt to remove node: " +
1799 |           node.toString() + " of "+ parent.toString());
1800 |     }
1801 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.JsDocInfoParser.parseTypeExpression(JsDocToken)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/parsing/JsDocInfoParser.java
Original range: 1659-1700
Documentation:
/**
   * TypeExpression := BasicTypeExpression
   *     | '?' BasicTypeExpression
   *     | '!' BasicTypeExpression
   *     | BasicTypeExpression '?'
   *     | BasicTypeExpression '!'
   *     | '?'
   */
Method code:
1659 |   private Node parseTypeExpression(JsDocToken token) {
1660 |     if (token == JsDocToken.QMARK) {
1661 |       // A QMARK could mean that a type is nullable, or that it's unknown.
1662 |       // We use look-ahead 1 to determine whether it's unknown. Otherwise,
1663 |       // we assume it means nullable. There are 5 cases:
1664 |       // {?} - right curly
1665 |       // {?=} - equals
1666 |       // {function(?, number)} - comma
1667 |       // {function(number, ?)} - right paren
1668 |       // {function(number, ...[?])} - right bracket
1669 |       // {function(): ?|number} - pipe
1670 |       // I'm not a big fan of using look-ahead for this, but it makes
1671 |       // the type language a lot nicer.
1672 |       token = next();
1673 |       if (token == JsDocToken.COMMA ||
1674 |           token == JsDocToken.EQUALS ||
1675 |           token == JsDocToken.RB ||
1676 |           token == JsDocToken.RC ||
1677 |           token == JsDocToken.RP ||
1678 |           token == JsDocToken.PIPE) {
1679 |         restoreLookAhead(token);
1680 |         return newNode(Token.QMARK);
1681 |       }
1682 | 
1683 |       return wrapNode(Token.QMARK, parseBasicTypeExpression(token));
1684 |     } else if (token == JsDocToken.BANG) {
1685 |       return wrapNode(Token.BANG, parseBasicTypeExpression(next()));
1686 |     } else {
1687 |       Node basicTypeExpr = parseBasicTypeExpression(token);
1688 |       if (basicTypeExpr != null) {
1689 |         if (match(JsDocToken.QMARK)) {
1690 |           next();
1691 |           return wrapNode(Token.QMARK, basicTypeExpr);
1692 |         } else if (match(JsDocToken.BANG)) {
1693 |           next();
1694 |           return wrapNode(Token.BANG, basicTypeExpr);
1695 |         }
1696 |       }
1697 | 
1698 |       return basicTypeExpr;
1699 |     }
1700 |   }

===== M0982 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ShadowVariables.DoShadowVariables.enterScope(NodeTraversal)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ShadowVariables.java
Original range: 175-226
Documentation:

Method code:
175 |     @Override
176 |     public void enterScope(NodeTraversal t) {
177 |       Scope s = t.getScope();
178 |       if (!s.isLocal()) {
179 |         return;
180 |       }
181 | 
182 |       // Since we don't shadow global, there is nothing to be done in the
183 |       // first immediate local scope as well.
184 |       if (s.getParent().isGlobal()) {
185 |         return;
186 |       }
187 | 
188 |       for (Iterator<Var> vars = s.getVars(); vars.hasNext();) {
189 |         Var var = vars.next();
190 | 
191 |         // Don't shadow variables that is bleed-out to fix an IE bug.
192 |         if (var.isBleedingFunction()) {
193 |           continue;
194 |         }
195 | 
196 |         // Don't shadow an exported local.
197 |         if (compiler.getCodingConvention().isExported(var.name, s.isLocal())) {
198 |           continue;
199 |         }
200 | 
201 |         // Try to look for the best shadow for the current candidate.
202 |         Assignment bestShadow = findBestShadow(s, var);
203 |         if (bestShadow == null) {
204 |           continue;
205 |         }
206 | 
207 |         // The name assignment being shadowed.
208 |         Assignment localAssignment = assignments.get(var.getName());
209 | 
210 |         // Only shadow if this increases the number of occurrences of the
211 |         // shadowed variable.
212 |         if (bestShadow.count < localAssignment.count) {
213 |           continue; // Hope the next local variable would have a smaller count.
214 |         }
215 | 
216 |         doShadow(localAssignment, bestShadow, var);
217 | 
218 |         if (oldPseudoNameMap != null) {
219 |           String targetPseudoName =
220 |             oldPseudoNameMap.get(s.getVar(bestShadow.oldName).nameNode);
221 |           for (Node use : varToNameUsage.get(var)) {
222 |             deltaPseudoNameMap.put(use, targetPseudoName);
223 |           }
224 |         }
225 |       }
226 |     }

===== M0983 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CollapseProperties.updateObjLitOrFunctionDeclaration(Name,String,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CollapseProperties.java
Original range: 622-649
Documentation:
/**
   * Updates the first initialization (a.k.a "declaration") of a global name.
   * This involves flattening the global name (if it's not just a global
   * variable name already), collapsing object literal keys into global
   * variables, declaring stub global variables for properties added later
   * in a local scope.
   *
   * It may seem odd that this function also takes care of declaring stubs
   * for direct children. The ultimate goal of this function is to eliminate
   * the global name entirely (when possible), so that "middlemen" namespaces
   * disappear, and to do that we need to make sure that all the direct children
   * will be collapsed as well.
   *
   * @param n An object representing a global name (e.g. "a", "a.b.c")
   * @param alias The flattened name for {@code n} (e.g. "a", "a$b$c")
   * @param canCollapseChildNames Whether it's possible to collapse children of
   *     this name. (This is mostly passed for convenience; it's equivalent to
   *     n.canCollapseChildNames()).
   */
Method code:
622 |   private void updateObjLitOrFunctionDeclaration(
623 |       Name n, String alias, boolean canCollapseChildNames) {
624 |     Ref decl = n.getDeclaration();
625 |     if (decl == null) {
626 |       // Some names do not have declarations, because they
627 |       // are only defined in local scopes.
628 |       return;
629 |     }
630 | 
631 |     if (decl.getTwin() != null) {
632 |       // Twin declarations will get handled when normal references
633 |       // are handled.
634 |       return;
635 |     }
636 | 
637 |     switch (decl.node.getParent().getType()) {
638 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
639 |         updateObjLitOrFunctionDeclarationAtAssignNode(
640 |             n, alias, canCollapseChildNames);
641 |         break;
642 |       case Token.VAR:
643 |         updateObjLitOrFunctionDeclarationAtVarNode(n, canCollapseChildNames);
644 |         break;
645 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
646 |         updateFunctionDeclarationAtFunctionNode(n, canCollapseChildNames);
647 |         break;
648 |     }
649 |   }

===== M0992 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.InlineVariables.InliningBehavior.isInlineableDeclaredConstant(Var,ReferenceCollection)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/InlineVariables.java
Original range: 454-485
Documentation:
/**
     * Determines whether the given variable is declared as a constant
     * and may be inlined.
     */
Method code:
454 |     private boolean isInlineableDeclaredConstant(Var var,
455 |         ReferenceCollection refInfo) {
456 |       if (!identifyConstants.apply(var)) {
457 |         return false;
458 |       }
459 | 
460 |       if (!refInfo.isAssignedOnceInLifetime()) {
461 |         return false;
462 |       }
463 | 
464 |       Reference init = refInfo.getInitializingReferenceForConstants();
465 |       if (init == null) {
466 |         return false;
467 |       }
468 | 
469 |       Node value = init.getAssignedValue();
470 |       if (value == null) {
471 |         // This constant is either externally defined or initialized indirectly
472 |         // (e.g. in an function expression used to hide
473 |         // temporary variables), so the constant is ineligible for inlining.
474 |         return false;
475 |       }
476 | 
477 |       // Is the constant's value immutable?
478 |       if (!NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(value)) {
479 |         return false;
480 |       }
481 | 
482 |       // Determine if we should really inline a String or not.
483 |       return !value.isString() ||
484 |           isStringWorthInlining(var, refInfo.references);
485 |     }

   * Try removing unneeded block nodes and their useless children
   */
Method code:
459 |   Node tryOptimizeBlock(Node n) {
460 |     // Remove any useless children
461 |     for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; ) {
462 |       Node next = c.getNext();  // save c.next, since 'c' may be removed
463 |       if (!mayHaveSideEffects(c) && !c.isSyntheticBlock()) {

471 |       }

473 |     }

32 |   @Override
33 |   Node optimizeSubtree(Node subtree) {
34 |     // if the operator is symertric
35 |     if (NodeUtil.isSymmetricOperation(subtree)
36 |         || NodeUtil.isRelationalOperation(subtree)) {
37 |       // right value is immutable and left is not

45 |         }

49 |         Node lastNode = subtree.getLastChild().detachFromParent();
50 | 
51 |         subtree.addChildrenToFront(lastNode);

===== M1033 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CollapseVariableDeclarations.GatherCollapses.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CollapseVariableDeclarations.java
Original range: 136-179
Documentation:

Method code:
136 |     @Override
137 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
138 |       if (n.isVar()) {
139 |         blacklistStubVars(t, n);
140 |       }
141 | 
142 |       // Only care about var nodes
143 |       if (!n.isVar() && !canBeRedeclared(n, t.getScope())) return;
144 | 
145 |       // If we've already looked at this node, skip it
146 |       if (nodesToCollapse.contains(n)) return;
147 | 
148 |       // Adjacent VAR children of an IF node are the if and else parts and can't
149 |       // be collapsed
150 |       if (parent.isIf()) return;
151 | 
152 |       Node varNode = n;
153 | 
154 |       boolean hasVar = n.isVar();
155 | 
156 |       // Find variable declarations that follow this one (if any)
157 |       n = n.getNext();
158 | 
159 |       boolean hasNodesToCollapse = false;
160 | 
161 |       while (n != null &&
162 |           (n.isVar() || canBeRedeclared(n, t.getScope()))) {
163 | 
164 |         if (n.isVar()) {
165 |           blacklistStubVars(t, n);
166 |           hasVar = true;
167 |         }
168 | 
169 |         nodesToCollapse.add(n);
170 |         hasNodesToCollapse = true;
171 | 
172 |         n = n.getNext();
173 |       }
174 | 
175 |       if (hasNodesToCollapse && hasVar) {
176 |         nodesToCollapse.add(varNode);
177 |         collapses.add(new Collapse(varNode, n, parent));
178 |       }
179 |     }

===== M1060 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeOptimizationsPass.traverse(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeOptimizationsPass.java
Original range: 113-135
Documentation:

Method code:
113 |   private void traverse(Node node) {
114 |     // The goal here is to avoid retraversing
115 |     // the entire AST to catch newly created opportunities.
116 |     // So we track whether a "unit of code" has changed,
117 |     // and revisit immediately.
118 |     if (!shouldVisit(node)) {
119 |       return;
120 |     }
121 | 
122 |     int visits = 0;
123 |     do {
124 |       for (Node c = node.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
125 |         traverse(c);
126 |       }
127 | 
128 |       visit(node);
129 |       visits++;
130 | 
131 |       Preconditions.checkState(visits < 10000, "too many interations");
132 |     } while (shouldRetraverse(node));
133 | 
134 |     exitNode(node);
135 |   }
