===== M1070 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.optimizeSubtree(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.java
Original range: 75-166
Documentation:
/**
   * Tries apply our various peephole minimizations on the passed in node.
   */
Method code:
75 |   @Override
76 |   @SuppressWarnings("fallthrough")
77 |   public Node optimizeSubtree(Node node) {
78 |     switch(node.getType()) {
79 |       case Token.RETURN: {
80 |         Node result = tryRemoveRedundantExit(node);
81 |         if (result != node) {
82 |           return result;
83 |         }
84 |         result = tryReplaceExitWithBreak(node);
85 |         if (result != node) {
86 |           return result;
87 |         }
88 |         return tryReduceReturn(node);
89 |       }
90 | 
91 |       case Token.THROW: {
92 |         Node result = tryRemoveRedundantExit(node);
93 |         if (result != node) {
94 |           return result;
95 |         }
96 |         return tryReplaceExitWithBreak(node);
97 |       }
98 | 
99 |       // TODO(johnlenz): Maybe remove redundant BREAK and CONTINUE. Overlaps
100 |       // with MinimizeExitPoints.
101 | 
102 |       case Token.NOT:
103 |         tryMinimizeCondition(node.getFirstChild());
104 |         return tryMinimizeNot(node);
105 | 
106 |       case Token.IF:
107 |         tryMinimizeCondition(node.getFirstChild());
108 |         return tryMinimizeIf(node);
109 | 
110 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
111 |         tryMinimizeCondition(node.getFirstChild());
112 |         return node;
113 | 
114 |       case Token.HOOK:
115 |         tryMinimizeCondition(node.getFirstChild());
116 |         return node;
117 | 
118 |       case Token.WHILE:
119 |       case Token.DO:
120 |         tryMinimizeCondition(NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(node));
121 |         return node;
122 | 
123 |       case Token.FOR:
124 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(node)) {
125 |           tryJoinForCondition(node);
126 |           tryMinimizeCondition(NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(node));
127 |         }
128 |         return node;
129 | 
130 |       case Token.TRUE:
131 |       case Token.FALSE:
132 |         return reduceTrueFalse(node);
133 | 
134 |       case Token.NEW:
135 |         node = tryFoldStandardConstructors(node);
136 |         if (!node.isCall()) {
137 |           return node;
138 |         }
139 |         // Fall through on purpose because tryFoldStandardConstructors() may
140 |         // convert a NEW node into a CALL node
141 |       case Token.CALL:
142 |         Node result =  tryFoldLiteralConstructor(node);
143 |         if (result == node) {
144 |           result = tryFoldSimpleFunctionCall(node);
145 |           if (result == node) {
146 |             result = tryFoldImmediateCallToBoundFunction(node);
147 |           }
148 |         }
149 |         return result;
150 | 
151 |       case Token.COMMA:
152 |         return trySplitComma(node);
153 | 
154 |       case Token.NAME:
155 |         return tryReplaceUndefined(node);
156 | 
157 |       case Token.BLOCK:
158 |         return tryReplaceIf(node);
159 | 
160 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
161 |         return tryMinimizeArrayLiteral(node);
162 | 
163 |       default:
164 |         return node; //Nothing changed
165 |     }
166 |   }

   *   function (x) {
   *     x=2;
   *     return x;
   *   }
   *
   * We don't want "undefined" to be substituted for "x", and get
   *   undefined=2
   *
   * @param n The node in question.
   * @param parent The parent of the node.
   * @param names The set of names to check.
   * @param unsafe The set of names that require aliases.
   * @param inInnerFunction Whether the inspection is occurring on a inner
   *     function.
   */
Method code:
195 |   private static Set<String> findModifiedParameters(
196 |       Node n, Node parent, Set<String> names, Set<String> unsafe,
197 |       boolean inInnerFunction) {
198 |     Preconditions.checkArgument(unsafe != null);
199 |     if (n.isName()) {
200 |       if (names.contains(n.getString())) {
201 |         if (inInnerFunction || canNameValueChange(n, parent)) {
202 |           unsafe.add(n.getString());
203 |         }
204 |       }
205 |     } else if (n.isFunction()) {
206 |       // A function parameter can not be replaced with a direct inlined value
207 |       // if it is referred to by an inner function. The inner function
208 |       // can out live the call we are replacing, so inner function must
209 |       // capture a unique name.  This approach does not work within loop
210 |       // bodies so those are forbidden elsewhere.
211 |       inInnerFunction = true;
212 |     }
213 | 
214 |     for (Node c : n.children()) {
215 |       findModifiedParameters(c, n, names, unsafe, inInnerFunction);
216 |     }
217 | 
218 |     return unsafe;
219 |   }

   * Simplify a toplevel expression, while preserving program

1650 |   private void replaceTopLevelExpressionWithRhs(Node parent, Node n) {
1651 |     // validate inputs
1652 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
1653 |       case Token.BLOCK:
1654 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
1655 |       case Token.FOR:

===== M1108 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ProcessClosurePrimitives.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ProcessClosurePrimitives.java
Original range: 175-266
Documentation:

Method code:
175 |   @Override
176 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
177 |     switch (n.getType()) {
178 |       case Token.CALL:
179 |         boolean isExpr = parent.isExprResult();
180 |         Node left = n.getFirstChild();
181 |         if (left.isGetProp()) {
182 |           Node name = left.getFirstChild();
183 |           if (name.isName() &&
184 |               GOOG.equals(name.getString())) {
185 |             // For the sake of simplicity, we report code changes
186 |             // when we see a provides/requires, and don't worry about
187 |             // reporting the change when we actually do the replacement.
188 |             String methodName = name.getNext().getString();
189 |             if ("base".equals(methodName)) {
190 |               processBaseClassCall(t, n);
191 |             } else if (!isExpr) {
192 |               // All other methods must be called in an EXPR.
193 |               break;
194 |             } else if ("require".equals(methodName)) {
195 |               processRequireCall(t, n, parent);
196 |             } else if ("provide".equals(methodName)) {
197 |               processProvideCall(t, n, parent);
198 |             } else if ("exportSymbol".equals(methodName)) {
199 |               Node arg = left.getNext();
200 |               if (arg.isString()) {
201 |                 int dot = arg.getString().indexOf('.');
202 |                 if (dot == -1) {
203 |                   exportedVariables.add(arg.getString());
204 |                 } else {
205 |                   exportedVariables.add(arg.getString().substring(0, dot));
206 |                 }
207 |               }
208 |             } else if ("addDependency".equals(methodName)) {
209 |               CodingConvention convention = compiler.getCodingConvention();
210 |               List<String> typeDecls =
211 |                   convention.identifyTypeDeclarationCall(n);
212 |               if (typeDecls != null) {
213 |                 for (String typeDecl : typeDecls) {
214 |                   compiler.getTypeRegistry().forwardDeclareType(typeDecl);
215 |                 }
216 |               }
217 | 
218 |               // We can't modify parent, so just create a node that will
219 |               // get compiled out.
220 |               parent.replaceChild(n, IR.number(0));
221 |               compiler.reportCodeChange();
222 |             } else if ("setCssNameMapping".equals(methodName)) {
223 |               processSetCssNameMapping(t, n, parent);
224 |             }
225 |           }
226 |         }
227 |         break;
228 | 
229 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
230 |       case Token.NAME:
231 |         // If this is an assignment to a provided name, remove the provided
232 |         // object.
233 |         handleCandidateProvideDefinition(t, n, parent);
234 |         break;
235 | 
236 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
237 |         handleTypedefDefinition(t, n, parent);
238 |         break;
239 | 
240 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
241 |         // If this is a declaration of a provided named function, this is an
242 |         // error. Hosited functions will explode if the're provided.
243 |         if (t.inGlobalScope() &&
244 |             !NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(n)) {
245 |           String name = n.getFirstChild().getString();
246 |           ProvidedName pn = providedNames.get(name);
247 |           if (pn != null) {
248 |             compiler.report(t.makeError(n, FUNCTION_NAMESPACE_ERROR, name));
249 |           }
250 |         }
251 |         break;
252 | 
253 |       case Token.NEW:
254 |         trySimplifyNewDate(t, n, parent);
255 |         break;
256 | 
257 |       case Token.GETPROP:
258 |         if (n.getFirstChild().isName() &&
259 |             !parent.isCall() &&
260 |             !parent.isAssign() &&
261 |             "goog.base".equals(n.getQualifiedName())) {
262 |           reportBadBaseClassUse(t, n, "May only be called directly.");
263 |         }
264 |         break;
265 |     }
266 |   }

===== M1119 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RemoveUnusedVars.interpretAssigns()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RemoveUnusedVars.java
Original range: 704-753
Documentation:
/**
   * Look at all the property assigns to all variables.
   * These may or may not count as references. For example,
   *
   * <code>
   * var x = {};
   * x.foo = 3; // not a reference.
   * var y = foo();
   * y.foo = 3; // is a reference.
   * </code>
   *
   * Interpreting assignments could mark a variable as referenced that
   * wasn't referenced before, in order to keep it alive. Because we find
   * references by lazily traversing subtrees, marking a variable as
   * referenced could trigger new traversals of new subtrees, which could
   * find new references.
   *
   * Therefore, this interpretation needs to be run to a fixed point.
   */
Method code:
704 |   private void interpretAssigns() {
705 |     boolean changes = false;
706 |     do {
707 |       changes = false;
708 | 
709 |       // We can't use traditional iterators and iterables for this list,
710 |       // because our lazily-evaluated continuations will modify it while
711 |       // we traverse it.
712 |       for (int current = 0; current < maybeUnreferenced.size(); current++) {
713 |         Var var = maybeUnreferenced.get(current);
714 |         if (referenced.contains(var)) {
715 |           maybeUnreferenced.remove(current);
716 |           current--;
717 |         } else {
718 |           boolean assignedToUnknownValue = false;
719 |           boolean hasPropertyAssign = false;
720 | 
721 |           if (var.getParentNode().isVar() &&
722 |               !NodeUtil.isForIn(var.getParentNode().getParent())) {
723 |             Node value = var.getInitialValue();
724 |             assignedToUnknownValue = value != null &&
725 |                 !NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(value, true);
726 |           } else {
727 |             // This was initialized to a function arg or a catch param
728 |             // or a for...in variable.
729 |             assignedToUnknownValue = true;
730 |           }
731 | 
732 |           boolean maybeEscaped = false;
733 |           for (Assign assign : assignsByVar.get(var)) {
734 |             if (assign.isPropertyAssign) {
735 |               hasPropertyAssign = true;
736 |             } else if (!NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(
737 |                 assign.assignNode.getLastChild(), true)) {
738 |               assignedToUnknownValue = true;
739 |             }
740 |             if (assign.maybeAliased) {
741 |               maybeEscaped = true;
742 |             }
743 |           }
744 | 
745 |           if ((assignedToUnknownValue || maybeEscaped) && hasPropertyAssign) {
746 |             changes = markReferencedVar(var) || changes;
747 |             maybeUnreferenced.remove(current);
748 |             current--;
749 |           }
750 |         }
751 |       }
752 |     } while (changes);
753 |   }

/**
     * Processes the GETPROP of prototype, which can either be under
     * another GETPROP (in the case of Foo.prototype.bar), or can be
     * under an assignment (in the case of Foo.prototype = ...).
     * @return True if a declaration was added.
     */
Method code:
454 |     private boolean processPrototypeRef(NodeTraversal t, Node ref) {
455 |       Node root = NodeUtil.getRootOfQualifiedName(ref);
456 | 
457 |       Node n = ref.getParent();
458 |       switch (n.getType()) {
459 |         // Foo.prototype.getBar = function() { ... }
460 |         case Token.GETPROP:
461 |           Node dest = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
462 |           Node parent = n.getParent();
463 |           Node grandParent = parent.getParent();
464 | 
465 |           if (dest.isString() &&
466 |               NodeUtil.isExprAssign(grandParent) &&
467 |               NodeUtil.isVarOrSimpleAssignLhs(n, parent)) {
468 |             String name = dest.getString();
469 |             Property prop = new AssignmentProperty(
470 |                 grandParent,
471 |                 maybeGetVar(t, root),
472 |                 t.getModule());
473 |             getNameInfoForName(name, PROPERTY).getDeclarations().add(prop);
474 |             return true;
475 |           }
476 |           break;
477 | 
478 |         // Foo.prototype = { "getBar" : function() { ... } }
479 |         case Token.ASSIGN:
480 |           Node map = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
481 |           if (map.isObjectLit()) {
482 |             for (Node key = map.getFirstChild();
483 |                  key != null; key = key.getNext()) {
484 |               // May be STRING, GETTER_DEF, or SETTER_DEF,
485 |               String name = key.getString();
486 |               Property prop = new LiteralProperty(
487 |                   key, key.getFirstChild(), map, n,
488 |                   maybeGetVar(t, root),
489 |                   t.getModule());
490 |               getNameInfoForName(name, PROPERTY).getDeclarations().add(prop);
491 |             }
492 |             return true;
493 |           }
494 |           break;
495 |       }
496 |       return false;
497 |     }

===== M1141 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.UnionTypeBuilder.addAlternate(JSType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/UnionTypeBuilder.java
Original range: 121-212
Documentation:
/**
   * Adds an alternate to the union type under construction. Returns this
   * for easy chaining.
   */
Method code:
121 |   UnionTypeBuilder addAlternate(JSType alternate) {
122 |     // build() returns the bottom type by default, so we can
123 |     // just bail out early here.
124 |     if (alternate.isNoType()) {
125 |       return this;
126 |     }
127 | 
128 |     isAllType = isAllType || alternate.isAllType();
129 | 
130 |     boolean isAlternateUnknown = alternate instanceof UnknownType;
131 |     isNativeUnknownType = isNativeUnknownType || isAlternateUnknown;
132 |     if (isAlternateUnknown) {
133 |       areAllUnknownsChecked = areAllUnknownsChecked &&
134 |           alternate.isCheckedUnknownType();
135 |     }
136 |     if (!isAllType && !isNativeUnknownType) {
137 |       if (alternate.isUnionType()) {
138 |         UnionType union = alternate.toMaybeUnionType();
139 |         for (JSType unionAlt : union.getAlternates()) {
140 |           addAlternate(unionAlt);
141 |         }
142 |       } else {
143 |         if (alternates.size() > maxUnionSize) {
144 |           return this;
145 |         }
146 | 
147 |         // Function types are special, because they have their
148 |         // own bizarro sub-lattice. See the commants on
149 |         // FunctionType#supAndInf helper and above at functionTypePosition.
150 |         if (alternate.isFunctionType() && functionTypePosition != -1) {
151 |           // See the comments on functionTypePosition above.
152 |           FunctionType other =
153 |               alternates.get(functionTypePosition).toMaybeFunctionType();
154 |           FunctionType supremum =
155 |               alternate.toMaybeFunctionType().supAndInfHelper(other, true);
156 |           alternates.set(functionTypePosition, supremum);
157 |           result = null;
158 |           return this;
159 |         }
160 | 
161 |         // Look through the alternates we've got so far,
162 |         // and check if any of them are duplicates of
163 |         // one another.
164 |         int currentIndex = 0;
165 |         Iterator<JSType> it = alternates.iterator();
166 |         while (it.hasNext()) {
167 |           JSType current = it.next();
168 | 
169 |           // Unknown and NoResolved types may just be names that haven't
170 |           // been resolved yet. So keep these in the union, and just use
171 |           // equality checking for simple de-duping.
172 |           if (alternate.isUnknownType() ||
173 |               current.isUnknownType() ||
174 |               alternate.isNoResolvedType() ||
175 |               current.isNoResolvedType()) {
176 |             if (alternate.isEquivalentTo(current)) {
177 |               // Alternate is unnecessary.
178 |               return this;
179 |             }
180 |           } else {
181 |             if (alternate.isSubtype(current)) {
182 |               // Alternate is unnecessary.
183 |               return this;
184 |             } else if (current.isSubtype(alternate)) {
185 |               // Alternate makes current obsolete
186 |               it.remove();
187 | 
188 |               if (currentIndex == functionTypePosition) {
189 |                 functionTypePosition = -1;
190 |               } else if (currentIndex < functionTypePosition) {
191 |                 functionTypePosition--;
192 |                 currentIndex--;
193 |               }
194 |             }
195 |           }
196 |           currentIndex++;
197 |         }
198 | 
199 |         if (alternate.isFunctionType()) {
200 |           // See the comments on functionTypePosition above.
201 |           Preconditions.checkState(functionTypePosition == -1);
202 |           functionTypePosition = alternates.size();
203 |         }
204 | 
205 |         alternates.add(alternate);
206 |         result = null; // invalidate the memoized result
207 |       }
208 |     } else {
209 |       result = null;
210 |     }
211 |     return this;
212 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.checkForStateChangeHelper(Node,boolean,AbstractCompiler)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 784-927
Documentation:
/**
   * Returns true if some node in n's subtree changes application state.
   * If {@code checkForNewObjects} is true, we assume that newly created
   * mutable objects (like object literals) change state. Otherwise, we assume
   * that they have no side effects.
   */
Method code:
784 |   private static boolean checkForStateChangeHelper(
785 |       Node n, boolean checkForNewObjects, AbstractCompiler compiler) {
786 |     // Rather than id which ops may have side effects, id the ones
787 |     // that we know to be safe
788 |     switch (n.getType()) {
789 |       // other side-effect free statements and expressions
790 |       case Token.AND:
791 |       case Token.BLOCK:
792 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
793 |       case Token.HOOK:
794 |       case Token.IF:
795 |       case Token.IN:
796 |       case Token.PARAM_LIST:
797 |       case Token.NUMBER:
798 |       case Token.OR:
799 |       case Token.THIS:
800 |       case Token.TRUE:
801 |       case Token.FALSE:
802 |       case Token.NULL:
803 |       case Token.STRING:
804 |       case Token.SWITCH:
805 |       case Token.TRY:
806 |       case Token.EMPTY:
807 |         break;
808 | 
809 |       // Throws are by definition side effects
810 |       case Token.THROW:
811 |         return true;
812 | 
813 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
814 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
815 |           return true;
816 |         }
817 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
818 |           if (checkForStateChangeHelper(
819 |                   c.getFirstChild(), checkForNewObjects, compiler)) {
820 |             return true;
821 |           }
822 |         }
823 |         return false;
824 | 
825 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
826 |       case Token.REGEXP:
827 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
828 |           return true;
829 |         }
830 |         break;
831 | 
832 |       case Token.VAR:    // empty var statement (no declaration)
833 |       case Token.NAME:   // variable by itself
834 |         if (n.getFirstChild() != null) {
835 |           return true;
836 |         }
837 |         break;
838 | 
839 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
840 |         // Function expressions don't have side-effects, but function
841 |         // declarations change the namespace. Either way, we don't need to
842 |         // check the children, since they aren't executed at declaration time.
843 |         return checkForNewObjects || !isFunctionExpression(n);
844 | 
845 |       case Token.NEW:
846 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
847 |           return true;
848 |         }
849 | 
850 |         if (!constructorCallHasSideEffects(n)) {
851 |           // loop below will see if the constructor parameters have
852 |           // side-effects
853 |           break;
854 |         }
855 |         return true;
856 | 
857 |       case Token.CALL:
858 |         // calls to functions that have no side effects have the no
859 |         // side effect property set.
860 |         if (!functionCallHasSideEffects(n, compiler)) {
861 |           // loop below will see if the function parameters have
862 |           // side-effects
863 |           break;
864 |         }
865 |         return true;
866 | 
867 |       default:
868 |         if (isSimpleOperatorType(n.getType())) {
869 |           break;
870 |         }
871 | 
872 |         if (isAssignmentOp(n)) {
873 |           Node assignTarget = n.getFirstChild();
874 |           if (assignTarget.isName()) {
875 |             return true;
876 |           }
877 | 
878 |           // Assignments will have side effects if
879 |           // a) The RHS has side effects, or
880 |           // b) The LHS has side effects, or
881 |           // c) A name on the LHS will exist beyond the life of this statement.
882 |           if (checkForStateChangeHelper(
883 |                   n.getFirstChild(), checkForNewObjects, compiler) ||
884 |               checkForStateChangeHelper(
885 |                   n.getLastChild(), checkForNewObjects, compiler)) {
886 |             return true;
887 |           }
888 | 
889 |           if (isGet(assignTarget)) {
890 |             // If the object being assigned to is a local object, don't
891 |             // consider this a side-effect as it can't be referenced
892 |             // elsewhere.  Don't do this recursively as the property might
893 |             // be an alias of another object, unlike a literal below.
894 |             Node current = assignTarget.getFirstChild();
895 |             if (evaluatesToLocalValue(current)) {
896 |               return false;
897 |             }
898 | 
899 |             // A literal value as defined by "isLiteralValue" is guaranteed
900 |             // not to be an alias, or any components which are aliases of
901 |             // other objects.
902 |             // If the root object is a literal don't consider this a
903 |             // side-effect.
904 |             while (isGet(current)) {
905 |               current = current.getFirstChild();
906 |             }
907 | 
908 |             return !isLiteralValue(current, true);
909 |           } else {
910 |             // TODO(johnlenz): remove this code and make this an exception. This
911 |             // is here only for legacy reasons, the AST is not valid but
912 |             // preserve existing behavior.
913 |             return !isLiteralValue(assignTarget, true);
914 |           }
915 |         }
916 | 
917 |         return true;
918 |     }
919 | 
920 |     for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
921 |       if (checkForStateChangeHelper(c, checkForNewObjects, compiler)) {
922 |         return true;
923 |       }
924 |     }
925 | 
926 |     return false;
927 |   }

211 |     @Override
212 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
213 |       if (!n.isName()) {
214 |         return;
215 |       }
216 | 
217 |       String name = n.getString();
218 | 
219 |       // Ignore anonymous functions
220 |       if (name.length() == 0) {
221 |         return;
222 |       }
223 | 
224 |       // Is this local or Global?
225 |       // Bleeding functions should be treated as part of their outer
226 |       // scope, because IE has bugs in how it handles bleeding
227 |       // functions.
228 |       Scope.Var var = t.getScope().getVar(name);
229 |       boolean local = (var != null) && var.isLocal() &&
230 |           (!var.scope.getParent().isGlobal() ||
231 |            !var.isBleedingFunction());
232 | 
233 |       // Are we renaming global variables?
234 |       if (!local && localRenamingOnly) {
235 |         reservedNames.add(name);
236 |         return;
237 |       }
238 | 
239 |       // Are we renaming function expression names?
240 |       if (preserveFunctionExpressionNames && var != null
241 |           && NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(var.getParentNode())) {
242 |         reservedNames.add(name);
243 |         return;
244 |       }
245 |

247 |       if (!okToRenameVar(name, local)) {
248 |         if (local) {
249 |           // Blindly de-uniquify for the Prototype library for issue 103.
250 |           String newName = MakeDeclaredNamesUnique.ContextualRenameInverter
251 |               .getOrginalName(name);
252 |           if (!newName.equals(name)) {
253 |             n.setString(newName);
254 |           }
255 |         }
256 |         return;
257 |       }
258 | 
259 |       if (isExternsPass_) {
260 |         // Keep track of extern globals.
261 |         if (!local) {
262 |           externNames.add(name);
263 |         }
264 |         return;
265 |       }
266 |

268 |         recordPseudoName(n);
269 |       }
270 | 
271 |       if (local) {
272 |         // Local var: assign a new name
273 |         String tempName = LOCAL_VAR_PREFIX + getLocalVarIndex(var);
274 |         incCount(tempName);
275 |         localNameNodes.add(n);
276 |         n.setString(tempName);
277 |       } else if (var != null) { // Not an extern
278 |         // If it's global, increment global count

104 |   public void hotSwapScript(Node root, Node originalRoot) {
105 |     Traversal traversal = new Traversal();
106 |     NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, root, traversal);
107 | 
108 |     if (!traversal.hasErrors()) {
109 | 
110 |       // Apply the aliases.
111 |       for (AliasUsage aliasUsage : traversal.getAliasUsages()) {
112 |         aliasUsage.applyAlias();
113 |       }
114 | 
115 |       // Remove the alias definitions.
116 |       for (Node aliasDefinition : traversal.getAliasDefinitionsInOrder()) {
117 |         if (aliasDefinition.getParent().isVar() &&
118 |             aliasDefinition.getParent().hasOneChild()) {
119 |           aliasDefinition.getParent().detachFromParent();
120 |         } else {
121 |           aliasDefinition.detachFromParent();
122 |         }
123 |       }
124 | 
125 |       // Collapse the scopes.
126 |       for (Node scopeCall : traversal.getScopeCalls()) {
127 |         Node expressionWithScopeCall = scopeCall.getParent();
128 |         Node scopeClosureBlock = scopeCall.getLastChild().getLastChild();
129 |         scopeClosureBlock.detachFromParent();
130 |         expressionWithScopeCall.getParent().replaceChild(
131 |             expressionWithScopeCall,
132 |             scopeClosureBlock);
133 |         NodeUtil.tryMergeBlock(scopeClosureBlock);
134 |       }
135 | 
136 |       if (traversal.getAliasUsages().size() > 0 ||
137 |           traversal.getAliasDefinitionsInOrder().size() > 0 ||
138 |           traversal.getScopeCalls().size() > 0) {
139 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
140 |       }
141 |     }
142 |   }

===== M1188 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.UnreachableCodeElimination.tryRemoveUnconditionalBranching(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/UnreachableCodeElimination.java
Original range: 130-179
Documentation:
/**
   * Tries to remove n if an unconditional branch node (break, continue or
   * return) if the target of n is the same as the the follow of n. That is, if
   * we remove n, the control flow remains the same. Also if n targets to
   * another unconditional branch, this function will recursively try to remove
   * the target branch as well. The reason why we want to cascade this removal
   * is because we only run this pass once. If we have code such as
   *
   * break -> break -> break
   *
   * where all 3 break's are useless. The order of removal matters. When we
   * first look at the first break, we see that it branches to the 2nd break.
   * However, if we remove the last break, the 2nd break becomes useless and
   * finally the first break becomes useless as well.
   *
   * @return The target of this jump. If the target is also useless jump,
   *     the target of that useless jump recursively.
   */
Method code:
130 |   @SuppressWarnings("fallthrough")
131 |   private Node tryRemoveUnconditionalBranching(Node n) {
132 |     /*
133 |      * For each of the unconditional branching control flow node, check to see
134 |      * if the ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode of that node is same as
135 |      * the branching target. If it is, the branch node is safe to be removed.
136 |      *
137 |      * This is not as clever as MinimizeExitPoints because it doesn't do any
138 |      * if-else conversion but it handles more complicated switch statements
139 |      * much nicer.
140 |      */
141 | 
142 |     // If n is null the target is the end of the function, nothing to do.
143 |     if (n == null) {
144 |        return n;
145 |     }
146 | 
147 |     DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> gNode = curCfg.getDirectedGraphNode(n);
148 | 
149 |     if (gNode == null) {
150 |       return n;
151 |     }
152 | 
153 |     switch (n.getType()) {
154 |       case Token.RETURN:
155 |         if (n.hasChildren()) {
156 |           break;
157 |         }
158 |       case Token.BREAK:
159 |       case Token.CONTINUE:
160 | 
161 |         // We are looking for a control flow changing statement that always
162 |         // branches to the same node. If removing it the control flow still
163 |         // branches to that same node. It is safe to remove it.
164 |         List<DiGraphEdge<Node,Branch>> outEdges = gNode.getOutEdges();
165 |         if (outEdges.size() == 1 &&
166 |             // If there is a next node, there is no chance this jump is useless.
167 |             (n.getNext() == null || n.getNext().isFunction())) {
168 | 
169 |           Preconditions.checkState(outEdges.get(0).getValue() == Branch.UNCOND);
170 |           Node fallThrough = computeFollowing(n);
171 |           Node nextCfgNode = outEdges.get(0).getDestination().getValue();
172 |           if (nextCfgNode == fallThrough) {
173 |             removeDeadExprStatementSafely(n);
174 |             return fallThrough;
175 |           }
176 |         }
177 |     }
178 |     return n;
179 |   }

/**
   * Creates name information for the current node during a traversal.
   *
   * @param t The node traversal
   * @param n The current node
   * @param parent The parent of n
   * @return The name information, or null if the name is irrelevant to this
   *     pass
   */
Method code:
1318 |   private NameInformation createNameInformation(NodeTraversal t, Node n,
1319 |       Node parent) {
1320 |     // Build the full name and find its root node by iterating down through all
1321 |     // GETPROP/GETELEM nodes.
1322 |     String name = "";
1323 |     Node rootNameNode = n;
1324 |     boolean bNameWasShortened = false;
1325 |     while (true) {
1326 |       if (NodeUtil.isGet(rootNameNode)) {
1327 |         Node prop = rootNameNode.getLastChild();
1328 |         if (rootNameNode.isGetProp()) {
1329 |           name = "." + prop.getString() + name;
1330 |         } else {
1331 |           // We consider the name to be "a.b" in a.b['c'] or a.b[x].d.
1332 |           bNameWasShortened = true;
1333 |           name = "";
1334 |         }
1335 |         rootNameNode = rootNameNode.getFirstChild();
1336 |       } else if (NodeUtil.isObjectLitKey(
1337 |           rootNameNode, rootNameNode.getParent())) {
1338 |         name = "." + rootNameNode.getString() + name;
1339 | 
1340 |         // Check if this is an object literal assigned to something.
1341 |         Node objLit = rootNameNode.getParent();
1342 |         Node objLitParent = objLit.getParent();
1343 |         if (objLitParent.isAssign()) {
1344 |           // This must be the right side of the assign.
1345 |           rootNameNode = objLitParent.getFirstChild();
1346 |         } else if (objLitParent.isName()) {
1347 |           // This must be a VAR initialization.
1348 |           rootNameNode = objLitParent;
1349 |         } else if (objLitParent.isString()) {
1350 |           // This must be a object literal key initialization.
1351 |           rootNameNode = objLitParent;
1352 |         } else {
1353 |           return null;
1354 |         }
1355 |       } else {
1356 |         break;
1357 |       }
1358 |     }
1359 | 
1360 |     // Check whether this is a class-defining call. Classes may only be defined
1361 |     // in the global scope.
1362 |     if (parent.isCall() && t.inGlobalScope()) {
1363 |       CodingConvention convention = compiler.getCodingConvention();
1364 |       SubclassRelationship classes = convention.getClassesDefinedByCall(parent);
1365 |       if (classes != null) {
1366 |         NameInformation nameInfo = new NameInformation();
1367 |         nameInfo.name = classes.subclassName;
1368 |         nameInfo.onlyAffectsClassDef = true;
1369 |         nameInfo.superclass = classes.superclassName;
1370 |         return nameInfo;
1371 |       }
1372 | 
1373 |       String singletonGetterClass =
1374 |           convention.getSingletonGetterClassName(parent);
1375 |       if (singletonGetterClass != null) {
1376 |         NameInformation nameInfo = new NameInformation();
1377 |         nameInfo.name = singletonGetterClass;
1378 |         nameInfo.onlyAffectsClassDef = true;
1379 |         return nameInfo;
1380 |       }
1381 |     }
1382 | 
1383 |     switch (rootNameNode.getType()) {
1384 |       case Token.NAME:
1385 |         // Check whether this is an assignment to a prototype property
1386 |         // of an object defined in the global scope.
1387 |         if (!bNameWasShortened &&
1388 |             n.isGetProp() &&
1389 |             parent.isAssign() &&
1390 |             "prototype".equals(n.getLastChild().getString())) {
1391 |           if (createNameInformation(t, n.getFirstChild(), n) != null) {
1392 |             name = rootNameNode.getString() + name;
1393 |             name = name.substring(0, name.length() - PROTOTYPE_SUFFIX_LEN);
1394 |             NameInformation nameInfo = new NameInformation();
1395 |             nameInfo.name = name;
1396 |             return nameInfo;
1397 |           } else {
1398 |             return null;
1399 |           }
1400 |         }
1401 |         return createNameInformation(
1402 |             rootNameNode.getString() + name, t.getScope(), rootNameNode);
1403 |       case Token.THIS:
1404 |         if (t.inGlobalScope()) {
1405 |           NameInformation nameInfo = new NameInformation();
1406 |           if (name.indexOf('.') == 0) {
1407 |             nameInfo.name = name.substring(1);  // strip leading "."
1408 |           } else {
1409 |             nameInfo.name = name;
1410 |           }
1411 |           nameInfo.isExternallyReferenceable = true;
1412 |           return nameInfo;
1413 |         }
1414 |         return null;
1415 |       default:
1416 |         return null;
1417 |     }
1418 |   }

/**
   * @param fnName The name of this function. This either the name of the
   *  variable to which the function is assigned or the name from the FUNCTION
   *  node.
   * @param fnNode The FUNCTION node of the function to inspect.
   * @return Whether the function node meets the minimum requirements for
   * inlining.
   */
Method code:
121 |   boolean doesFunctionMeetMinimumRequirements(
122 |       final String fnName, Node fnNode) {
123 |     Node block = NodeUtil.getFunctionBody(fnNode);
124 | 
125 |     // Basic restrictions on functions that can be inlined:
126 |     // 1) It contains a reference to itself.
127 |     // 2) It uses its parameters indirectly using "arguments" (it isn't
128 |     //    handled yet.
129 |     // 3) It references "eval". Inline a function containing eval can have
130 |     //    large performance implications.
131 | 
132 |     final String fnRecursionName = fnNode.getFirstChild().getString();
133 |     Preconditions.checkState(fnRecursionName != null);
134 | 
135 |     // If the function references "arguments" directly in the function
136 |     boolean referencesArguments = NodeUtil.isNameReferenced(
137 |         block, "arguments", NodeUtil.MATCH_NOT_FUNCTION);
138 | 
139 |     // or it references "eval" or one of its names anywhere.
140 |     Predicate<Node> p = new Predicate<Node>(){
141 |       @Override
142 |       public boolean apply(Node n) {
143 |         if (n.isName()) {
144 |           return n.getString().equals("eval")
145 |             || (!fnName.isEmpty()
146 |                 && n.getString().equals(fnName))
147 |             || (!fnRecursionName.isEmpty()
148 |                 && n.getString().equals(fnRecursionName));
149 |         }
150 |         return false;
151 |       }
152 |     };
153 | 
154 |     return !referencesArguments
155 |         && !NodeUtil.has(block, p, Predicates.<Node>alwaysTrue());
156 |   }

/**
   * @return true if this node marks the start of a new basic block
   */
Method code:
207 |   private static boolean isBlockBoundary(Node n, Node parent) {
208 |     if (parent != null) {
209 |       switch (parent.getType()) {
210 |         case Token.DO:
211 |         case Token.FOR:
212 |         case Token.TRY:
213 |         case Token.WHILE:
214 |         case Token.WITH:
215 |           // NOTE: TRY has up to 3 child blocks:
216 |           // TRY
217 |           //   BLOCK
218 |           //   BLOCK
219 |           //     CATCH
220 |           //   BLOCK
221 |           // Note that there is an explcit CATCH token but no explicit
222 |           // FINALLY token. For simplicity, we consider each BLOCK
223 |           // a separate basic BLOCK.
224 |           return true;
225 |         case Token.AND:
226 |         case Token.HOOK:
227 |         case Token.IF:
228 |         case Token.OR:
229 |           // The first child of a conditional is not a boundary,
230 |           // but all the rest of the children are.
231 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
232 | 
233 |       }
234 |     }
235 | 
236 |     return n.isCase();
237 |   }

   * Run all the passes in the optimizer.

Method code:
175 |   @Override
176 |   public void process(Node externs, Node root) {
177 |     double progress = 0.0;
178 |     double progressStep = 0.0;
179 |     if (progressRange != null) {
180 |       progressStep = (progressRange.maxValue - progressRange.initialValue)
181 |           / passes.size();
182 |       progress = progressRange.initialValue;
183 |     }
184 |     for (CompilerPass pass : passes) {
185 |       pass.process(externs, root);
186 |       if (progressRange != null) {
187 |         progress += progressStep;
188 |         compiler.setProgress(progress);
189 |       }

191 |         return;
192 |       }
193 |     }

/**
     * Determines whether the result of a hook (x?y:z) or boolean expression
     * (x||y) or (x&&y) is assigned to a specific global name.
     *
     * @param t The traversal
     * @param parent The parent of the current node in the traversal. This node
     *     should already be known to be a HOOK, AND, or OR node.
     * @param name A name that is already known to be global in the current
     *     scope (e.g. "a" or "a.b.c.d")
     * @return The expression's get type, either {@link Ref.Type#DIRECT_GET} or
     *     {@link Ref.Type#ALIASING_GET}
     */
Method code:
707 |     Ref.Type determineGetTypeForHookOrBooleanExpr(
708 |         NodeTraversal t, Node parent, String name) {
709 |       Node prev = parent;
710 |       for (Node anc : parent.getAncestors()) {
711 |         switch (anc.getType()) {
712 |           case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
713 |           case Token.VAR:
714 |           case Token.IF:
715 |           case Token.WHILE:
716 |           case Token.FOR:
717 |           case Token.TYPEOF:
718 |           case Token.VOID:
719 |           case Token.NOT:
720 |           case Token.BITNOT:
721 |           case Token.POS:
722 |           case Token.NEG:
723 |             return Ref.Type.DIRECT_GET;
724 |           case Token.HOOK:
725 |             if (anc.getFirstChild() == prev) {
726 |               return Ref.Type.DIRECT_GET;
727 |             }
728 |             break;
729 |           case Token.ASSIGN:
730 |             if (!name.equals(anc.getFirstChild().getQualifiedName())) {
731 |               return Ref.Type.ALIASING_GET;
732 |             }
733 |             break;
734 |           case Token.NAME:  // a variable declaration
735 |             if (!name.equals(anc.getString())) {
736 |               return Ref.Type.ALIASING_GET;
737 |             }
738 |             break;
739 |           case Token.CALL:
740 |             if (anc.getFirstChild() != prev) {
741 |               return Ref.Type.ALIASING_GET;
742 |             }
743 |             break;
744 |           case Token.DELPROP:
745 |             return Ref.Type.DELETE_PROP;
746 |         }
747 |         prev = anc;
748 |       }
749 |       return Ref.Type.ALIASING_GET;

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.OptimizeArgumentsArray.tryReplaceArguments(Scope)

Original range: 177-289

/**
   * Tries to optimize all the arguments array access in this scope by assigning
   * a name to each element.
   *
   * @param scope scope of the function
   * @return true if any modification has been done to the AST
   */
Method code:
177 |   private boolean tryReplaceArguments(Scope scope) {
178 | 
179 |     Node parametersList = scope.getRootNode().getFirstChild().getNext();
180 |     Preconditions.checkState(parametersList.isParamList());
181 | 
182 |     // Keep track of rather this function modified the AST and needs to be
183 |     // reported back to the compiler later.
184 |     boolean changed = false;
185 | 
186 |     // Number of parameter that can be accessed without using the arguments
187 |     // array.
188 |     int numNamedParameter = parametersList.getChildCount();
189 | 
190 |     // We want to guess what the highest index that has been access from the
191 |     // arguments array. We will guess that it does not use anything index higher
192 |     // than the named parameter list first until we see other wise.
193 |     int highestIndex = numNamedParameter - 1;
194 | 
195 |     // Iterate through all the references to arguments array in the function to
196 |     // determine the real highestIndex.
197 |     for (Node ref : currentArgumentsAccess) {
198 | 
199 |       Node getElem = ref.getParent();
200 | 
201 |       // Bail on anything but argument[c] access where c is a constant.
202 |       // TODO(user): We might not need to bail out all the time, there might
203 |       // be more cases that we can cover.
204 |       if (!getElem.isGetElem()) {
205 |         return false;
206 |       }
207 | 
208 |       Node index = ref.getNext();
209 | 
210 |       // We have something like arguments[x] where x is not a constant. That
211 |       // means at least one of the access is not known.
212 |       if (!index.isNumber()) {
213 |         // TODO(user): Its possible not to give up just yet. The type
214 |         // inference did a 'semi value propagation'. If we know that string
215 |         // is never a subclass of the type of the index. We'd know that
216 |         // it is never 'callee'.
217 |         return false; // Give up.
218 |       }
219 | 
220 |       Node getElemParent = getElem.getParent();
221 |       // When we have argument[0](), replacing it with a() is semantically
222 |       // different if argument[0] is a function call that refers to 'this'
223 |       if (getElemParent.isCall() &&
224 |           getElemParent.getFirstChild() == getElem) {
225 |         // TODO(user): We can consider using .call() if aliasing that
226 |         // argument allows shorter alias for other arguments.
227 |         return false;
228 |       }
229 | 
230 |       // Replace the highest index if we see an access that has a higher index
231 |       // than all the one we saw before.
232 |       int value = (int) index.getDouble();
233 |       if (value > highestIndex) {
234 |         highestIndex = value;
235 |       }
236 |     }
237 | 
238 |     // Number of extra arguments we need.
239 |     // For example: function() { arguments[3] } access index 3 so
240 |     // it will need 4 extra named arguments to changed into:
241 |     // function(a,b,c,d) { d }.
242 |     int numExtraArgs = highestIndex - numNamedParameter + 1;
243 | 
244 |     // Temporary holds the new names as string for quick access later.
245 |     String[] argNames = new String[numExtraArgs];
246 | 
247 |     // Insert the formal parameter to the method's signature.
248 |     // Example: function() --> function(r0, r1, r2)
249 |     for (int i = 0; i < numExtraArgs; i++) {
250 |       String name = getNewName();
251 |       argNames[i] = name;
252 |       parametersList.addChildrenToBack(IR.name(name));
253 |       changed = true;
254 |     }
255 | 
256 |     // This loop performs the replacement of arguments[x] -> a if x is known.
257 |     for (Node ref : currentArgumentsAccess) {
258 |       Node index = ref.getNext();
259 | 
260 |       // Skip if it is unknown.
261 |       if (!index.isNumber()) {
262 |         continue;
263 |       }
264 |       int value = (int) index.getDouble();
265 | 
266 |       // Unnamed parameter.
267 |       if (value >= numNamedParameter) {
268 |         ref.getParent().getParent().replaceChild(ref.getParent(),
269 |             IR.name(argNames[value - numNamedParameter]));
270 |       } else {
271 | 
272 |         // Here, for no apparent reason, the user is accessing a named parameter
273 |         // with arguments[idx]. We can replace it with the actual name for them.
274 |         Node name = parametersList.getFirstChild();
275 | 
276 |         // This is a linear search for the actual name from the signature.
277 |         // It is not necessary to make this fast because chances are the user
278 |         // will not deliberately write code like this.
279 |         for (int i = 0; i < value; i++) {
280 |           name = name.getNext();
281 |         }
282 |         ref.getParent().getParent().replaceChild(ref.getParent(),
283 |             IR.name(name.getString()));
284 |       }
285 |       changed = true;
286 |     }
287 | 
288 |     return changed;
289 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.DataFlowAnalysis.analyze(int)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/DataFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 199-227
Documentation:
/**
   * Finds a fixed-point solution. The function has the side effect of replacing
   * the existing node annotations with the computed solutions using {@link
   * com.google.javascript.jscomp.graph.GraphNode#setAnnotation(Annotation)}.
   *
   * <p>Initially, each node's input and output flow state contains the value
   * given by {@link #createInitialEstimateLattice()} (with the exception of the
   * entry node of the graph which takes on the {@link #createEntryLattice()}
   * value. Each node will use the output state of its predecessor and compute a
   * output state according to the instruction. At that time, any nodes that
   * depends on the node's newly modified output value will need to recompute
   * their output state again. Each step will perform a computation at one node
   * until no extra computation will modify any existing output state anymore.
   *
   * @param maxSteps Max number of iterations before the method stops and throw
   *        a {@link MaxIterationsExceededException}. This will prevent the
   *        analysis from going into a infinite loop.
   */
Method code:
199 |   final void analyze(int maxSteps) {
200 |     initialize();
201 |     int step = 0;
202 |     while (!orderedWorkSet.isEmpty()) {
203 |       if (step > maxSteps) {
204 |         throw new MaxIterationsExceededException(
205 |           "Analysis did not terminate after " + maxSteps + " iterations");
206 |       }
207 |       DiGraphNode<N, Branch> curNode = orderedWorkSet.iterator().next();
208 |       orderedWorkSet.remove(curNode);
209 |       joinInputs(curNode);
210 |       if (flow(curNode)) {
211 |         // If there is a change in the current node, we want to grab the list
212 |         // of nodes that this node affects.
213 |         List<DiGraphNode<N, Branch>> nextNodes = isForward() ?
214 |             cfg.getDirectedSuccNodes(curNode) :
215 |             cfg.getDirectedPredNodes(curNode);
216 |         for (DiGraphNode<N, Branch> nextNode : nextNodes) {
217 |           if (nextNode != cfg.getImplicitReturn()) {
218 |             orderedWorkSet.add(nextNode);
219 |           }
220 |         }
221 |       }
222 |       step++;
223 |     }
224 |     if (isForward()) {
225 |       joinInputs(getCfg().getImplicitReturn());
226 |     }
227 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.getImpureBooleanValue(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 76-116
Documentation:
/**
   * Gets the boolean value of a node that represents a expression. This method
   * effectively emulates the <code>Boolean()</code> JavaScript cast function.
   * Note: unlike getBooleanValue this function does not return UNKNOWN
   * for expressions with side-effects.
   */
Method code:
76 |   static TernaryValue getImpureBooleanValue(Node n) {
77 |     switch (n.getType()) {
78 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
79 |       case Token.COMMA:
80 |         // For ASSIGN and COMMA the value is the value of the RHS.
81 |         return getImpureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild());
82 |       case Token.NOT:
83 |         TernaryValue value = getImpureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild());
84 |         return value.not();
85 |       case Token.AND: {
86 |         TernaryValue lhs = getImpureBooleanValue(n.getFirstChild());
87 |         TernaryValue rhs = getImpureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild());
88 |         return lhs.and(rhs);
89 |       }
90 |       case Token.OR:  {
91 |         TernaryValue lhs = getImpureBooleanValue(n.getFirstChild());
92 |         TernaryValue rhs = getImpureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild());
93 |         return lhs.or(rhs);
94 |       }
95 |       case Token.HOOK:  {
96 |         TernaryValue trueValue = getImpureBooleanValue(
97 |             n.getFirstChild().getNext());
98 |         TernaryValue falseValue = getImpureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild());
99 |         if (trueValue.equals(falseValue)) {
100 |           return trueValue;
101 |         } else {
102 |           return TernaryValue.UNKNOWN;
103 |         }
104 |       }
105 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
106 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
107 |         // ignoring side-effects
108 |         return TernaryValue.TRUE;
109 | 
110 |       case Token.VOID:
111 |         return TernaryValue.FALSE;
112 | 
113 |       default:
114 |         return getPureBooleanValue(n);
115 |     }
116 |   }

===== M1306 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.GatherSideEffectSubexpressionsCallback.shouldTraverse(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/GatherSideEffectSubexpressionsCallback.java
Original range: 221-260
Documentation:
/**
   * Computes the list of subtrees whose root nodes have side effects.
   *
   * <p>If the current subtree's root has side effects this method should
   * call accumulator.keepSubTree and return 'false' to add the
   * subtree to the result list and avoid avoid traversing the nodes children.
   *
   * <p>Branching nodes whose then or else branch contain side effects
   * must be simplified by doing a recursive traversal; this method
   * should call the appropriate accumulator 'keepSimplified' method
   * and return 'false' to stop the regular traversal.
   */
Method code:
221 |   @Override
222 |   public boolean shouldTraverse(
223 |       NodeTraversal traversal, Node node, Node parent) {
224 |     if (FORBIDDEN_TYPES.contains(node.getType()) ||
225 |         NodeUtil.isControlStructure(node)) {
226 |       throw new IllegalArgumentException(
227 |           Token.name(node.getType()) + " nodes are not supported.");
228 |     }
229 | 
230 |     // Do not recurse into nested functions.
231 |     if (node.isFunction()) {
232 |       return false;
233 |     }
234 | 
235 |     // simplify and maybe keep hook expression.
236 |     if (node.isHook()) {
237 |       return processHook(node);
238 |     }
239 | 
240 |     // simplify and maybe keep AND/OR expression.
241 |     if ((node.isAnd()) || (node.isOr())) {
242 |       return processShortCircuitExpression(node);
243 |     }
244 | 
245 |     if (!NodeUtil.nodeTypeMayHaveSideEffects(node)) {
246 |       return true;
247 |     } else {
248 | 
249 |       // Node type suggests that the expression has side effects.
250 | 
251 |       if (node.isCall()) {
252 |         return processFunctionCall(node);
253 |       } else if (node.isNew()) {
254 |         return processConstructorCall(node);
255 |       } else {
256 |         accumulator.keepSubTree(node);
257 |         return false;
258 |       }
259 |     }
260 |   }

/**
   * Returns the index within the scope stack.
   * e.g. function Foo(a) { var b; function c(d) { } }
   * a = 0, b = 1, c = 2, d = 3
   */
Method code:
545 |   private int getLocalVarIndex(Var v) {
546 |     int num = v.index;
547 |     Scope s = v.scope.getParent();
548 |     if (s == null) {
549 |       throw new IllegalArgumentException("Var is not local");

553 |         localBleedingFunctions.contains(v);

557 |         num += localBleedingFunctionsPerScope.get(s).indexOf(v) + 1;
558 |         isBleedingIntoScope = false;

===== M1315 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.InlineVariables.InliningBehavior.canInline(Reference,Reference,Reference)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/InlineVariables.java
Original range: 519-580
Documentation:
/**
     * @return true if the provided reference and declaration can be safely
     *         inlined according to our criteria
     */
Method code:
519 |     private boolean canInline(
520 |         Reference declaration,
521 |         Reference initialization,
522 |         Reference reference) {
523 |       if (!isValidDeclaration(declaration)
524 |           || !isValidInitialization(initialization)
525 |           || !isValidReference(reference)) {
526 |         return false;
527 |       }
528 | 
529 |       // If the value is read more than once, skip it.
530 |       // VAR declarations and EXPR_RESULT don't need the value, but other
531 |       // ASSIGN expressions parents do.
532 |       if (declaration != initialization &&
533 |           !initialization.getGrandparent().isExprResult()) {
534 |         return false;
535 |       }
536 | 
537 |       // Be very conservative and do no cross control structures or
538 |       // scope boundaries
539 |       if (declaration.getBasicBlock() != initialization.getBasicBlock()
540 |           || declaration.getBasicBlock() != reference.getBasicBlock()) {
541 |         return false;
542 |       }
543 | 
544 |       // Do not inline into a call node. This would change
545 |       // the context in which it was being called. For example,
546 |       //   var a = b.c;
547 |       //   a();
548 |       // should not be inlined, because it calls a in the context of b
549 |       // rather than the context of the window.
550 |       //   var a = b.c;
551 |       //   f(a)
552 |       // is ok.
553 |       Node value = initialization.getAssignedValue();
554 |       Preconditions.checkState(value != null);
555 |       if (value.isGetProp()
556 |           && reference.getParent().isCall()
557 |           && reference.getParent().getFirstChild() == reference.getNode()) {
558 |         return false;
559 |       }
560 | 
561 |       if (value.isFunction()) {
562 |         Node callNode = reference.getParent();
563 |         if (reference.getParent().isCall()) {
564 |           CodingConvention convention = compiler.getCodingConvention();
565 |           // Bug 2388531: Don't inline subclass definitions into class defining
566 |           // calls as this confused class removing logic.
567 |           SubclassRelationship relationship =
568 |               convention.getClassesDefinedByCall(callNode);
569 |           if (relationship != null) {
570 |             return false;
571 |           }
572 | 
573 |           // issue 668: Don't inline singleton getter methods
574 |           // calls as this confused class removing logic.
575 |         }
576 |       }
577 | 
578 |       return canMoveAggressively(value) ||
579 |           canMoveModerately(initialization, reference);
580 |     }

/**
     * Updates our respresentation of the global namespace to reflect a read
     * of a global name.
     *
     * @param t The traversal
     * @param n The node currently being visited
     * @param parent {@code n}'s parent
     * @param name The global name (e.g. "a" or "a.b.c.d")
     */
Method code:
643 |     void handleGet(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent, String name) {
644 |       if (maybeHandlePrototypePrefix(t, n, parent, name)) return;
645 | 
646 |       Ref.Type type = Ref.Type.DIRECT_GET;
647 |       if (parent != null) {
648 |         switch (parent.getType()) {
649 |           case Token.IF:
650 |           case Token.TYPEOF:
651 |           case Token.VOID:
652 |           case Token.NOT:
653 |           case Token.BITNOT:
654 |           case Token.POS:
655 |           case Token.NEG:
656 |             break;
657 |           case Token.CALL:
658 |             type = n == parent.getFirstChild()
659 |                    ? Ref.Type.CALL_GET
660 |                    : Ref.Type.ALIASING_GET;
661 |             break;
662 |           case Token.NEW:
663 |             type = n == parent.getFirstChild()
664 |                    ? Ref.Type.DIRECT_GET
665 |                    : Ref.Type.ALIASING_GET;
666 |             break;
667 |           case Token.OR:
668 |           case Token.AND:
669 |             // This node is x or y in (x||y) or (x&&y). We only know that an
670 |             // alias is not getting created for this name if the result is used
671 |             // in a boolean context or assigned to the same name
672 |             // (e.g. var a = a || {}).
673 |             type = determineGetTypeForHookOrBooleanExpr(t, parent, name);
674 |             break;
675 |           case Token.HOOK:

677 |               // This node is y or z in (x?y:z). We only know that an alias is
678 |               // not getting created for this name if the result is assigned to
679 |               // the same name (e.g. var a = a ? a : {}).
680 |               type = determineGetTypeForHookOrBooleanExpr(t, parent, name);
681 |             }
682 |             break;
683 |           case Token.DELPROP:
684 |             type = Ref.Type.DELETE_PROP;
685 |             break;
686 |           default:
687 |             type = Ref.Type.ALIASING_GET;
688 |             break;
689 |         }
690 |       }
691 |

693 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ClosureCodingConvention.getClassesDefinedByCall(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ClosureCodingConvention.java
Original range: 74-129
Documentation:
/**
   * {@inheritDoc}
   *
   * <p>Understands several different inheritance patterns that occur in
   * Google code (various uses of {@code inherits} and {@code mixin}).
   */
Method code:
74 |   @Override
75 |   public SubclassRelationship getClassesDefinedByCall(Node callNode) {
76 |     Node callName = callNode.getFirstChild();
77 |     SubclassType type = typeofClassDefiningName(callName);
78 |     if (type != null) {
79 |       Node subclass = null;
80 |       Node superclass = callNode.getLastChild();
81 | 
82 |       // There are six possible syntaxes for a class-defining method:
83 |       // SubClass.inherits(SuperClass)
84 |       // goog.inherits(SubClass, SuperClass)
85 |       // goog$inherits(SubClass, SuperClass)
86 |       // SubClass.mixin(SuperClass.prototype)
87 |       // goog.mixin(SubClass.prototype, SuperClass.prototype)
88 |       // goog$mixin(SubClass.prototype, SuperClass.prototype)
89 |       boolean isDeprecatedCall = callNode.getChildCount() == 2 &&
90 |           callName.isGetProp();
91 |       if (isDeprecatedCall) {
92 |         // SubClass.inherits(SuperClass)
93 |         subclass = callName.getFirstChild();
94 |       } else if (callNode.getChildCount() == 3) {
95 |         // goog.inherits(SubClass, SuperClass)
96 |         subclass = callName.getNext();
97 |       } else {
98 |         return null;
99 |       }
100 | 
101 |       if (type == SubclassType.MIXIN) {
102 |         // Only consider mixins that mix two prototypes as related to
103 |         // inheritance.
104 |         if (!endsWithPrototype(superclass)) {
105 |           return null;
106 |         }
107 |         if (!isDeprecatedCall) {
108 |           if (!endsWithPrototype(subclass)) {
109 |             return null;
110 |           }
111 |           // Strip off the prototype from the name.
112 |           subclass = subclass.getFirstChild();
113 |         }
114 |         superclass = superclass.getFirstChild();
115 |       }
116 | 
117 |       // bail out if either of the side of the "inherits"
118 |       // isn't a real class name. This prevents us from
119 |       // doing something weird in cases like:
120 |       // goog.inherits(MySubClass, cond ? SuperClass1 : BaseClass2)
121 |       if (subclass != null &&
122 |           subclass.isUnscopedQualifiedName() &&
123 |           superclass.isUnscopedQualifiedName()) {
124 |         return new SubclassRelationship(type, subclass, superclass);
125 |       }
126 |     }
127 | 
128 |     return null;
129 |   }

508 |         break;
509 |       case Token.MUL:

511 |         break;
512 |       case Token.RSH:
513 |         newType = Token.ASSIGN_RSH;
514 |         break;
515 |       case Token.SUB:
516 |         newType = Token.ASSIGN_SUB;
517 |         break;
518 |       case Token.URSH:
519 |         newType = Token.ASSIGN_URSH;
520 |         break;
521 |       default:
522 |         return n;
523 |     }
524 | 
525 |     Node newNode = new Node(newType,
526 |         left.detachFromParent(), newRight.detachFromParent());
527 |     n.getParent().replaceChild(n, newNode);

===== M1355 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.DevirtualizePrototypeMethods.isEligibleDefinition(SimpleDefinitionFinder,DefinitionSite)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/DevirtualizePrototypeMethods.java
Original range: 205-278
Documentation:
/**
   * Determines if a method definition is eligible for rewrite as a
   * global function.  In order to be eligible for rewrite, the
   * definition must:
   *
   * - Refer to a function that takes a fixed number of arguments.
   * - Function must not be exported.
   * - Function must be used at least once.
   * - Property is never accesed outside a function call context.
   * - The definition under consideration must be the only possible
   *   choice at each call site.
   * - Definition must happen in a module loaded before the first use.
   */
Method code:
205 |   private boolean isEligibleDefinition(SimpleDefinitionFinder defFinder,
206 |                                        DefinitionSite definitionSite) {
207 | 
208 |     Definition definition = definitionSite.definition;
209 |     JSModule definitionModule = definitionSite.module;
210 | 
211 |     // Only functions may be rewritten.
212 |     // Functions that access "arguments" are not eligible since
213 |     // rewrite changes the structure of this object.
214 |     Node rValue = definition.getRValue();
215 |     if (rValue == null ||
216 |         !rValue.isFunction() ||
217 |         NodeUtil.isVarArgsFunction(rValue)) {
218 |       return false;
219 |     }
220 | 
221 |     // Exporting a method prevents rewrite.
222 |     Node lValue = definition.getLValue();
223 |     if ((lValue == null) ||
224 |         !lValue.isGetProp()) {
225 |       return false;
226 |     }
227 |     CodingConvention codingConvention = compiler.getCodingConvention();
228 |     if (codingConvention.isExported(lValue.getLastChild().getString())) {
229 |       return false;
230 |     }
231 | 
232 |     Collection<UseSite> useSites = defFinder.getUseSites(definition);
233 | 
234 |     // Rewriting unused methods is not sound.
235 |     if (useSites.isEmpty()) {
236 |       return false;
237 |     }
238 | 
239 |     JSModuleGraph moduleGraph = compiler.getModuleGraph();
240 | 
241 |     for (UseSite site : useSites) {
242 |       // Accessing the property directly prevents rewrite.
243 |       if (!isCall(site)) {
244 |         return false;
245 |       }
246 | 
247 |       // Multiple definitions prevent rewrite.
248 |       Node nameNode = site.node;
249 | 
250 |       // Don't rewrite methods called in functions that can't be specialized
251 |       // if we are specializing
252 |       if (specializationState != null &&
253 |           !specializationState.canFixupSpecializedFunctionContainingNode(
254 |               nameNode)) {
255 |         return false;
256 |       }
257 | 
258 |       Collection<Definition> singleSiteDefinitions =
259 |           defFinder.getDefinitionsReferencedAt(nameNode);
260 |       if (singleSiteDefinitions.size() > 1) {
261 |         return false;
262 |       }
263 |       Preconditions.checkState(!singleSiteDefinitions.isEmpty());
264 |       Preconditions.checkState(singleSiteDefinitions.contains(definition));
265 | 
266 |       // Accessing the property in a module loaded before the
267 |       // definition module prevents rewrite; accessing a variable
268 |       // before definition results in a parse error.
269 |       JSModule callModule = site.module;
270 |       if ((definitionModule != callModule) &&
271 |           ((callModule == null) ||
272 |           !moduleGraph.dependsOn(callModule, definitionModule))) {
273 |         return false;
274 |       }
275 |     }
276 | 
277 |     return true;
278 |   }

/**
     * Updates our respresentation of the global namespace to reflect a read
     * of a global name's longest prefix before the "prototype" property if the
     * name includes the "prototype" property. Does nothing otherwise.
     *
     * @param t The current node traversal
     * @param n The node currently being visited
     * @param parent {@code n}'s parent
     * @param name The global name (e.g. "a" or "a.b.c.d")
     * @return Whether the name was handled
     */
Method code:
781 |     boolean maybeHandlePrototypePrefix(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent,
782 |         String name) {
783 |       // We use a string-based approach instead of inspecting the parse tree
784 |       // to avoid complexities with object literals, possibly nested, beneath
785 |       // assignments.
786 | 
787 |       int numLevelsToRemove;
788 |       String prefix;
789 |       if (name.endsWith(".prototype")) {
790 |         numLevelsToRemove = 1;
791 |         prefix = name.substring(0, name.length() - 10);
792 |       } else {
793 |         int i = name.indexOf(".prototype.");
794 |         if (i == -1) {
795 |           return false;
796 |         }
797 |         prefix = name.substring(0, i);
798 |         numLevelsToRemove = 2;
799 |         i = name.indexOf('.', i + 11);
800 |         while (i >= 0) {
801 |           numLevelsToRemove++;
802 |           i = name.indexOf('.', i + 1);
803 |         }
804 |       }
805 | 
806 |       if (parent != null && NodeUtil.isObjectLitKey(n, parent)) {
807 |         // Object literal keys have no prefix that's referenced directly per
808 |         // key, so we're done.
809 |         return true;
810 |       }
811 | 
812 |       for (int i = 0; i < numLevelsToRemove; i++) {
813 |         parent = n;
814 |         n = n.getFirstChild();
815 |       }
816 | 
817 |       handleGet(t, n, parent, prefix, Ref.Type.PROTOTYPE_GET);
818 |       return true;

===== M1397 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Compiler.runCallable(Callable<T>,boolean,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Compiler.java
Original range: 594-646
Documentation:

Method code:
594 |   @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
595 |   static <T> T runCallable(
596 |       final Callable<T> callable, boolean useLargeStackThread, boolean trace) {
597 | 
598 |     // Under JRE 1.6, the jscompiler overflows the stack when running on some
599 |     // large or complex js code. Here we start a new thread with a larger
600 |     // stack in order to let the compiler do its thing, without having to
601 |     // increase the stack size for *every* thread (which is what -Xss does).
602 |     // Might want to add thread pool support for clients that compile a lot.
603 | 
604 |     final boolean dumpTraceReport = trace;
605 |     final Object[] result = new Object[1];
606 |     final Throwable[] exception = new Throwable[1];
607 |     Runnable runnable = new Runnable() {
608 |       @Override
609 |       public void run() {
610 |         try {
611 |           if (dumpTraceReport) {
612 |             Tracer.initCurrentThreadTrace();
613 |           }
614 |           result[0] = callable.call();
615 |         } catch (Throwable e) {
616 |           exception[0] = e;
617 |         } finally {
618 |           if (dumpTraceReport) {
619 |             Tracer.logAndClearCurrentThreadTrace();
620 |           }
621 |         }
622 |       }
623 |     };
624 | 
625 |     if (useLargeStackThread) {
626 |       Thread th = new Thread(null, runnable, "jscompiler", COMPILER_STACK_SIZE);
627 |       th.start();
628 |       while (true) {
629 |         try {
630 |           th.join();
631 |           break;
632 |         } catch (InterruptedException ignore) {
633 |           // ignore
634 |         }
635 |       }
636 |     } else {
637 |       runnable.run();
638 |     }
639 | 
640 |     // Pass on any exception caught by the runnable object.
641 |     if (exception[0] != null) {
642 |       throw new RuntimeException(exception[0]);
643 |     }
644 | 
645 |     return (T) result[0];
646 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.DeadAssignmentsElimination.enterScope(NodeTraversal)

70 |   @Override
71 |   public void enterScope(NodeTraversal t) {
72 |     Scope scope = t.getScope();
73 |     // Global scope _SHOULD_ work, however, liveness won't finish without
74 |     // -Xmx1024 in closure. We might have to look at coding conventions for
75 |     // exported variables as well.
76 |     if (scope.isGlobal()) {
77 |       return;
78 |     }
79 | 
80 |     if (LiveVariablesAnalysis.MAX_VARIABLES_TO_ANALYZE <
81 |         t.getScope().getVarCount()) {
82 |       return;
83 |     }
84 | 
85 |     // We are not going to do any dead assignment elimination in when there is
86 |     // at least one inner function because in most browsers, when there is a
87 |     // closure, ALL the variables are saved (escaped).
88 |     Node fnBlock = t.getScopeRoot().getLastChild();
89 |     if (NodeUtil.containsFunction(fnBlock)) {
90 |       return;
91 |     }
92 | 
93 |     // We don't do any dead assignment elimination if there are no assigns
94 |     // to eliminate. :)
95 |     if (!NodeUtil.has(fnBlock, matchRemovableAssigns,
96 |             Predicates.<Node>alwaysTrue())) {
97 |       return;
98 |     }
99 |

101 |     ControlFlowGraph<Node> cfg = t.getControlFlowGraph();
102 |     liveness = new LiveVariablesAnalysis(cfg, scope, compiler);
103 |     liveness.analyze();
104 |     tryRemoveDeadAssignments(t, cfg);
105 |   }

/**
   * Traverses a branch.
   */
Method code:
476 |   @SuppressWarnings("fallthrough")
477 |   private void traverseBranch(Node n, Node parent) {
478 |     int type = n.getType();
479 |     if (type == Token.SCRIPT) {
480 |       inputId = n.getInputId();
481 |       sourceName = getSourceName(n);
482 |     }
483 | 
484 |     curNode = n;
485 |     if (!callback.shouldTraverse(this, n, parent)) return;
486 | 
487 |     switch (type) {
488 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
489 |         traverseFunction(n, parent);
490 |         break;
491 | 
492 |       default:
493 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild(); child != null; ) {
494 |           // child could be replaced, in which case our child node
495 |           // would no longer point to the true next
496 |           Node next = child.getNext();
497 |           traverseBranch(child, n);
498 |           child = next;
499 |         }
500 |         break;
501 |     }
502 | 
503 |     curNode = n;
504 |     callback.visit(this, n, parent);
505 |   }

===== M1472 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.shouldTraverse(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 217-292
Documentation:

Method code:
217 |   @Override
218 |   public boolean shouldTraverse(
219 |       NodeTraversal nodeTraversal, Node n, Node parent) {
220 |     astPosition.put(n, astPositionCounter++);
221 | 
222 |     switch (n.getType()) {
223 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
224 |         if (shouldTraverseFunctions || n == cfg.getEntry().getValue()) {
225 |           exceptionHandler.push(n);
226 |           return true;
227 |         }
228 |         return false;
229 |       case Token.TRY:
230 |         exceptionHandler.push(n);
231 |         return true;
232 |     }
233 | 
234 |     /*
235 |      * We are going to stop the traversal depending on what the node's parent
236 |      * is.
237 |      *
238 |      * We are only interested in adding edges between nodes that change control
239 |      * flow. The most obvious ones are loops and IF-ELSE's. A statement
240 |      * transfers control to its next sibling.
241 |      *
242 |      * In case of an expression tree, there is no control flow within the tree
243 |      * even when there are short circuited operators and conditionals. When we
244 |      * are doing data flow analysis, we will simply synthesize lattices up the
245 |      * expression tree by finding the meet at each expression node.
246 |      *
247 |      * For example: within a Token.SWITCH, the expression in question does not
248 |      * change the control flow and need not to be considered.
249 |      */
250 |     if (parent != null) {
251 |       switch (parent.getType()) {
252 |         case Token.FOR:
253 |           // Only traverse the body of the for loop.
254 |           return n == parent.getLastChild();
255 | 
256 |         // Skip the conditions.
257 |         case Token.IF:
258 |         case Token.WHILE:
259 |         case Token.WITH:
260 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
261 |         case Token.DO:
262 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild().getNext();
263 |         // Only traverse the body of the cases
264 |         case Token.SWITCH:
265 |         case Token.CASE:
266 |         case Token.CATCH:
267 |         case Token.LABEL:
268 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
269 |         case Token.FUNCTION:
270 |           return n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext();
271 |         case Token.CONTINUE:
272 |         case Token.BREAK:
273 |         case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
274 |         case Token.VAR:
275 |         case Token.RETURN:
276 |         case Token.THROW:
277 |           return false;
278 |         case Token.TRY:
279 |           /* Just before we are about to visit the second child of the TRY node,
280 |            * we know that we will be visiting either the CATCH or the FINALLY.
281 |            * In other words, we know that the post order traversal of the TRY
282 |            * block has been finished, no more exceptions can be caught by the
283 |            * handler at this TRY block and should be taken out of the stack.
284 |            */
285 |           if (n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext()) {
286 |             Preconditions.checkState(exceptionHandler.peek() == parent);
287 |             exceptionHandler.pop();
288 |           }
289 |       }
290 |     }
291 |     return true;
292 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PhaseOptimizer.consume(List<PassFactory>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PhaseOptimizer.java
Original range: 123-144
Documentation:
/**
   * Add the passes generated by the given factories to the compile sequence.
   *
   * Automatically pulls multi-run passes into fixed point loops. If there
   * are 2 or more multi-run passes in a row, they will run together in
   * the same fixed point loop. If A and B are in the same fixed point loop,
   * the loop will continue to run both A and B until both are finished
   * making changes.
   *
   * Other than that, the PhaseOptimizer is free to tweak the order and
   * frequency of multi-run passes in a fixed-point loop.
   */
Method code:
123 |   void consume(List<PassFactory> factories) {
124 |     Loop currentLoop = new LoopInternal();
125 |     boolean isCurrentLoopPopulated = false;
126 |     for (PassFactory factory : factories) {
127 |       if (factory.isOneTimePass()) {
128 |         if (isCurrentLoopPopulated) {
129 |           passes.add(currentLoop);
130 | 
131 |           currentLoop = new LoopInternal();
132 |           isCurrentLoopPopulated = false;
133 |         }
134 |         addOneTimePass(factory);
135 |       } else {
136 |         currentLoop.addLoopedPass(factory);
137 |         isCurrentLoopPopulated = true;
138 |       }
139 |     }
140 | 
141 |     if (isCurrentLoopPopulated) {
142 |       passes.add(currentLoop);
143 |     }
144 |   }
