===== M1502 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NameAnalyzer.valueConsumedByParent(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NameAnalyzer.java
Original range: 1714-1737
Documentation:
/**
   * Determine if the parent reads the value of a child expression
   * directly.  This is true children used in predicates, RETURN
   * statements and, rhs of variable declarations and assignments.
   *
   * In the case of:
   * if (a) b else c
   *
   * This method returns true for "a", and false for "b" and "c": the
   * IF expression does something special based on "a"'s value.  "b"
   * and "c" are effectivelly outputs.  Same logic applies to FOR,
   * WHILE and DO loop predicates.  AND/OR/HOOK expressions are
   * syntactic sugar for IF statements; therefore this method returns
   * true for the predicate and false otherwise.
   */
Method code:
1714 |   private boolean valueConsumedByParent(Node n, Node parent) {
1715 |     if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(parent)) {
1716 |       return parent.getLastChild() == n;
1717 |     }
1718 | 
1719 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
1720 |       case Token.NAME:
1721 |       case Token.RETURN:
1722 |         return true;
1723 |       case Token.AND:
1724 |       case Token.OR:
1725 |       case Token.HOOK:
1726 |         return parent.getFirstChild() == n;
1727 |       case Token.FOR:
1728 |         return parent.getFirstChild().getNext() == n;
1729 |       case Token.IF:
1730 |       case Token.WHILE:
1731 |         return parent.getFirstChild() == n;
1732 |       case Token.DO:
1733 |         return parent.getLastChild() == n;
1734 |       default:
1735 |         return false;
1736 |     }
1737 |   }

/**
   * Eliminate parameters if they are always constant.
   *
   * function foo(a, b) {...}
   * foo(1,2);
   * foo(1,3)
   * becomes
   * function foo(b) { var a = 1 ... }
   * foo(2);
   * foo(3);
   */
Method code:
184 |   private void tryEliminateConstantArgs(
185 |       DefinitionSite defSite, SimpleDefinitionFinder defFinder) {
186 | 
187 |     List<Parameter> parameters = Lists.newArrayList();
188 |     boolean firstCall = true;
189 | 
190 |     // Build a list of parameters to remove
191 |     Definition definition = defSite.definition;
192 |     Collection<UseSite> useSites = defFinder.getUseSites(definition);
193 |     boolean continueLooking = false;
194 |     for (UseSite site : useSites) {
195 |       Preconditions.checkState(SimpleDefinitionFinder.isCallOrNewSite(site));
196 |       Node call = site.node.getParent();
197 | 
198 |       Node cur = call.getFirstChild();
199 |       if (firstCall) {
200 |         // Use the first call to construct a list of parameters of the
201 |         // function.
202 |         continueLooking = buildParameterList(parameters, cur, site.scope);
203 |         firstCall = false;
204 |       } else {
205 |         continueLooking= findFixedParameters(parameters, cur);
206 |       }
207 |       if (!continueLooking) {
208 |         return;
209 |       }
210 |     }
211 | 
212 |     continueLooking = adjustForSideEffects(parameters);
213 |     if (!continueLooking) {
214 |       return;
215 |     }
216 | 
217 |     // Remove the constant parameters in all the calls
218 |     for (UseSite site : useSites) {
219 |       Preconditions.checkState(SimpleDefinitionFinder.isCallOrNewSite(site));
220 |       Node call = site.node.getParent();

/** Re-arrange the passes in an optimal order. */
Method code:
385 |     private void optimizePasses() {
386 |       // It's important that this ordering is deterministic, so that
387 |       // multiple compiles with the same input produce exactly the same
388 |       // results.
389 |       //
390 |       // To do this, grab any passes we recognize, and move them to the end
391 |       // in an "optimal" order.

396 |             optimalPasses.add(pass);
397 |             break;
398 |           }
399 |         }
400 |       }
401 | 
402 |       myPasses.removeAll(optimalPasses);
403 |       myPasses.addAll(optimalPasses);
404 |     }

129 |     @Override
130 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
131 |       // Skipping over non-name nodes and empty function names.
132 |       if (!NodeUtil.isReferenceName(n)) {
133 |         return;
134 |       }
135 | 
136 |       // We focus on shadowing local variables as their name occurs much more
137 |       // than global names.

151 |         // We will not shadow a global variable name.
152 |         return;

159 |           scopeUpRefMap.put(s.getRootNode(), var.name);

164 |         scopeUpRefMap.put(t.getScopeRoot(), var.name);
165 |       }
166 |

168 |       varToNameUsage.put(var, n);

128 |     @Override
129 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
130 |       switch (n.getType()) {
131 |         case Token.GETPROP:
132 |         case Token.GETELEM: {
133 |           Node dest = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
134 | 
135 |           if (!dest.isString()) {
136 |             return;
137 |           }
138 | 
139 |           String name = dest.getString();
140 | 
141 |           // We have a signature. Parse tree of the form:
142 |           // assign                       <- parent
143 |           //      getprop                 <- n
144 |           //          name methods
145 |           //          string setTimeout
146 |           //      function
147 |           if (parent.isAssign() &&
148 |               parent.getFirstChild() == n &&
149 |               n.getNext().isFunction()) {
150 |             addSignature(name, n.getNext(), t.getSourceName());
151 |           } else {
152 |             getSignatureStore().removeSignature(name);
153 |             externMethodsWithoutSignatures.add(name);
154 |           }
155 | 
156 |           externMethods.add(name);
157 |         } break;
158 | 
159 |         case Token.OBJECTLIT: {
160 |           for (Node key = n.getFirstChild(); key != null; key = key.getNext()) {
161 |             Node value = key.getFirstChild();
162 |             String name = key.getString();
163 |             if (key.isString()
164 |                 && value.isFunction()) {
165 |               addSignature(name, value, t.getSourceName());
166 |             } else {
167 |               getSignatureStore().removeSignature(name);
168 |               externMethodsWithoutSignatures.add(name);
169 |             }
170 |             externMethods.add(name);
171 |           }
172 |         } break;
173 |       }
174 |     }

60 |       }
61 |       Node value = getValue(child);
62 |       if (value == null || !isInterestingValue(value)) {
63 |         // No initializer or not an Object or Array literal.
64 |         continue;
65 |       }
66 | 
67 |       Node propertyCandidate;
68 |       while ((propertyCandidate = child.getNext()) != null) {
69 |         // This does not infinitely loop because collectProperty always
70 |         // removes propertyCandidate from its parent when it returns true.
71 |         if (!collectProperty(propertyCandidate, name.getString(), value)) {
72 |           break;
73 |         }
74 |         codeChanged = true;
75 |       }
76 |     }
77 | 
78 |     if (codeChanged) {
79 |       reportCodeChange();
80 |     }
81 |     return subtree;
82 |   }

/**
     * Determines whether a set operation is a constructor or enumeration
     * declaration. The set operation may either be an assignment to a name,
     * a variable declaration, or an object literal key mapping.
     *
     * @param n The node that represents the name being set
     * @param parent Parent node of {@code n} (an ASSIGN, VAR, or OBJLIT node)
     * @return Whether the set operation is either a constructor or enum
     *     declaration
     */
Method code:
577 |     private boolean isConstructorOrEnumDeclaration(Node n, Node parent) {

580 |       switch (parent.getType()) {
581 |         case Token.ASSIGN:
582 |           info = parent.getJSDocInfo();
583 |           valueNodeType = n.getNext().getType();
584 |           break;
585 |         case Token.VAR:
586 |           info = n.getJSDocInfo();
587 |           if (info == null) {

589 |           }
590 |           Node valueNode = n.getFirstChild();

592 |           break;
593 |         default:

595 |             info = parent.getJSDocInfo();

597 |             break;
598 |           }
599 |           return false;
600 |       }
601 |       // Heed the annotations only if they're sensibly used.
602 |       return info != null &&
603 |              (info.isConstructor() && valueNodeType == Token.FUNCTION ||
604 |               info.hasEnumParameterType() && valueNodeType == Token.OBJECTLIT);

===== M1563 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NameAnalyzer.referenceAliases()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NameAnalyzer.java
Original range: 1270-1279
Documentation:
/**
   * The NameAnalyzer algorithm works best when all objects have a canonical
   * name in the global scope. When multiple names in the global scope
   * point to the same object, things start to break down.
   *
   * For example, if we have
   * <code>
   * var a = {};
   * var b = a;
   * a.foo = 3;
   * alert(b.foo);
   * </code>
   * then a.foo and b.foo are the same name, even though NameAnalyzer doesn't
   * represent them as such.
   *
   * To handle this case, we look at all the aliases in the program.
   * If descendant properties of that alias are assigned, then we create a
   * directional reference from the original name to the alias. For example,
   * in this case, the assign to {@code a.foo} triggers a reference from
   * {@code b} to {@code a}, but NOT from a to b.
   *
   * Similarly, "instanceof" checks do not prevent the removal
   * of a unaliased name but an instanceof check on an alias can only be removed
   * if the other aliases are also removed, so we add a connection here.
   */
Method code:
1270 |   private void referenceAliases() {
1271 |     for (Map.Entry<String, AliasSet> entry : aliases.entrySet()) {
1272 |       JsName name = getName(entry.getKey(), false);
1273 |       if (name.hasWrittenDescendants || name.hasInstanceOfReference) {
1274 |         for (String alias : entry.getValue().names) {
1275 |           recordReference(alias, entry.getKey(), RefType.REGULAR);
1276 |         }
1277 |       }
1278 |     }
1279 |   }

/**
   * Parses a {@link JSDocInfo} object. This parsing method reads all tokens
   * returned by the {@link JsDocTokenStream#getJsDocToken()} method until the

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.SyntacticScopeCreator.scanVars(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/SyntacticScopeCreator.java
Original range: 124-178
Documentation:
/**
   * Scans and gather variables declarations under a Node
   */
Method code:
124 |   private void scanVars(Node n, Node parent) {
125 |     switch (n.getType()) {
126 |       case Token.VAR:
127 |         // Declare all variables. e.g. var x = 1, y, z;
128 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild();
129 |              child != null;) {
130 |           Node next = child.getNext();
131 |           declareVar(child);
132 |           child = next;
133 |         }
134 |         return;
135 | 
136 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
137 |         if (NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(n)) {
138 |           return;
139 |         }
140 | 
141 |         String fnName = n.getFirstChild().getString();
142 |         if (fnName.isEmpty()) {
143 |           // This is invalid, but allow it so the checks can catch it.
144 |           return;
145 |         }
146 |         declareVar(n.getFirstChild());
147 |         return;   // should not examine function's children
148 | 
149 |       case Token.CATCH:
150 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 2);
151 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.getFirstChild().isName());
152 |         // the first child is the catch var and the third child
153 |         // is the code block
154 | 
155 |         final Node var = n.getFirstChild();
156 |         final Node block = var.getNext();
157 | 
158 |         declareVar(var);
159 |         scanVars(block, n);
160 |         return;  // only one child to scan
161 | 
162 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
163 |         inputId = n.getInputId();
164 |         Preconditions.checkNotNull(inputId);
165 |         break;
166 |     }
167 | 
168 |     // Variables can only occur in statement-level nodes, so
169 |     // we only need to traverse children in a couple special cases.
170 |     if (NodeUtil.isControlStructure(n) || NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(n)) {
171 |       for (Node child = n.getFirstChild();
172 |            child != null;) {
173 |         Node next = child.getNext();
174 |         scanVars(child, n);
175 |         child = next;
176 |       }
177 |     }
178 |   }

/**
     * Transforms the given node and then sets its type to Token.STRING if it
     * was Token.NAME. If its type was already Token.STRING, then quotes it.
     * Used for properties, as the old AST uses String tokens, while the new one
     * uses Name tokens for unquoted strings. For example, in
     * var o = {'a' : 1, b: 2};
     * the string 'a' is quoted, while the name b is turned into a string, but
     * unquoted.
     */

===== M1627 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Normalize.NormalizeStatements.extractForInitializer(Node,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Normalize.java
Original range: 495-542
Documentation:
/**
     * Bring the initializers out of FOR loops.  These need to be placed
     * before any associated LABEL nodes. This needs to be done from the top
     * level label first so this is called as a pre-order callback (from
     * shouldTraverse).
     *
     * @param n The node to inspect.
     * @param before The node to insert the initializer before.
     * @param beforeParent The parent of the node before which the initializer
     *     will be inserted.
     */
Method code:
495 |     private void extractForInitializer(
496 |         Node n, Node before, Node beforeParent) {
497 | 
498 |       for (Node next, c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = next) {
499 |         next = c.getNext();
500 |         Node insertBefore = (before == null) ? c : before;
501 |         Node insertBeforeParent = (before == null) ? n : beforeParent;
502 |         switch (c.getType()) {
503 |           case Token.LABEL:
504 |             extractForInitializer(c, insertBefore, insertBeforeParent);
505 |             break;
506 |           case Token.FOR:
507 |             if (NodeUtil.isForIn(c)) {
508 |               Node first = c.getFirstChild();
509 |               if (first.isVar()) {
510 |                 // Transform:
511 |                 //    for (var a = 1 in b) {}
512 |                 // to:
513 |                 //    var a = 1; for (a in b) {};
514 |                 Node newStatement = first;
515 |                 // Clone just the node, to remove any initialization.
516 |                 Node name = newStatement.getFirstChild().cloneNode();
517 |                 first.getParent().replaceChild(first, name);
518 |                 insertBeforeParent.addChildBefore(newStatement, insertBefore);
519 |                 reportCodeChange("FOR-IN var declaration");
520 |               }
521 |             } else if (!c.getFirstChild().isEmpty()) {
522 |               Node init = c.getFirstChild();
523 |               Node empty = IR.empty();
524 |               empty.copyInformationFrom(c);
525 |               c.replaceChild(init, empty);
526 | 
527 |               Node newStatement;
528 |               // Only VAR statements, and expressions are allowed,
529 |               // but are handled differently.
530 |               if (init.isVar()) {
531 |                 newStatement = init;
532 |               } else {
533 |                 newStatement = NodeUtil.newExpr(init);
534 |               }
535 | 
536 |               insertBeforeParent.addChildBefore(newStatement, insertBefore);
537 |               reportCodeChange("FOR initializer");
538 |             }
539 |             break;
540 |         }
541 |       }
542 |     }

===== M1639 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.connectToPossibleExceptionHandler(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 828-855
Documentation:
/**
   * Connects cfgNode to the proper CATCH block if target subtree might throw
   * an exception. If there are FINALLY blocks reached before a CATCH, it will
   * make the corresponding entry in finallyMap.
   */
Method code:
828 |   private void connectToPossibleExceptionHandler(Node cfgNode, Node target) {
829 |     if (mayThrowException(target) && !exceptionHandler.isEmpty()) {
830 |       Node lastJump = cfgNode;
831 |       for (Node handler : exceptionHandler) {
832 |         if (handler.isFunction()) {
833 |           return;
834 |         }
835 |         Preconditions.checkState(handler.isTry());
836 |         Node catchBlock = NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(handler);
837 | 
838 |         if (!NodeUtil.hasCatchHandler(catchBlock)) { // No catch but a FINALLY.
839 |           if (lastJump == cfgNode) {
840 |             createEdge(cfgNode, Branch.ON_EX, handler.getLastChild());
841 |           } else {
842 |             finallyMap.put(lastJump, handler.getLastChild());
843 |           }
844 |         } else { // Has a catch.
845 |           if (lastJump == cfgNode) {
846 |             createEdge(cfgNode, Branch.ON_EX, catchBlock);
847 |             return;
848 |           } else {
849 |             finallyMap.put(lastJump, catchBlock);
850 |           }
851 |         }
852 |         lastJump = handler;
853 |       }
854 |     }
855 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ReferenceCollectingCallback.BasicBlock.provablyExecutesBefore(BasicBlock)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ReferenceCollectingCallback.java
Original range: 703-722
Documentation:
/**
     * Determines whether this block is guaranteed to begin executing before
     * the given block does.
     */
Method code:
703 |     boolean provablyExecutesBefore(BasicBlock thatBlock) {
704 |       // If thatBlock is a descendant of this block, and there are no hoisted
705 |       // blocks between them, then this block must start before thatBlock.
706 |       BasicBlock currentBlock;
707 |       for (currentBlock = thatBlock;
708 |            currentBlock != null && currentBlock != this;
709 |            currentBlock = currentBlock.getParent()) {
710 |         if (currentBlock.isHoisted) {
711 |           return false;
712 |         }
713 |       }
714 | 
715 |       if (currentBlock == this) {
716 |         return true;
717 |       }
718 |       if (isGlobalScopeBlock() && thatBlock.isGlobalScopeBlock()) {
719 |         return true;
720 |       }
721 |       return false;
722 |     }

===== M1661 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.MethodCompilerPass.GatherSignatures.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/MethodCompilerPass.java
Original range: 182-226
Documentation:

Method code:
182 |     @Override
183 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
184 |       switch (n.getType()) {
185 |         case Token.GETPROP:
186 |         case Token.GETELEM:
187 |           Node dest = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
188 | 
189 |           if (dest.isString()) {
190 |             if (dest.getString().equals("prototype")) {
191 |               processPrototypeParent(t, parent);
192 |             } else {
193 |               // Static methods of the form Foo.bar = function() {} or
194 |               // Static methods of the form Foo.bar = baz (where baz is a
195 |               // function name). Parse tree looks like:
196 |               // assign                 <- parent
197 |               //      getprop           <- n
198 |               //          name Foo
199 |               //          string bar
200 |               //      function or name  <- n.getNext()
201 |               if (parent.isAssign() &&
202 |                   parent.getFirstChild() == n) {
203 |                 addPossibleSignature(dest.getString(), n.getNext(), t);
204 |               }
205 |             }
206 |           }
207 |           break;
208 | 
209 |         case Token.OBJECTLIT:
210 |           for (Node key = n.getFirstChild(); key != null; key = key.getNext()) {
211 |             switch(key.getType()) {
212 |               case Token.STRING:
213 |                 addPossibleSignature(key.getString(), key.getFirstChild(), t);
214 |                 break;
215 |               case Token.SETTER_DEF:
216 |               case Token.GETTER_DEF:
217 |                 nonMethodProperties.add(key.getString());
218 |                 break;
219 |               default:
220 |                 throw new IllegalStateException(
221 |                     "unexpect OBJECTLIT key: " + key);
222 |             }
223 |           }
224 |           break;
225 |       }
226 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeFoldConstants.tryFoldGetProp(Node,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeFoldConstants.java
Original range: 1372-1407
Documentation:
/**
   * Try to fold array-length. e.g [1, 2, 3].length ==> 3, [x, y].length ==> 2
   */
Method code:
1372 |   private Node tryFoldGetProp(Node n, Node left, Node right) {
1373 |     Preconditions.checkArgument(n.isGetProp());
1374 | 
1375 |     if (left.isObjectLit()) {
1376 |       return tryFoldObjectPropAccess(n, left, right);
1377 |     }
1378 | 
1379 |     if (right.isString() &&
1380 |         right.getString().equals("length")) {
1381 |       int knownLength = -1;
1382 |       switch (left.getType()) {
1383 |         case Token.ARRAYLIT:
1384 |           if (mayHaveSideEffects(left)) {
1385 |             // Nope, can't fold this, without handling the side-effects.
1386 |             return n;
1387 |           }
1388 |           knownLength = left.getChildCount();
1389 |           break;
1390 |         case Token.STRING:
1391 |           knownLength = left.getString().length();
1392 |           break;
1393 |         default:
1394 |           // Not a foldable case, forget it.
1395 |           return n;
1396 |       }
1397 | 
1398 |       Preconditions.checkState(knownLength != -1);
1399 |       Node lengthNode = IR.number(knownLength);
1400 |       n.getParent().replaceChild(n, lengthNode);
1401 |       reportCodeChange();
1402 | 
1403 |       return lengthNode;
1404 |     }
1405 | 
1406 |     return n;
1407 |   }

648 |   private void compileInternal() {

650 |     parse();
651 |     // 15 percent of the work is assumed to be for parsing (based on some
652 |     // minimal analysis on big JS projects, of course this depends on options)
653 |     setProgress(0.15);

655 |       return;
656 |     }

659 |       return;

665 |       return;

669 |       check();
670 |       if (hasErrors()) {
671 |         return;
672 |       }
673 |

675 |           || options.externExportsPath != null) {
676 |         externExports();
677 |       }
678 | 
679 |       // IDE-mode is defined to stop here, before the heavy rewriting begins.
680 |       if (!options.ideMode) {
681 |         optimize();
682 |       }
683 |     }
684 | 
685 |     if (options.recordFunctionInformation) {
686 |       recordFunctionInformation();
687 |     }
688 | 
689 |     if (options.devMode == DevMode.START_AND_END) {
690 |       runSanityCheck();
691 |     }
692 |     setProgress(1.0);
693 |   }

/**
   * Runs through all namespaces (prefixes of classes and enums), and checks if
   * any of them have been used in an unsafe way.
   */
Method code:
249 |   private void checkNamespaces() {
250 |     for (Name name : nameMap.values()) {
251 |       if (name.isNamespace() &&
252 |           (name.aliasingGets > 0 || name.localSets + name.globalSets > 1 ||
253 |            name.deleteProps > 0)) {
254 |         boolean initialized = name.getDeclaration() != null;

256 |           if (ref == name.getDeclaration()) {
257 |             continue;

259 |

261 |             if (initialized) {
262 |               warnAboutNamespaceRedefinition(name, ref);
263 |             }
264 |           } else if (
265 |               ref.type == Ref.Type.SET_FROM_GLOBAL ||
266 |               ref.type == Ref.Type.SET_FROM_LOCAL) {
267 |             if (initialized) {
268 |               warnAboutNamespaceRedefinition(name, ref);
269 |             }
270 | 
271 |             initialized = true;
272 |           } else if (ref.type == Ref.Type.ALIASING_GET) {

===== M1728 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowGraph.isEnteringNewCfgNode(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowGraph.java
Original range: 151-195
Documentation:
/**
   * @return True if n should be represented by a new CFG node in the control
   * flow graph.
   */
Method code:
151 |   public static boolean isEnteringNewCfgNode(Node n) {
152 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
153 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
154 |       case Token.BLOCK:
155 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
156 |       case Token.TRY:
157 |         return true;
158 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
159 |         // A function node represents the start of a function where the name
160 |         // is bleed into the local scope and parameters has been assigned
161 |         // to the formal argument names. The node includes the name of the
162 |         // function and the LP list since we assume the whole set up process
163 |         // is atomic without change in control flow. The next change of
164 |         // control is going into the function's body represent by the second
165 |         // child.
166 |         return n != parent.getFirstChild().getNext();
167 |       case Token.WHILE:
168 |       case Token.DO:
169 |       case Token.IF:
170 |         // Theses control structure is represented by its node that holds the
171 |         // condition. Each of them is a branch node based on its condition.
172 |         return NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(parent) != n;
173 | 
174 |       case Token.FOR:
175 |         // The FOR(;;) node differs from other control structure in that
176 |         // it has a initialization and a increment statement. Those
177 |         // two statements have its corresponding CFG nodes to represent them.
178 |         // The FOR node represents the condition check for each iteration.
179 |         // That way the following:
180 |         // for(var x = 0; x < 10; x++) { } has a graph that is isomorphic to
181 |         // var x = 0; while(x<10) {  x++; }
182 |         if (NodeUtil.isForIn(parent)) {
183 |           return n == parent.getLastChild();
184 |         } else {
185 |           return NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(parent) != n;
186 |         }
187 |       case Token.SWITCH:
188 |       case Token.CASE:
189 |       case Token.CATCH:
190 |       case Token.WITH:
191 |         return n != parent.getFirstChild();
192 |       default:
193 |         return false;
194 |     }
195 |   }

/**
   * Is a FUNCTION node an function expression? An function expression is one
   * that has either no name or a name that is not added to the current scope.
   *
   * <p>Some examples of function expressions:
   * <pre>
   * (function () {})
   * (function f() {})()
   * [ function f() {} ]
   * var f = function f() {};
   * for (function f() {};;) {}
   * </pre>
   *
   * <p>Some examples of functions that are <em>not</em> expressions:
   * <pre>
   * function f() {}
   * if (x); else function f() {}
   * for (;;) { function f() {} }
   * </pre>
   *
   * @param n A node
   * @return Whether n is an function used within an expression.
   */
Method code:
1902 |   static boolean isFunctionExpression(Node n) {
1903 |     return n.isFunction() && !isStatement(n);
1904 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.VarCheck.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/VarCheck.java
Original range: 120-203
Documentation:

Method code:
120 |   @Override
121 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
122 |     if (!n.isName()) {
123 |       return;
124 |     }
125 | 
126 |     String varName = n.getString();
127 | 
128 |     // Only a function can have an empty name.
129 |     if (varName.isEmpty()) {
130 |       Preconditions.checkState(parent.isFunction());
131 |       Preconditions.checkState(NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(parent));
132 |       return;
133 |     }
134 | 
135 |     // Check if this is a declaration for a var that has been declared
136 |     // elsewhere. If so, mark it as a duplicate.
137 |     if ((parent.isVar() ||
138 |          NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(parent)) &&
139 |         varsToDeclareInExterns.contains(varName)) {
140 |       createSynthesizedExternVar(varName);
141 | 
142 |       n.addSuppression("duplicate");
143 |     }
144 | 
145 |     // Check that the var has been declared.
146 |     Scope scope = t.getScope();
147 |     Scope.Var var = scope.getVar(varName);
148 |     if (var == null) {
149 |       if (NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(parent)) {
150 |         // e.g. [ function foo() {} ], it's okay if "foo" isn't defined in the
151 |         // current scope.
152 |       } else {
153 |         // The extern checks are stricter, don't report a second error.
154 |         if (!strictExternCheck || !t.getInput().isExtern()) {
155 |           t.report(n, UNDEFINED_VAR_ERROR, varName);
156 |         }
157 | 
158 |         if (sanityCheck) {
159 |           throw new IllegalStateException("Unexpected variable " + varName);
160 |         } else {
161 |           createSynthesizedExternVar(varName);
162 |           scope.getGlobalScope().declare(varName, n,
163 |               null, getSynthesizedExternsInput());
164 |         }
165 |       }
166 |       return;
167 |     }
168 | 
169 |     CompilerInput currInput = t.getInput();
170 |     CompilerInput varInput = var.input;
171 |     if (currInput == varInput || currInput == null || varInput == null) {
172 |       // The variable was defined in the same file. This is fine.
173 |       return;
174 |     }
175 | 
176 |     // Check module dependencies.
177 |     JSModule currModule = currInput.getModule();
178 |     JSModule varModule = varInput.getModule();
179 |     JSModuleGraph moduleGraph = compiler.getModuleGraph();
180 |     if (!sanityCheck &&
181 |         varModule != currModule && varModule != null && currModule != null) {
182 |       if (moduleGraph.dependsOn(currModule, varModule)) {
183 |         // The module dependency was properly declared.
184 |       } else {
185 |         if (scope.isGlobal()) {
186 |           if (moduleGraph.dependsOn(varModule, currModule)) {
187 |             // The variable reference violates a declared module dependency.
188 |             t.report(n, VIOLATED_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
189 |                      currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
190 |           } else {
191 |             // The variable reference is between two modules that have no
192 |             // dependency relationship. This should probably be considered an
193 |             // error, but just issue a warning for now.
194 |             t.report(n, MISSING_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
195 |                      currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
196 |           }
197 |         } else {
198 |           t.report(n, STRICT_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
199 |                    currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
200 |         }
201 |       }
202 |     }
203 |   }

===== M1753 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode(Node,Node,ControlFlowAnalysis)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 690-787
Documentation:
/**
   * Computes the follow() node of a given node and its parent. There is a side
   * effect when calling this function. If this function computed an edge that
   * exists a FINALLY, it'll attempt to connect the fromNode to the outer
   * FINALLY according to the finallyMap.
   *
   * @param fromNode The original source node since {@code node} is changed
   *        during recursion.
   * @param node The node that follow() should compute.
   */
Method code:
690 |   private static Node computeFollowNode(
691 |       Node fromNode, Node node, ControlFlowAnalysis cfa) {
692 |     /*
693 |      * This is the case where:
694 |      *
695 |      * 1. Parent is null implies that we are transferring control to the end of
696 |      * the script.
697 |      *
698 |      * 2. Parent is a function implies that we are transferring control back to
699 |      * the caller of the function.
700 |      *
701 |      * 3. If the node is a return statement, we should also transfer control
702 |      * back to the caller of the function.
703 |      *
704 |      * 4. If the node is root then we have reached the end of what we have been
705 |      * asked to traverse.
706 |      *
707 |      * In all cases we should transfer control to a "symbolic return" node.
708 |      * This will make life easier for DFAs.
709 |      */
710 |     Node parent = node.getParent();
711 |     if (parent == null || parent.isFunction() ||
712 |         (cfa != null && node == cfa.root)) {
713 |       return null;
714 |     }
715 | 
716 |     // If we are just before a IF/WHILE/DO/FOR:
717 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
718 |       // The follow() of any of the path from IF would be what follows IF.
719 |       case Token.IF:
720 |         return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
721 |       case Token.CASE:
722 |       case Token.DEFAULT_CASE:
723 |         // After the body of a CASE, the control goes to the body of the next
724 |         // case, without having to go to the case condition.
725 |         if (parent.getNext() != null) {
726 |           if (parent.getNext().isCase()) {
727 |             return parent.getNext().getFirstChild().getNext();
728 |           } else if (parent.getNext().isDefaultCase()) {
729 |             return parent.getNext().getFirstChild();
730 |           } else {
731 |             Preconditions.checkState(false, "Not reachable");
732 |           }
733 |         } else {
734 |           return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
735 |         }
736 |         break;
737 |       case Token.FOR:
738 |         if (NodeUtil.isForIn(parent)) {
739 |           return parent;
740 |         } else {
741 |           return parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext();
742 |         }
743 |       case Token.WHILE:
744 |       case Token.DO:
745 |         return parent;
746 |       case Token.TRY:
747 |         // If we are coming out of the TRY block...
748 |         if (parent.getFirstChild() == node) {
749 |           if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(parent)) { // and have FINALLY block.
750 |             return computeFallThrough(parent.getLastChild());
751 |           } else { // and have no FINALLY.
752 |             return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
753 |           }
754 |         // CATCH block.
755 |         } else if (NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(parent) == node){
756 |           if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(parent)) { // and have FINALLY block.
757 |             return computeFallThrough(node.getNext());
758 |           } else {
759 |             return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
760 |           }
761 |         // If we are coming out of the FINALLY block...
762 |         } else if (parent.getLastChild() == node){
763 |           if (cfa != null) {
764 |             for (Node finallyNode : cfa.finallyMap.get(parent)) {
765 |               cfa.createEdge(fromNode, Branch.UNCOND, finallyNode);
766 |             }
767 |           }
768 |           return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
769 |         }
770 |     }
771 | 
772 |     // Now that we are done with the special cases follow should be its
773 |     // immediate sibling, unless its sibling is a function
774 |     Node nextSibling = node.getNext();
775 | 
776 |     // Skip function declarations because control doesn't get pass into it.
777 |     while (nextSibling != null && nextSibling.isFunction()) {
778 |       nextSibling = nextSibling.getNext();
779 |     }
780 | 
781 |     if (nextSibling != null) {
782 |       return computeFallThrough(nextSibling);
783 |     } else {
784 |       // If there are no more siblings, control is transfered up the AST.
785 |       return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
786 |     }
787 |   }

122 |     //  - a simple assignment (x.a = 1)
123 |     //  - a compound assignment or increment (x++, x += 1) whose result is
124 |     //    otherwise unused
125 | 
126 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
127 |     if (n == parent.getFirstChild()) {
128 |       if (parent.isAssign()) {
129 |         // A simple assignment doesn't pin the property.
130 |         return false;
131 |       } else if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(parent)
132 |             || parent.isInc() || parent.isDec()) {
133 |         // In general, compound assignments are both reads and writes, but
134 |         // if the property is never otherwise read we can consider it simply
135 |         // a write.
136 |         // However if the assign expression is used as part of a larger
137 |         // expression, we much consider it a read. For example:
138 |         //    x = (y.a += 1);
139 |         return NodeUtil.isExpressionResultUsed(parent);
140 |       }
141 |     }
142 |     return true;
143 |   }

306 |   boolean canModifyDefinition(Definition definition) {
307 |     if (isExported(definition)) {
308 |       return false;
309 |     }
310 | 
311 |     // Don't modify unused definitions for two reasons:
312 |     // 1) It causes unnecessary churn
313 |     // 2) Other definitions might be used to reflect on this one using
314 |     //    goog.reflect.object (the check for definitions with uses is below).
315 |     Collection<UseSite> useSites = getUseSites(definition);
316 |     if (useSites.isEmpty()) {
317 |       return false;
318 |     }
319 | 
320 |     for (UseSite site : useSites) {
321 |       // This catches the case where an object literal in goog.reflect.object
322 |       // and a prototype method have the same property name.
323 | 
324 |       // NOTE(nicksantos): Maps and trogedit both do this by different
325 |       // mechanisms.
326 |

328 |       Collection<Definition> singleSiteDefinitions =
329 |           getDefinitionsReferencedAt(nameNode);
330 |       if (singleSiteDefinitions.size() > 1) {
331 |         return false;
332 |       }
333 | 
334 |       Preconditions.checkState(!singleSiteDefinitions.isEmpty());
335 |       Preconditions.checkState(singleSiteDefinitions.contains(definition));
336 |     }

339 |   }

/**
   * Parses the JavaScript text given by a reader.

104 |   public static Node parse(StaticSourceFile sourceFile,
105 |                            String sourceString,

107 |                            ErrorReporter errorReporter,

109 |     Context cx = Context.enter();

111 |     cx.setLanguageVersion(Context.VERSION_1_5);
112 |     CompilerEnvirons compilerEnv = new CompilerEnvirons();
113 |     compilerEnv.initFromContext(cx);
114 |     compilerEnv.setRecordingComments(true);
115 |     compilerEnv.setRecordingLocalJsDocComments(true);

135 |     } catch (EvaluatorException e) {

===== M1855 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.FunctionRewriter.process(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/FunctionRewriter.java
Original range: 57-104
Documentation:

Method code:
57 |   @Override
58 |   public void process(Node externs, Node root) {
59 |     List<Reducer> reducers = ImmutableList.of(new ReturnConstantReducer(),
60 |                                               new GetterReducer(),
61 |                                               new SetterReducer(),
62 |                                               new EmptyFunctionReducer(),
63 |                                               new IdentityReducer());
64 | 
65 |     Multimap<Reducer, Reduction> reductionMap = HashMultimap.create();
66 | 
67 |     // Accumulate possible reductions in the reduction multi map.  They
68 |     // will be applied in the loop below.
69 |     NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, root,
70 |                            new ReductionGatherer(reducers, reductionMap));
71 | 
72 |     // Apply reductions iff they will provide some savings.
73 |     for (Reducer reducer : reducers) {
74 |       Collection<Reduction> reductions = reductionMap.get(reducer);
75 |       if (reductions.isEmpty()) {
76 |         continue;
77 |       }
78 | 
79 |       Node helperCode = parseHelperCode(reducer);
80 |       if (helperCode == null) {
81 |         continue;
82 |       }
83 | 
84 |       int helperCodeCost = InlineCostEstimator.getCost(helperCode);
85 | 
86 |       // Estimate savings
87 |       int savings = 0;
88 |       for (Reduction reduction : reductions) {
89 |         savings += reduction.estimateSavings();
90 |       }
91 | 
92 |       // Compare estimated savings against the helper cost.  Apply
93 |       // reductions if doing so will result in some savings.
94 |       if (savings > (helperCodeCost + SAVINGS_THRESHOLD)) {
95 |         for (Reduction reduction : reductions) {
96 |           reduction.apply();
97 |         }
98 | 
99 |         Node addingRoot = compiler.getNodeForCodeInsertion(null);
100 |         addingRoot.addChildrenToFront(helperCode);
101 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
102 |       }
103 |     }
104 |   }

Method code:
227 |   private Node tryFoldImmediateCallToBoundFunction(Node n) {
228 |     // Rewriting "(fn.bind(a,b))()" to "fn.call(a,b)" makes it inlinable
229 |     Preconditions.checkState(n.isCall());
230 |     Node callTarget = n.getFirstChild();
231 |     Bind bind = getCodingConvention().describeFunctionBind(callTarget);
232 |     if (bind != null) {
233 |       // replace the call target
234 |       bind.target.detachFromParent();
235 |       n.replaceChild(callTarget, bind.target);
236 |       callTarget = bind.target;
237 | 
238 |       // push the parameters
239 |       addParameterAfter(bind.parameters, callTarget);
240 | 
241 |       // add the this value before the parameters if necessary
242 |       if (bind.thisValue != null && !NodeUtil.isUndefined(bind.thisValue)) {
243 |         // rewrite from "fn(a, b)" to "fn.call(thisValue, a, b)"
244 |         Node newCallTarget = IR.getprop(
245 |             callTarget.cloneTree(),
246 |             IR.string("call").srcref(callTarget));
247 |         n.replaceChild(callTarget, newCallTarget);
248 |         n.addChildAfter(bind.thisValue.cloneTree(), newCallTarget);
249 |         n.putBooleanProp(Node.FREE_CALL, false);
250 |       } else {
251 |         n.putBooleanProp(Node.FREE_CALL, true);
252 |       }
253 |       reportCodeChange();
254 |     }
255 |     return n;
256 |   }

===== M1863 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CodeGenerator.add(Node,Context)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CodeGenerator.java
Original range: 85-747
Documentation:

Method code:
85 |   void add(Node n, Context context) {
86 |     if (!cc.continueProcessing()) {
87 |       return;
88 |     }
89 | 
90 |     int type = n.getType();
91 |     String opstr = NodeUtil.opToStr(type);
92 |     int childCount = n.getChildCount();
93 |     Node first = n.getFirstChild();
94 |     Node last = n.getLastChild();
95 | 
96 |     // Handle all binary operators
97 |     if (opstr != null && first != last) {
98 |       Preconditions.checkState(
99 |           childCount == 2,
100 |           "Bad binary operator \"%s\": expected 2 arguments but got %s",
101 |           opstr, childCount);
102 |       int p = NodeUtil.precedence(type);
103 |       addExpr(first, p, context);
104 |       cc.addOp(opstr, true);
105 | 
106 |       // For right-hand-side of operations, only pass context if it's
107 |       // the IN_FOR_INIT_CLAUSE one.
108 |       Context rhsContext = getContextForNoInOperator(context);
109 | 
110 |       // Handle associativity.
111 |       // e.g. if the parse tree is a * (b * c),
112 |       // we can simply generate a * b * c.
113 |       if (last.getType() == type &&
114 |           NodeUtil.isAssociative(type)) {
115 |         addExpr(last, p, rhsContext);
116 |       } else if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n) && NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(last)) {
117 |         // Assignments are the only right-associative binary operators
118 |         addExpr(last, p, rhsContext);
119 |       } else {
120 |         addExpr(last, p + 1, rhsContext);
121 |       }
122 |       return;
123 |     }
124 | 
125 |     cc.startSourceMapping(n);
126 | 
127 |     switch (type) {
128 |       case Token.TRY: {
129 |         Preconditions.checkState(first.getNext().isBlock() &&
130 |                 !first.getNext().hasMoreThanOneChild());
131 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount >= 2 && childCount <= 3);
132 | 
133 |         add("try");
134 |         add(first, Context.PRESERVE_BLOCK);
135 | 
136 |         // second child contains the catch block, or nothing if there
137 |         // isn't a catch block
138 |         Node catchblock = first.getNext().getFirstChild();
139 |         if (catchblock != null) {
140 |           add(catchblock);
141 |         }
142 | 
143 |         if (childCount == 3) {
144 |           add("finally");
145 |           add(last, Context.PRESERVE_BLOCK);
146 |         }
147 |         break;
148 |       }
149 | 
150 |       case Token.CATCH:
151 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
152 |         add("catch(");
153 |         add(first);
154 |         add(")");
155 |         add(last, Context.PRESERVE_BLOCK);
156 |         break;
157 | 
158 |       case Token.THROW:
159 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
160 |         add("throw");
161 |         add(first);
162 | 
163 |         // Must have a ';' after a throw statement, otherwise safari can't
164 |         // parse this.
165 |         cc.endStatement(true);
166 |         break;
167 | 
168 |       case Token.RETURN:
169 |         add("return");
170 |         if (childCount == 1) {
171 |           add(first);
172 |         } else {
173 |           Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
174 |         }
175 |         cc.endStatement();
176 |         break;
177 | 
178 |       case Token.VAR:
179 |         if (first != null) {
180 |           add("var ");
181 |           addList(first, false, getContextForNoInOperator(context));
182 |         }
183 |         break;
184 | 
185 |       case Token.LABEL_NAME:
186 |         Preconditions.checkState(!n.getString().isEmpty());
187 |         addIdentifier(n.getString());
188 |         break;
189 | 
190 |       case Token.NAME:
191 |         if (first == null || first.isEmpty()) {
192 |           addIdentifier(n.getString());
193 |         } else {
194 |           Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
195 |           addIdentifier(n.getString());
196 |           cc.addOp("=", true);
197 |           if (first.isComma()) {
198 |             addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(Token.ASSIGN), Context.OTHER);
199 |           } else {
200 |             // Add expression, consider nearby code at lowest level of
201 |             // precedence.
202 |             addExpr(first, 0, getContextForNoInOperator(context));
203 |           }
204 |         }
205 |         break;
206 | 
207 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
208 |         add("[");
209 |         addArrayList(first);
210 |         add("]");
211 |         break;
212 | 
213 |       case Token.PARAM_LIST:
214 |         add("(");
215 |         addList(first);
216 |         add(")");
217 |         break;
218 | 
219 |       case Token.COMMA:
220 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
221 | 
222 |         // We could use addList recursively here, but sometimes we produce
223 |         // very deeply nested commas and run out of stack space, so we
224 |         // just unroll the recursion.
225 |         //
226 |         // We assume COMMA nodes are left-recursive.
227 |         Node firstNonComma = n.getFirstChild();
228 |         while (firstNonComma.getType() == Token.COMMA) {
229 |           firstNonComma = firstNonComma.getFirstChild();
230 |         }
231 | 
232 |         addExpr(firstNonComma, 0, context);
233 | 
234 |         Node current = firstNonComma;
235 |         do {
236 |           current = current.getParent();

238 |           addExpr(current.getFirstChild().getNext(), 0, Context.OTHER);
239 |         } while (current != n);
240 | 
241 |         break;
242 | 
243 |       case Token.NUMBER:
244 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
245 |         cc.addNumber(n.getDouble());
246 |         break;
247 | 
248 |       case Token.TYPEOF:
249 |       case Token.VOID:
250 |       case Token.NOT:
251 |       case Token.BITNOT:
252 |       case Token.POS: {
253 |         // All of these unary operators are right-associative
254 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
255 |         cc.addOp(NodeUtil.opToStrNoFail(type), false);
256 |         addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(type), Context.OTHER);
257 |         break;
258 |       }
259 | 
260 |       case Token.NEG: {
261 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
262 | 
263 |         // It's important to our sanity checker that the code
264 |         // we print produces the same AST as the code we parse back.
265 |         // NEG is a weird case because Rhino parses "- -2" as "2".
266 |         if (n.getFirstChild().isNumber()) {
267 |           cc.addNumber(-n.getFirstChild().getDouble());
268 |         } else {

270 |           addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(type), Context.OTHER);
271 |         }
272 |

274 |       }

278 |         int p = NodeUtil.precedence(type);

283 |         addExpr(last, 1, Context.OTHER);
284 |         break;
285 |       }

287 |       case Token.REGEXP:
288 |         if (!first.isString() ||

291 |         }

294 |

298 |         } else {

300 |           add(regexp);
301 |         }
302 |         break;
303 | 
304 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
305 |         if (n.getClass() != Node.class) {
306 |           throw new Error("Unexpected Node subclass.");
307 |         }
308 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 3);
309 |         boolean funcNeedsParens = (context == Context.START_OF_EXPR);
310 |         if (funcNeedsParens) {
311 |           add("(");
312 |         }
313 | 
314 |         add("function");
315 |         add(first);
316 | 
317 |         add(first.getNext());
318 |         add(last, Context.PRESERVE_BLOCK);
319 |         cc.endFunction(context == Context.STATEMENT);
320 | 
321 |         if (funcNeedsParens) {
322 |           add(")");
323 |         }
324 |         break;
325 | 
326 |       case Token.GETTER_DEF:
327 |       case Token.SETTER_DEF:
328 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.getParent().isObjectLit());
329 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
330 |         Preconditions.checkState(first.isFunction());
331 | 
332 |         // Get methods are unnamed
333 |         Preconditions.checkState(first.getFirstChild().getString().isEmpty());
334 |         if (type == Token.GETTER_DEF) {
335 |           // Get methods have no parameters.
336 |           Preconditions.checkState(!first.getChildAtIndex(1).hasChildren());
337 |           add("get ");
338 |         } else {
339 |           // Set methods have one parameter.
340 |           Preconditions.checkState(first.getChildAtIndex(1).hasOneChild());
341 |           add("set ");
342 |         }
343 | 
344 |         // The name is on the GET or SET node.
345 |         String name = n.getString();
346 |         Node fn = first;
347 |         Node parameters = fn.getChildAtIndex(1);
348 |         Node body = fn.getLastChild();
349 | 
350 |         // Add the property name.
351 |         if (!n.isQuotedString() &&
352 |             TokenStream.isJSIdentifier(name) &&
353 |             // do not encode literally any non-literal characters that were
354 |             // unicode escaped.
355 |             NodeUtil.isLatin(name)) {
356 |           add(name);
357 |         } else {
358 |           // Determine if the string is a simple number.
359 |           double d = getSimpleNumber(name);
360 |           if (!Double.isNaN(d)) {
361 |             cc.addNumber(d);
362 |           } else {
363 |             addJsString(n);
364 |           }
365 |         }
366 | 
367 |         add(parameters);
368 |         add(body, Context.PRESERVE_BLOCK);
369 |         break;
370 | 
371 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
372 |       case Token.BLOCK: {
373 |         if (n.getClass() != Node.class) {
374 |           throw new Error("Unexpected Node subclass.");
375 |         }
376 |         boolean preserveBlock = context == Context.PRESERVE_BLOCK;
377 |         if (preserveBlock) {
378 |           cc.beginBlock();
379 |         }
380 | 
381 |         boolean preferLineBreaks =
382 |             type == Token.SCRIPT ||
383 |             (type == Token.BLOCK &&
384 |                 !preserveBlock &&
385 |                 n.getParent() != null &&
386 |                 n.getParent().isScript());
387 |         for (Node c = first; c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
388 |           add(c, Context.STATEMENT);
389 | 
390 |           // VAR doesn't include ';' since it gets used in expressions
391 |           if (c.isVar()) {
392 |             cc.endStatement();
393 |           }

395 |           if (c.isFunction()) {
396 |             cc.maybeLineBreak();
397 |           }
398 | 
399 |           // Prefer to break lines in between top-level statements
400 |           // because top level statements are more homogeneous.
401 |           if (preferLineBreaks) {
402 |             cc.notePreferredLineBreak();
403 |           }
404 |         }
405 |         if (preserveBlock) {
406 |           cc.endBlock(cc.breakAfterBlockFor(n, context == Context.STATEMENT));
407 |         }
408 |         break;
409 |       }
410 | 
411 |       case Token.FOR:
412 |         if (childCount == 4) {
413 |           add("for(");
414 |           if (first.isVar()) {
415 |             add(first, Context.IN_FOR_INIT_CLAUSE);
416 |           } else {
417 |             addExpr(first, 0, Context.IN_FOR_INIT_CLAUSE);
418 |           }
419 |           add(";");
420 |           add(first.getNext());
421 |           add(";");
422 |           add(first.getNext().getNext());
423 |           add(")");
424 |           addNonEmptyStatement(
425 |               last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), false);
426 |         } else {
427 |           Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 3);
428 |           add("for(");
429 |           add(first);
430 |           add("in");
431 |           add(first.getNext());
432 |           add(")");
433 |           addNonEmptyStatement(
434 |               last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), false);
435 |         }
436 |         break;
437 | 
438 |       case Token.DO:
439 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
440 |         add("do");
441 |         addNonEmptyStatement(first, Context.OTHER, false);
442 |         add("while(");
443 |         add(last);
444 |         add(")");
445 |         cc.endStatement();
446 |         break;
447 | 
448 |       case Token.WHILE:
449 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
450 |         add("while(");
451 |         add(first);
452 |         add(")");
453 |         addNonEmptyStatement(
454 |             last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), false);
455 |         break;
456 | 
457 |       case Token.EMPTY:
458 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
459 |         break;
460 | 
461 |       case Token.GETPROP: {
462 |         Preconditions.checkState(
463 |             childCount == 2,
464 |             "Bad GETPROP: expected 2 children, but got %s", childCount);
465 |         Preconditions.checkState(
466 |             last.isString(),
467 |             "Bad GETPROP: RHS should be STRING");
468 |         boolean needsParens = (first.isNumber());
469 |         if (needsParens) {
470 |           add("(");
471 |         }
472 |         addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(type), context);
473 |         if (needsParens) {
474 |           add(")");
475 |         }
476 |         add(".");
477 |         addIdentifier(last.getString());
478 |         break;
479 |       }
480 | 
481 |       case Token.GETELEM:
482 |         Preconditions.checkState(
483 |             childCount == 2,
484 |             "Bad GETELEM: expected 2 children but got %s", childCount);
485 |         addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(type), context);
486 |         add("[");
487 |         add(first.getNext());
488 |         add("]");
489 |         break;
490 | 
491 |       case Token.WITH:
492 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
493 |         add("with(");
494 |         add(first);
495 |         add(")");
496 |         addNonEmptyStatement(
497 |             last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), false);
498 |         break;
499 | 
500 |       case Token.INC:
501 |       case Token.DEC: {
502 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
503 |         String o = type == Token.INC ? "++" : "--";
504 |         int postProp = n.getIntProp(Node.INCRDECR_PROP);
505 |         // A non-zero post-prop value indicates a post inc/dec, default of zero
506 |         // is a pre-inc/dec.
507 |         if (postProp != 0) {
508 |           addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(type), context);
509 |           cc.addOp(o, false);
510 |         } else {
511 |           cc.addOp(o, false);
512 |           add(first);
513 |         }
514 |         break;
515 |       }
516 | 
517 |       case Token.CALL:
518 |         // We have two special cases here:
519 |         // 1) If the left hand side of the call is a direct reference to eval,
520 |         // then it must have a DIRECT_EVAL annotation. If it does not, then
521 |         // that means it was originally an indirect call to eval, and that
522 |         // indirectness must be preserved.
523 |         // 2) If the left hand side of the call is a property reference,
524 |         // then the call must not a FREE_CALL annotation. If it does, then
525 |         // that means it was originally an call without an explicit this and
526 |         // that must be preserved.
527 |         if (isIndirectEval(first)
528 |             || n.getBooleanProp(Node.FREE_CALL) && NodeUtil.isGet(first)) {
529 |           add("(0,");
530 |           addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(Token.COMMA), Context.OTHER);
531 |           add(")");
532 |         } else {
533 |           addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(type), context);
534 |         }
535 |         add("(");
536 |         addList(first.getNext());
537 |         add(")");
538 |         break;
539 | 
540 |       case Token.IF:
541 |         boolean hasElse = childCount == 3;
542 |         boolean ambiguousElseClause =
543 |             context == Context.BEFORE_DANGLING_ELSE && !hasElse;
544 |         if (ambiguousElseClause) {
545 |           cc.beginBlock();
546 |         }
547 | 
548 |         add("if(");
549 |         add(first);
550 |         add(")");
551 | 
552 |         if (hasElse) {
553 |           addNonEmptyStatement(
554 |               first.getNext(), Context.BEFORE_DANGLING_ELSE, false);
555 |           add("else");
556 |           addNonEmptyStatement(
557 |               last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), false);
558 |         } else {
559 |           addNonEmptyStatement(first.getNext(), Context.OTHER, false);
560 |           Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
561 |         }
562 | 
563 |         if (ambiguousElseClause) {
564 |           cc.endBlock();
565 |         }
566 |         break;
567 | 
568 |       case Token.NULL:
569 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
570 |         add("null");
571 |         break;
572 | 
573 |       case Token.THIS:
574 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
575 |         add("this");
576 |         break;
577 | 
578 |       case Token.FALSE:
579 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
580 |         add("false");
581 |         break;
582 | 
583 |       case Token.TRUE:
584 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
585 |         add("true");
586 |         break;
587 | 
588 |       case Token.CONTINUE:
589 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount <= 1);
590 |         add("continue");
591 |         if (childCount == 1) {
592 |           if (!first.isLabelName()) {
593 |             throw new Error("Unexpected token type. Should be LABEL_NAME.");
594 |           }
595 |           add(" ");
596 |           add(first);
597 |         }
598 |         cc.endStatement();
599 |         break;
600 | 
601 |       case Token.DEBUGGER:
602 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
603 |         add("debugger");
604 |         cc.endStatement();
605 |         break;
606 | 
607 |       case Token.BREAK:
608 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount <= 1);
609 |         add("break");
610 |         if (childCount == 1) {
611 |           if (!first.isLabelName()) {
612 |             throw new Error("Unexpected token type. Should be LABEL_NAME.");
613 |           }
614 |           add(" ");
615 |           add(first);
616 |         }
617 |         cc.endStatement();
618 |         break;
619 | 
620 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
621 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
622 |         add(first, Context.START_OF_EXPR);
623 |         cc.endStatement();
624 |         break;
625 | 
626 |       case Token.NEW:
627 |         add("new ");
628 |         int precedence = NodeUtil.precedence(type);
629 | 
630 |         // If the first child contains a CALL, then claim higher precedence
631 |         // to force parentheses. Otherwise, when parsed, NEW will bind to the
632 |         // first viable parentheses (don't traverse into functions).
633 |         if (NodeUtil.containsType(
634 |             first, Token.CALL, NodeUtil.MATCH_NOT_FUNCTION)) {
635 |           precedence = NodeUtil.precedence(first.getType()) + 1;
636 |         }
637 |         addExpr(first, precedence, Context.OTHER);
638 | 
639 |         // '()' is optional when no arguments are present
640 |         Node next = first.getNext();
641 |         if (next != null) {
642 |           add("(");
643 |           addList(next);
644 |           add(")");
645 |         }
646 |         break;
647 | 
648 |       case Token.STRING:
649 |         if (childCount !=
650 |             ((n.getParent() != null &&
651 |               n.getParent().isObjectLit()) ? 1 : 0)) {
652 |           throw new IllegalStateException(
653 |               "Unexpected String children: " + n.getParent().toStringTree());
654 |         }
655 |         addJsString(n);
656 |         break;
657 | 
658 |       case Token.DELPROP:
659 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
660 |         add("delete ");
661 |         add(first);
662 |         break;
663 | 
664 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT: {
665 |         boolean needsParens = (context == Context.START_OF_EXPR);
666 |         if (needsParens) {
667 |           add("(");
668 |         }
669 |         add("{");
670 |         for (Node c = first; c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
671 |           if (c != first) {
672 |             cc.listSeparator();
673 |           }
674 | 
675 |           if (c.isGetterDef() || c.isSetterDef()) {
676 |             add(c);
677 |           } else {
678 |             Preconditions.checkState(c.isString());
679 |             String key = c.getString();
680 |             // Object literal property names don't have to be quoted if they
681 |             // are not JavaScript keywords
682 |             if (!c.isQuotedString() &&
683 |                 !TokenStream.isKeyword(key) &&
684 |                 TokenStream.isJSIdentifier(key) &&
685 |                 // do not encode literally any non-literal characters that
686 |                 // were unicode escaped.
687 |                 NodeUtil.isLatin(key)) {
688 |               add(key);
689 |             } else {
690 |               // Determine if the string is a simple number.
691 |               double d = getSimpleNumber(key);
692 |               if (!Double.isNaN(d)) {
693 |                 cc.addNumber(d);
694 |               } else {
695 |                 addExpr(c, 1, Context.OTHER);
696 |               }
697 |             }
698 |             add(":");
699 |             addExpr(c.getFirstChild(), 1, Context.OTHER);
700 |           }
701 |         }
702 |         add("}");
703 |         if (needsParens) {
704 |           add(")");
705 |         }
706 |         break;
707 |       }
708 | 
709 |       case Token.SWITCH:
710 |         add("switch(");
711 |         add(first);
712 |         add(")");
713 |         cc.beginBlock();
714 |         addAllSiblings(first.getNext());
715 |         cc.endBlock(context == Context.STATEMENT);
716 |         break;
717 | 
718 |       case Token.CASE:
719 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
720 |         add("case ");
721 |         add(first);
722 |         addCaseBody(last);
723 |         break;
724 | 
725 |       case Token.DEFAULT_CASE:
726 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
727 |         add("default");
728 |         addCaseBody(first);
729 |         break;
730 | 
731 |       case Token.LABEL:
732 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
733 |         if (!first.isLabelName()) {
734 |           throw new Error("Unexpected token type. Should be LABEL_NAME.");
735 |         }
736 |         add(first);
737 |         add(":");
738 |         addNonEmptyStatement(
739 |             last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), true);
740 |         break;
741 | 
742 |       default:
743 |         throw new Error("Unknown type " + type + "\n" + n.toStringTree());
744 |     }
745 | 
746 |     cc.endSourceMapping(n);
747 |   }

Method code:
396 |     @Override
397 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal traversal, Node node, Node parent) {
398 | 
399 |       if (inExterns) {
400 |         return;
401 |       }
402 | 
403 |       if (!NodeUtil.nodeTypeMayHaveSideEffects(node)
404 |           && !node.isReturn()) {
405 |         return;
406 |       }
407 | 
408 |       if (node.isCall() || node.isNew()) {
409 |         allFunctionCalls.add(node);
410 |       }
411 | 
412 |       Node enclosingFunction = traversal.getEnclosingFunction();
413 |       if (enclosingFunction != null) {
414 |         FunctionInformation sideEffectInfo =
415 |             functionSideEffectMap.get(enclosingFunction);
416 |         Preconditions.checkNotNull(sideEffectInfo);
417 | 
418 |         if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(node)) {
419 |           visitAssignmentOrUnaryOperator(
420 |               sideEffectInfo, traversal.getScope(),
421 |               node, node.getFirstChild(), node.getLastChild());
422 |         } else {
423 |           switch(node.getType()) {
424 |             case Token.CALL:
425 |             case Token.NEW:
426 |               visitCall(sideEffectInfo, node);
427 |               break;
428 |             case Token.DELPROP:

430 |             case Token.INC:
431 |               visitAssignmentOrUnaryOperator(
432 |                   sideEffectInfo, traversal.getScope(),
433 |                   node, node.getFirstChild(), null);
434 |               break;
435 |             case Token.NAME:
436 |               // Variable definition are not side effects.
437 |               // Just check that the name appears in the context of a
438 |               // variable declaration.
439 |               Preconditions.checkArgument(
440 |                   NodeUtil.isVarDeclaration(node));
441 |               Node value = node.getFirstChild();
442 |               // Assignment to local, if the value isn't a safe local value,
443 |               // new object creation or literal or known primitive result
444 |               // value, add it to the local blacklist.
445 |               if (value != null && !NodeUtil.evaluatesToLocalValue(value)) {
446 |                 Scope scope = traversal.getScope();
447 |                 Var var = scope.getVar(node.getString());
448 |                 sideEffectInfo.blacklistLocal(var);
449 |               }
450 |               break;
451 |             case Token.THROW:
452 |               visitThrow(sideEffectInfo);
453 |               break;
454 |             case Token.RETURN:
455 |               if (node.hasChildren()
456 |                   && !NodeUtil.evaluatesToLocalValue(node.getFirstChild())) {
457 |                 sideEffectInfo.setTaintsReturn();
458 |               }
459 |               break;
460 |             default:
461 |               throw new IllegalArgumentException(
462 |                   "Unhandled side effect node type " +
463 |                   Token.name(node.getType()));
464 |           }
465 |         }
466 |       }
467 |     }

/**
   * Traverses a function, which creates a new scope in javascript.
   *
   * Note that CATCH blocks also create a new scope, but only for the
   * catch variable. Declarations within the block actually belong to the
   * enclosing scope. Because we don't remove catch variables, there's

601 |     private void visitFunction(NodeTraversal traversal,
602 |                                Node node,
603 |                                Node parent,

605 |       Preconditions.checkArgument(!functionSideEffectMap.containsKey(node));
606 | 
607 |       FunctionInformation sideEffectInfo = new FunctionInformation(inExterns);

616 |           if (isLocalValueType(jstypeReturn, true)) {

638 |           if (inExterns) {
639 |             hasSpecificSideEffects = true;

643 |           }

655 |           }

Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NameAnalyzer.java

/**
   * Replace n with a simpler expression, while preserving program
   * behavior.
   *
   * If the n's value is used, replace it with its rhs; otherwise
   * replace it with the subexpressions that have side effects.
   */
Method code:
1618 |   private void replaceWithRhs(Node parent, Node n) {
1619 |     if (valueConsumedByParent(n, parent)) {
1620 |       // parent reads from n directly; replace it with n's rhs + lhs
1621 |       // subexpressions with side effects.
1622 |       List<Node> replacements = getRhsSubexpressions(n);
1623 |       List<Node> newReplacements = Lists.newArrayList();
1624 |       for (int i = 0; i < replacements.size() - 1; i++) {
1625 |         newReplacements.addAll(getSideEffectNodes(replacements.get(i)));
1626 |       }
1627 |       Node valueExpr = replacements.get(replacements.size() - 1);
1628 |       valueExpr.detachFromParent();
1629 |       newReplacements.add(valueExpr);
1630 |       changeProxy.replaceWith(
1631 |           parent, n, collapseReplacements(newReplacements));
1632 |     } else if (n.isAssign() && !parent.isFor()) {
1633 |       // assignment appears in a RHS expression.  we have already
1634 |       // considered names in the assignment's RHS as being referenced;
1635 |       // replace the assignment with its RHS.
1636 |       // TODO(user) make the pass smarter about these cases and/or run
1637 |       // this pass and RemoveConstantExpressions together in a loop.
1638 |       Node replacement = n.getLastChild();
1639 |       replacement.detachFromParent();
1640 |       changeProxy.replaceWith(parent, n, replacement);
1641 |     } else {
1642 |       replaceTopLevelExpressionWithRhs(parent, n);
1643 |     }
1644 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.PrototypeObjectType.isSubtype(JSType)

Original range: 443-491
Documentation:

Method code:
443 |   @Override
444 |   public boolean isSubtype(JSType that) {
445 |     if (JSType.isSubtypeHelper(this, that)) {
446 |       return true;
447 |     }
448 | 
449 |     // Union types
450 |     if (that.isUnionType()) {
451 |       // The static {@code JSType.isSubtype} check already decomposed
452 |       // union types, so we don't need to check those again.
453 |       return false;
454 |     }
455 | 
456 |     // record types
457 |     if (that.isRecordType()) {
458 |       return RecordType.isSubtype(this, that.toMaybeRecordType());
459 |     }
460 | 
461 |     // Interfaces
462 |     // Find all the interfaces implemented by this class and compare each one
463 |     // to the interface instance.
464 |     ObjectType thatObj = that.toObjectType();
465 |     ObjectType thatCtor = thatObj == null ? null : thatObj.getConstructor();
466 |     if (thatCtor != null && thatCtor.isInterface()) {
467 |       Iterable<ObjectType> thisInterfaces = getCtorImplementedInterfaces();
468 |       for (ObjectType thisInterface : thisInterfaces) {
469 |         if (thisInterface.isSubtype(that)) {
470 |           return true;
471 |         }
472 |       }
473 |     }
474 | 
475 |     if (getConstructor() != null && getConstructor().isInterface()) {
476 |       for (ObjectType thisInterface : getCtorExtendedInterfaces()) {
477 |         if (thisInterface.isSubtype(that)) {
478 |           return true;
479 |         }
480 |       }
481 |     }
482 | 
483 |     // other prototype based objects
484 |     if (isUnknownType() || implicitPrototypeChainIsUnknown()) {
485 |       // If unsure, say 'yes', to avoid spurious warnings.
486 |       // TODO(user): resolve the prototype chain completely in all cases,
487 |       // to avoid guessing.
488 |       return true;
489 |     }
490 |     return this.isImplicitPrototype(thatObj);
491 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.LiveVariablesAnalysis.flowThrough(Node,LiveVariableLattice)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/LiveVariablesAnalysis.java
Original range: 151-170
Documentation:

Method code:
151 |   @Override
152 |   LiveVariableLattice flowThrough(Node node, LiveVariableLattice input) {
153 |     final BitSet gen = new BitSet(input.liveSet.size());
154 |     final BitSet kill = new BitSet(input.liveSet.size());
155 | 
156 |     // Make kills conditional if the node can end abruptly by an exception.
157 |     boolean conditional = false;
158 |     List<DiGraphEdge<Node, Branch>> edgeList = getCfg().getOutEdges(node);
159 |     for (DiGraphEdge<Node, Branch> edge : edgeList) {
160 |       if (Branch.ON_EX.equals(edge.getValue())) {
161 |         conditional = true;
162 |       }
163 |     }
164 |     computeGenKill(node, gen, kill, conditional);
165 |     LiveVariableLattice result = new LiveVariableLattice(input);
166 |     // L_in = L_out - Kill + Gen
167 |     result.liveSet.andNot(kill);
168 |     result.liveSet.or(gen);
169 |     return result;
170 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.MustBeReachingVariableDef.computeMustDef(Node,Node,MustDef,boolean)

/**
   * @param n The node in question.
   * @param cfgNode The node to add
   * @param conditional true if the definition is not always executed.
   */
Method code:
222 |   private void computeMustDef(
223 |       Node n, Node cfgNode, MustDef output, boolean conditional) {
224 |     switch (n.getType()) {
225 | 
226 |       case Token.BLOCK:
227 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
228 |         return;
229 | 
230 |       case Token.WHILE:
231 |       case Token.DO:
232 |       case Token.IF:
233 |         computeMustDef(
234 |             NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), cfgNode, output, conditional);
235 |         return;
236 | 
237 |       case Token.FOR:
238 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(n)) {
239 |           computeMustDef(
240 |               NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), cfgNode, output, conditional);
241 |         } else {
242 |           // for(x in y) {...}
243 |           Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
244 |           Node rhs = lhs.getNext();
245 |           if (lhs.isVar()) {
246 |             lhs = lhs.getLastChild(); // for(var x in y) {...}
247 |           }
248 |           if (lhs.isName()) {
249 |             addToDefIfLocal(lhs.getString(), cfgNode, rhs, output);
250 |           }
251 |         }
252 |         return;
253 | 
254 |       case Token.AND:
255 |       case Token.OR:
256 |         computeMustDef(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
257 |         computeMustDef(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
258 |         return;
259 | 
260 |       case Token.HOOK:
261 |         computeMustDef(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
262 |         computeMustDef(n.getFirstChild().getNext(), cfgNode, output, true);
263 |         computeMustDef(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
264 |         return;
265 | 
266 |       case Token.VAR:
267 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
268 |           if (c.hasChildren()) {
269 |             computeMustDef(c.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
270 |             addToDefIfLocal(c.getString(), conditional ? null : cfgNode,
271 |                 c.getFirstChild(), output);
272 |           }
273 |         }
274 |         return;
275 | 
276 |       default:
277 |         if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n)) {
278 |           if (n.getFirstChild().isName()) {
279 |             Node name = n.getFirstChild();
280 |             computeMustDef(name.getNext(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
281 |             addToDefIfLocal(name.getString(), conditional ? null : cfgNode,
282 |               n.getLastChild(), output);
283 |             return;
284 |           } else if (NodeUtil.isGet(n.getFirstChild())) {
285 |             // Treat all assignments to arguments as redefining the
286 |             // parameters itself.
287 |             Node obj = n.getFirstChild().getFirstChild();
288 |             if (obj.isName() && "arguments".equals(obj.getString())) {
289 |               // TODO(user): More accuracy can be introduced
290 |               // ie: We know exactly what arguments[x] is if x is a constant
291 |               // number.
292 |               escapeParameters(output);
293 |             }
294 |           }
295 |         }
296 | 
297 |         if (n.isName() && "arguments".equals(n.getString())) {
298 |           escapeParameters(output);
299 |         }
300 | 
301 |         // DEC and INC actually defines the variable.
302 |         if (n.isDec() || n.isInc()) {
303 |           Node target = n.getFirstChild();
304 |           if (target.isName()) {
305 |             addToDefIfLocal(target.getString(),
306 |                 conditional ? null : cfgNode, null, output);
307 |             return;
308 |           }
309 |         }
310 | 
311 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
312 |           computeMustDef(c, cfgNode, output, conditional);
313 |         }
314 |     }
315 |   }

/**
   * Removes any vars in the scope that were not referenced. Removes any
   * assignments to those variables as well.
   */
Method code:
784 |   private void removeUnreferencedVars() {
785 |     CodingConvention convention = codingConvention;
786 | 
787 |     for (Iterator<Var> it = maybeUnreferenced.iterator(); it.hasNext(); ) {
788 |       Var var = it.next();
789 | 
790 |       // Remove calls to inheritance-defining functions where the unreferenced
791 |       // class is the subclass.
792 |       for (Node exprCallNode : inheritsCalls.get(var)) {
793 |         NodeUtil.removeChild(exprCallNode.getParent(), exprCallNode);
794 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
795 |       }
796 | 
797 |       // Regardless of what happens to the original declaration,
798 |       // we need to remove all assigns, because they may contain references
799 |       // to other unreferenced variables.
800 |       removeAllAssigns(var);
801 | 
802 |       compiler.addToDebugLog("Unreferenced var: " + var.name);
803 |       Node nameNode = var.nameNode;
804 |       Node toRemove = nameNode.getParent();
805 |       Node parent = toRemove.getParent();
806 | 
807 |       Preconditions.checkState(
808 |           toRemove.isVar() ||
809 |           toRemove.isFunction() ||
810 |           toRemove.isParamList() &&
811 |           parent.isFunction(),
812 |           "We should only declare vars and functions and function args");
813 | 
814 |       if (toRemove.isParamList() &&
815 |           parent.isFunction()) {
816 |         // Don't remove function arguments here. That's a special case
817 |         // that's taken care of in removeUnreferencedFunctionArgs.
818 |       } else if (NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(toRemove)) {
819 |         if (!preserveFunctionExpressionNames) {
820 |           toRemove.getFirstChild().setString("");
821 |           compiler.reportCodeChange();
822 |         }
823 |         // Don't remove bleeding functions.
824 |       } else if (parent != null &&
825 |           parent.isFor() &&
826 |           parent.getChildCount() < 4) {
827 |         // foreach iterations have 3 children. Leave them alone.
828 |       } else if (toRemove.isVar() &&
829 |           nameNode.hasChildren() &&
830 |           NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(nameNode.getFirstChild())) {
831 |         // If this is a single var declaration, we can at least remove the
832 |         // declaration itself and just leave the value, e.g.,
833 |         // var a = foo(); => foo();
834 |         if (toRemove.getChildCount() == 1) {
835 |           parent.replaceChild(toRemove,
836 |               IR.exprResult(nameNode.removeFirstChild()));
837 |           compiler.reportCodeChange();
838 |         }
839 |       } else if (toRemove.isVar() &&
840 |           toRemove.getChildCount() > 1) {
841 |         // For var declarations with multiple names (i.e. var a, b, c),
842 |         // only remove the unreferenced name
843 |         toRemove.removeChild(nameNode);
844 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
845 |       } else if (parent != null) {
846 |         NodeUtil.removeChild(parent, toRemove);
847 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
848 |       }
849 |     }
850 |   }
